# Step 15d: Sales returns, credit notes and refunds — when goods or money come back

> The implementation guide for the last part of "Phase 5 → Step 15" of [build-plan.bn.md](build-plan.bn.md): which
> file gets what code, and which command runs where. Step 15 (Sales) is split into four guides: 15a (customers, price
> lists, VAT), 15b (quotations, orders, deliveries), 15c (invoices, money receipts, the credit limit), and this one.
>
> Every file in this guide was placed in a separate copy of the repo (on top of commit `83a4d9d`, the end of
> step 15c) and checked on 2026-10-12: `pnpm dedupe --check`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (364 — 42 new), `pnpm test:integration` (331 — 24 new), `pnpm test:tenant-leak` (63 — 4 new), `pnpm build`, `pnpm test:bundle-size` (first load 196.5 KB gz, budget 200; the sales returns list 99.4 KB, the adjustment form 99.1 KB, the refunds and receipts lists 98.9 KB), `pnpm gen:openapi` (144 paths), `pnpm test:openapi`, `pnpm boundaries` and `pnpm test:e2e` (Playwright, 170 — 22 new, desktop and 390px; one test on the phone failed once on a busy machine and passed when run again, 15d.8) — all pass, with the turbo cache bypassed (`--force`).
>
> Also checked:
>
> - **The database rules on their own**, in a throwaway Postgres: 83 checks of migration 0032 run as `omnivo_app`
>   with SQL the API would never send (a posted return changed, "credited" written by hand, a credit note line that
>   names another invoice's line, a refund larger than the money left), and two races: two returns of the last piece
>   of one challan line, and a receipt and a credit note settling one invoice. In each, the second waits, then fails
>   (15d.2's "Check this part").
> - **The whole chain in a browser**, through the end-to-end tests on a desktop and a 390px phone: goods taken back
>   from a challan, a challan billed after part of it came back, a credit note written from a return, a whole invoice
>   credited, a credit note's money applied to another invoice, money paid back from a receipt and from a credit
>   note, a refund voided, and the "Sales accounts" setting.
> - **Guards broken on purpose**: without the `FOR UPDATE` on the challan lines in `SalesReturnsService`, the race
>   between a return and an invoice of one challan line fails; with `FOR UPDATE` instead of `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` on the
>   invoice, two credit notes posted at once deadlock (15d.4, a bug found and fixed there); without
>   `billableQuantity()` in the mock, the "bills only what is left" test fails (15d.7). Each check ran its whole test

## Goal

↩️ **When goods or money come back.** 15b sent goods out with a challan, 15c billed them and took the money in. Real
sales do not always end there: a pharmacy sends back syrup that expired on its shelf, a dealer gets the wrong size,
a price was agreed lower after the invoice went out, or a customer paid twice. This step handles all of these the
way a Bangladeshi company already does on paper: a sales return for the goods, a credit note for the money, and a
refund when cash goes back out.

After this step:

- **Sales returns** (`SR-2026-27-0001`): goods come back into a warehouse you pick (a "Damage and expiry" store, or
  the main one). A line comes from a posted challan (the same batch and serial numbers that left, at the cost they
  left with), or stands on its own for goods sold before Omnivo (at the average cost that day). Posting books Dr
  Inventory / Cr Cost of goods sold. If the goods were not billed yet, the order counts them as not delivered, and
  the invoice later bills only what is left.
- **Credit notes** (`CN-2026-27-0001`): money taken off one posted invoice, for goods that came back or for a price
  cut. Posting books Dr Sales returns (or Sales) / Dr VAT payable / Cr Accounts receivable, at the VAT rate the
  invoice charged. The credit note first lowers what is due on its invoice; anything left is the customer's advance.
  "Credit whole invoice" writes a draft for every line in one click.
- **Refunds** (`RF-2026-27-0001`): money paid back out of a money account, from a receipt's or a credit note's
  money that was not used. Dr Accounts receivable / Cr Cash or Bank. A refund made by mistake is voided, like a
  money receipt.
- **Invoices** say "Credited" or "Partly credited", list their credit notes, and owe less. **Challans** say "Partly
  returned" or "Returned". A **credit note older than 6 months** after its invoice shows a warning.
- **Settings → Sales accounts**: the account credit notes take sales back from. The pharmacy and retail charts
  start with "4120 Sales returns"; the others debit Sales itself.

```
packages/contracts   sales-returns.ts · credit-notes.ts · refunds.ts · sales-accounts.ts (new)
      │               series SR, CN, RF · 3 permissions · journal sources sales_return (stock), sales_credit_note,
      │               sales_refund · movement kind sales_return · 30 errors · 12 audit actions
      │               deliveries: returnedQuantity, returnState, returns, billableQuantity() · invoices: amountCredited,
      │               creditNoteTotal, creditNotes, credited, amountDueOf() · receipts: refunded, unappliedOf()
      ▼
packages/db          sales_returns + lines · credit_notes + lines + allocations · refunds
                     delivery_lines.returned_quantity · invoices.amount_credited, credit_note_total · invoice_lines.credited
                     receipts.refunded · tenant_settings.sales_returns_account_id
                     0031 (drizzle, indexes moved up) · 0032 (RLS, guards, two money triggers, the 4120 preset)
      │
      ▼
apps/api             sales/: SalesReturnsService · CreditNotesService · RefundsService · SalesAccountsService
                     allocations.ts (one check for receipts and credit notes) · stock-books: the return's entry
                     sales-books: the credit note's and the refund's entries · deliveries, invoices, receipts: what
                     came back and what was credited · setup: the 4120 preset and the role templates
      │
      ▼
apps/app             /sales-returns · /credit-notes · /refunds (list, new, one) · Settings → Sales accounts
                     challan: Take goods back · invoice: Write credit note, Credit whole invoice · receipt: Pay back
                     print: return, credit note, refund · packages/i18n: the words · packages/ui: the sidebar scrolls
                     MSW: the same rules · Playwright: returns, credit notes, refunds

one return of goods already billed, then its credit note:
  Post return ──POST /sales-returns/{id}/post──► API, one transaction:
     lock the draft · date in an open period · lock its challan lines (FOR UPDATE, by id)
     every line: not more than left the gate minus what came back before · serial numbers that left on that line
     number SR-… · stock in (kind sales_return) at the challan line's cost, to the paisa
     Dr Inventory (the return warehouse's branch) / Cr Cost of goods sold (the challan's branch), source sales_return
     delivery_lines.returned_quantity += · the line remembers the invoice line that billed it
  Return page: "Write credit note" ──► the form, with the return's lines at the invoice's prices
  Post credit note ──POST /credit-notes/{id}/post──► lock the invoice (FOR NO KEY UPDATE)
     each line ≤ what its invoice line billed (quantity, and money across all credit notes)
     number CN-… · Dr Sales returns / Dr VAT payable / Cr Accounts receivable (the customer), source sales_credit_note
     invoice_lines.credited += · invoices.credit_note_total +=
     applied to its own invoice: min(total, what is due) ──► trigger: invoices.amount_credited, credit_notes.applied
  Invoice page: "Credited" or "Partly credited", owes less · anything left: an advance, applied later or paid back
```

## The decisions behind this step

You made the first eight on 2026-10-11 (the last two while the contract was written). Step 15's own choices are in
the 15a guide, and the invoice and receipt rules in 15c. The others came up while building it; please read 9–40 with
care: they are mine.

1. **Two documents.** (You chose this.) A sales return brings goods back into stock and reverses their cost; a
   credit note takes money off an invoice and reverses the sale and its VAT. They are separate, like the challan
   and the invoice. A credit note can come from a return, or have no goods at all (a price cut). A return can come
   before the goods were billed.
2. **A return costs what the challan line cost.** (You chose this.) The cost of goods sold is reversed exactly, at
   the cost per unit the goods left with. A return line with no challan uses the average cost on the return date.
3. **Everything goes back into stock.** (You chose this.) The whole return goes into the warehouse you pick, for
   example a "Damage and expiry" store. Goods that cannot be sold are written off later with a stock adjustment
   (step 13's reasons), not on the return.
4. **A credit note is applied to its invoice, then kept as an advance; a refund pays money back.** (You chose this.)
   What is left after the invoice is the customer's advance, applied to later invoices like a receipt's. A refund
   pays money out of a money account.
5. **"Credit whole invoice".** (You chose this.) One click writes a draft credit note for every line of a posted
   invoice. The invoice keeps its number and its entry and shows "Credited"; there is no invoice void.
6. **The 6-month rule is a warning.** (You chose this.) A credit note dated more than 6 months after its invoice
   shows a warning, but saving and posting are allowed. The Mushak 6.7 format comes later, with 6.3.
7. **The sales returns account is a setting.** (You chose this, in 15d.1.) Settings → Sales accounts; empty means
   a credit note debits the Sales account itself. The pharmacy and retail templates, and migration 0032 for
   workspaces that have a "4120 Sales returns", start with it chosen.
8. **A return before billing lowers the order's delivered quantity.** (You chose this, in 15d.1.) A "Delivered"
   order goes back to "Confirmed", so a replacement can go on the same order, or the order is closed. After
   billing, the order is not touched: the sale stands, and a credit note corrects the money.

**The return (15d.1–15d.3):**

9. **One warehouse per return, chosen on the header.** Decision 3 says all goods go back into one place; a line
   does not pick its own.
10. **A return's reason** (damaged, expired, wrong item, quality, unsold, other) decides nothing in the books. It is
    printed and will go on the Mushak 6.7 later.
11. **A challan line's batch is taken from the challan**, never typed: one challan line left with one batch (15b).
    Its serial numbers must be ones that left on that line.
12. **The return's value is worked out cumulatively**, so a challan line returned in parts gives back exactly its
    value: three injections worth ৳1,000.00 come back as 333.33, 333.34 and 333.33, never ৳999.99.
13. **The entry's two branches.** Inventory goes up in the return warehouse's branch; the cost of goods sold goes
    down in the branch that booked it (the challan's warehouse). A line with no challan uses the return's branch for
    both. A return worth ৳0 has no entry.
14. **What a return writes on a challan line is a counter**, `delivery_lines.returned_quantity`, written by the API
    at posting and only allowed to grow. A drafted return holds nothing back.
15. **A return line remembers the invoice line that billed it**, at posting (`invoice_id`, `invoice_line_id`), and
    never later. "Billed or not" is that column, so the credit note can only take back what that invoice billed.
16. **An invoice bills what is left of a partly returned challan line**, in the item's base unit
    (`billableQuantity()`), and a fully returned line drops out of "Not invoiced".
17. **A closed order's header is not touched** by a return: migration 0028 freezes it, even its version. Only the
    order line's delivered quantity goes down.
18. **A line on its own for an item with no average cost is refused** (`return_cost_unknown`, new), instead of
    coming back at ৳0 and spoiling the average.

**The credit note (15d.1–15d.3):**

19. **A credit note is always for one posted invoice**, so its VAT is reversed at the rate that invoice charged.
    The customer and the branch are the invoice's; "prices include VAT" is read from it, not stored again.
20. **A line points at an invoice line**, with no item or VAT rate of its own: the server copies them. Any unit of
    the item may be used.
21. **Two caps on every invoice line:** the quantity, and the money across all posted credit notes. So a price cut
    on all 100 pieces and a later return of 10 can both be credited, up to what was billed, never more.
22. **A posted credit note is never changed or voided**, like a posted invoice. There is no debit note in 15d: a
    credit note that took off too much is put right with a new invoice for the difference.
23. **The money is kept like a receipt's**: `credit_note_allocations` rows, and a trigger keeps
    `invoices.amount_credited` and `credit_notes.applied`. What an invoice owes is `amountDueOf()`: total − paid −
    credited.
24. **"Credit whole invoice" needs no route.** The app builds the lines (`wholeInvoiceCreditLines()`) and saves a
    draft. It is offered only while the invoice has no posted credit note, so the full amounts always fit the caps.
25. **The invoice is locked with `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`**, not `FOR UPDATE`, when a credit note is posted or applied.
    15d.4 found two credit notes posted at once deadlocking: the draft's foreign key already holds a lock that
    `FOR UPDATE` waits for.

**The refund (15d.1–15d.3):**

26. **A refund pays back one source**: a receipt's or a credit note's money not yet applied, never "the customer's
    balance" in general. So every taka paid out is tied to the taka that came in.
27. **Saved is posted**, like a money receipt; a refund made by mistake is voided with a reason, and the entry is
    reversed.
28. **A receipt with a refund cannot be voided** (`receipt_has_refunds`): void the refund first, or the books would
    pay the same money back twice.
29. **No credit limit check** on a return, a credit note or a refund: the first two lower what the customer owes,
    and a refund only pays back the customer's own advance.

**The rest (15d.1–15d.8):**

30. **Three permissions, one per document**, and paying money out is its own key: a cashier who takes money in
    cannot also hand it out.
31. **The role templates** (15d.8): the people who post challans take goods back; the accountant writes credit notes
    and refunds; a shop manager or a small company's manager does all three; a cashier and a sales officer do none.
32. **Thirty new error codes**, two of them found while writing the API (`return_cost_unknown`,
    `account_used_by_sales`).
33. **One allocation check for receipts and credit notes** (`allocations.ts`), so the two cannot drift apart.

**The screens (15d.6–15d.7):**

34. **The return form** takes the warehouse from the challan ("Take goods back") or the only one; challan lines have
    no batch box; a line on its own picks a lot from any warehouse that has stock. Another customer drops the challan
    lines but keeps the lines on their own.
35. **The credit note form** picks the customer, then one of their posted invoices; both lock while lines exist.
    Lines come from the invoice (as billed) or from a return (opened one by one), on the sales line grid with the
    item and VAT fixed.
36. **The refund form** has one source list (receipts and credit notes with money left, oldest first); picking one
    fills the amount and the branch.
37. **Pills:** invoice Credited and Partly credited (neutral, `Invoice04`); challan Partly returned
    (`DeliveryReturn01`) and Returned (`PackageReceive`), both neutral; return and credit note Draft / Posted; refund
    Posted / Voided. Work that is done is not a warning.
38. **Print:** the return like a challan (no prices), the credit note like an invoice with the original invoice
    number and date, the refund like a receipt. A voided refund does not print.
39. **The pills moved to `sales-pills.tsx`**, and the opening balances page loads its pickers lazily: the new
    contracts pushed several pages over the 100 KB budget.
40. **The mock API keeps its own `returns` data** (`mocks/return-data.ts`), works sums out on read, and stores only
    what is fixed at posting. The seeds post no 15d document; the tests make their own.

## Not in this step, on purpose

| What | Why not now / when |
|---|---|
| Mushak 6.7 (the VAT credit note form) | Step 16 (document output), with Mushak 6.3 (decision 6) |
| Blocking a credit note after 6 months | Decision 6: a warning, the VAT adviser decides |
| Restock or scrap per line, a restocking fee | Decision 3: all back to stock, write-offs with a stock adjustment |
| Voiding a posted credit note, a debit note | Decision 22; a new invoice corrects a wrong credit note |
| A rebate with no invoice (a year-end discount) | Later; a credit note is always for one invoice (decision 19) |
| Returns through a courier (cash on delivery) | The COD step |
| Refunds through bKash, Nagad or SSLCommerz | Later, with online payment; today a refund names its method and reference |
| Supplier returns and debit notes | Step 17 (purchasing) |

## What changes in the code you already have

- **No new package**, no new `.env` line, no new database role, no new worker job.
- **`pnpm db:migrate`** adds six tables (0031) and their rules (0032), writes the three new permissions and chooses
  "4120 Sales returns" where a workspace has it. Then restart `pnpm dev` so the API has the new routes.
- **Contracts:** three number series, three permissions, three journal sources, a movement kind, 30 error codes and
  12 audit actions. The delivery gets `returnedQuantity` on a line, `returnState`, `returns` and a `return` filter;
  the invoice `amountCredited`, `creditNoteTotal`, `creditNotes` and a line's `credited`; what an invoice owes is
  `amountDueOf()` everywhere; the receipt gets `refunded`.
- **Database:** 15b's and 15c's guards let a posted challan line's `returned_quantity` grow, let a delivered order
  go back to confirmed, and let an invoice's credit counters grow; the invoice's "paid" check counts credits too.
- **API:** a challan says what came back; an invoice bills only what is left and says what was credited; a receipt
  counts its refunds and refuses a void while one stands; the journal's Reverse refuses the three new sources;
  deleting a customer, a product or an account that a new document uses answers `..._in_use`, and archiving the
  chosen returns account answers `account_used_by_sales`; the setup gives new workspaces the 4120 setting and the
  new permissions (15d.8) — existing roles do not get them; an owner ticks them on the Roles page.
- **ui:** the app shell's sidebar scrolls on its own (`overflow-y-auto`, 15d.7). With 15d's three new items the
  navigation is taller than an 800px screen, and "Settings" was out of reach.
- **app:** `receipt-dialogs.tsx` becomes `money-dialogs.tsx` (the credit note uses its apply form); the status pills
  move to `sales-pills.tsx`; the stock line row and the sales line editor learn the return's modes; the opening
  balances page loads its customer box and date picker lazily (the 100 KB budget, 15d.6).
- **Existing tests that change:** the numbering test counts 17 series; the setup test expects the new permissions
  of the Accountant and the Store keeper, and the 4120 setting; the templates test checks that setting's account; the
  contracts' and the app's invoice tests get `returnedQuantity` and `amountCredited` on their fixtures; the stock
  card test checks the new movement kind.

---

## 15d.1 — `packages/contracts`: the contract

The contract comes first, as in every step. Once it type-checks, the API and the app cannot disagree about a field
name.

Four new files hold what 15d adds: `sales-returns.ts` (goods that come back), `credit-notes.ts` (the money taken off
an invoice), `refunds.ts` (money paid back to a customer) and `sales-accounts.ts` (the "Sales returns" account in
Settings). The rest are small changes to files you already have: three number series, three permissions, three
journal sources, a stock movement kind, the error codes and the audit actions. Two 15c documents learn about 15d too:
a challan line now knows how much came back, and an invoice now knows what credit notes took off it.

### `numbering.ts`, `permissions.ts`, `journal.ts`, `stock.ts`

- **Three series: SR, CN, RF.** A sales return, a credit note and a refund are numbered documents, like a challan
  and a money receipt. They use the default yearly style (`CN-2026-27-0001`). "CN" is the short name an accountant
  in Bangladesh already writes on a credit note.

- **`sales.return.manage`.** Taking goods back into a warehouse. In a distribution company this is the store keeper,
  the same person who posts challans. A return moves stock, not money, so it does not need the accountant.
- **`sales.credit_note.manage`.** Writing, posting and applying credit notes: the accountant. A credit note lowers
  what the customer owes and lowers VAT, so it must not come with the return permission by accident.
- **`sales.refund.manage`.** Paying money out to a customer. It is its own key on purpose: the cashier who takes
  money in (`sales.receipt.manage`) should not also be able to hand it out unless the owner says so.

```diff
@@ -55,11 +63,13 @@ export function isStockJournalSource(value: string): value is StockJournalSource
 }
 
 // The sources a sales document posts (step 15c). Their entries are not reversed from the journal
-// either: an invoice is corrected by a credit note (15d), a receipt by voiding it on its own page,
-// so the document and the books never disagree.
+// either: an invoice is corrected by a credit note (15d), a receipt or a refund by voiding it on its
+// own page, so the document and the books never disagree. A credit note is never undone.
 export const SALES_JOURNAL_SOURCES = [
   'sales_invoice',
   'sales_receipt',
+  'sales_credit_note',
+  'sales_refund',
 ] as const satisfies readonly JournalSource[];
 export type SalesJournalSource = (typeof SALES_JOURNAL_SOURCES)[number];
 
```

- **`sales_return` joins `STOCK_JOURNAL_SOURCES`.** A return puts goods back into stock and their cost back into the
  inventory account. That is a stock entry, like a challan's: it may post to a stock account (step 14's
  `allowStock`), and the journal's Reverse refuses it, because reversing it alone would leave the goods in the
  warehouse while the books say they are gone.
- **`sales_credit_note` and `sales_refund` join `SALES_JOURNAL_SOURCES`.** They never touch a stock account, so they
  sit with the invoice and the receipt. Reverse refuses them too: a refund has its own Void button (like a receipt),
  and a credit note is never undone. If a credit note is wrong, the fix is a new invoice, and both documents stay in
  the books for the auditor to read.
- **`DOCUMENT_JOURNAL_SOURCES` needs no change.** It is built from the two lists, so the three new sources are in it
  at once. The database check that holds the same list grows in 15d.2.

```diff
 // revaluation (step 14): a change of value without a change of quantity — its quantity is zero.
 // delivery (step 15b): goods leaving for a customer on a delivery challan.
+// sales_return (step 15d): goods a customer sent back.
 export const MOVEMENT_KINDS = [
   'adjustment',
   'transfer_out',
   'transfer_in',
   'revaluation',
   'delivery',
+  'sales_return',
 ] as const;
 export type MovementKind = (typeof MOVEMENT_KINDS)[number];
 
```

- **`sales_return` as a movement kind.** The stock card shows "SR-2026-27-0003" with the right label, and a filter
  by kind can tell goods that came back from goods found in a count.

```diff
+  'return_cost_unknown',
+  'credit_note_invoice_required',
+  'credit_note_invoice_invalid',
+  'credit_note_date',
+  'credit_note_line_invalid',
+  'credit_note_over_quantity',
+  'credit_note_over_line',
+  'credit_note_return_invalid',
+  'credit_note_return_twice',
+  'credit_note_over_return',
+  'credit_note_not_posted',
+  'credit_note_amount_required',
+  'credit_note_allocation_invalid',
+  'credit_note_invoice_twice',
+  'credit_note_over_allocated',
+  'credit_note_over_invoice',
+  'refund_amount_required',
+  'refund_account_invalid',
+  'refund_source',
+  'refund_source_invalid',
+  'refund_over_source',
+  'refund_voided',
+  'receipt_has_refunds',
+  'sales_account_invalid',
+  'account_used_by_sales',
   // HTTP ও সার্ভার
   'invalid_cursor',
   'version_conflict',
```

- **The `return_*` codes.** `return_delivery_line_invalid`: a challan line that is not posted, not this customer's,
  or not the same item. `return_line_twice`: one challan line on two lines of a return. `return_batch_not_allowed`:
  a batch on a challan line (it comes back with the challan line's own batch). `return_serial_invalid`: a serial
  number that did not leave on that challan line. `return_over_delivered`: more than left on the line, less what
  came back already. `return_cost_unknown`: a line on its own for an item that never had a cost (no opening stock,
  nothing bought), so there is no average cost to bring it back at. (This one was added while writing the API in
  15d.3: the stock code's own `stock_cost_required` says "enter what it cost", and a return has no cost box.)
- **The `credit_note_*` codes for the document.** `credit_note_invoice_required` (no invoice chosen),
  `credit_note_invoice_invalid` (not posted, or another customer's), `credit_note_date` (dated before the invoice),
  `credit_note_line_invalid` (a line of another invoice; a unit the item does not have is `stock_unit_invalid`, as
  on every line). The three caps:
  `credit_note_over_quantity` (more than the line billed), `credit_note_over_line` (more money than the line has
  left to credit) and `credit_note_over_return` (more than the return line brought back).
  `credit_note_return_invalid` and `credit_note_return_twice` are about the return line a credit line names.
  `credit_note_not_posted`: applying the money of a draft.
- **The `credit_note_*` codes for the allocations** are the receipt's codes with their own names
  (`credit_note_amount_required`, `credit_note_allocation_invalid`, `credit_note_invoice_twice`,
  `credit_note_over_allocated`, `credit_note_over_invoice`). The words are almost the same, but "This receipt
  applies more than was paid" would be wrong on a credit note.
- **The `refund_*` codes.** `refund_source`: neither or both of receipt and credit note. `refund_source_invalid`:
  a source of another customer, a voided receipt or a draft credit note. `refund_over_source`: more than the source
  has left. `refund_voided`: a change to a voided refund. `refund_account_invalid`: an account that does not hold
  money. A refund's void reuses the receipt's codes (`receipt_void_reason_required`, `receipt_void_date`): it is the
  same form with the same words.
- **`receipt_has_refunds`.** Voiding a receipt whose money was partly paid back would take back money the customer
  never kept. The refund is voided first.
- **`sales_account_invalid`.** The sales returns account is not an active income account, or it is a group.
- **`account_used_by_sales`.** Archiving or deleting the account chosen as the sales returns account, like step 14's
  `account_used_by_stock`. Archived, it would refuse every credit note. (Also added in 15d.3.)

```diff
@@ -126,6 +126,20 @@ export const AUDIT_ACTIONS = [
   // An order confirmed or an invoice posted over the customer's credit limit, by someone with
   // sales.credit.override. The entity is that order or invoice.
   'credit_limit.overridden',
+  // step 15d
+  'sales_return.created',
+  'sales_return.updated',
+  'sales_return.deleted',
+  'sales_return.posted',
+  'credit_note.created',
+  'credit_note.updated',
+  'credit_note.deleted',
+  'credit_note.posted',
+  'credit_note.allocated',
+  'refund.created',
+  'refund.voided',
+  // The sales returns account in Settings → Sales. The entity is the workspace, like settings.
+  'sales_accounts.changed',
 ] as const;
 export type AuditAction = (typeof AUDIT_ACTIONS)[number];
 
@@ -164,6 +178,9 @@ export const AUDIT_ENTITY_TYPES = [
   'delivery',
   'invoice',
   'receipt',
+  'sales_return',
+  'credit_note',
+  'refund',
 ] as const;

```

- **The same pattern as 15c.** `credit_note.allocated` is its own action for the same reason as `receipt.allocated`:
  moving a credit from one invoice to another changes nothing in the books, but it changes what each invoice owes.
- **`refund.created` and `refund.voided`.** Money that leaves the company always leaves a row with who did it.
- **`sales_accounts.changed`.** Changing the returns account changes where every later credit note posts, so it is
  written down like `stock_accounts.changed` (step 14). The entity is the workspace.

### `sales-returns.ts` (new)

```ts
import { z } from 'zod';

import { errorCode } from './errors.js';
import { optionalText, versionSchema } from './fields.js';
import { defineRoute } from './http.js';
import { entryRefSchema, partyRefSchema } from './journal.js';
import { pageOf, pageQuerySchema } from './pagination.js';
import { documentRefSchema } from './sales.js';
import { STOCK_DOCUMENT_STATUSES } from './stock-adjustments.js';
import {
  documentSerialRules,
  MAX_STOCK_LINES,
  optionalIdSchema,
  stockLineFieldsSchema,
  stockLineRules,
  stockLineSchema,
} from './stock.js';

// A sales return (SR-2026-27-0001) brings goods a customer sent back into a warehouse. It is the
// challan the other way round: a draft can be changed, "Post" numbers it, puts the stock back and
// books its cost back (Dr Inventory / Cr Cost of goods sold). It moves no money: what the customer
// gets back is a credit note (credit-notes.ts), a separate document, like challan and invoice (you
// chose this).
//
// Every line comes back into the one warehouse the return names (you chose this): a pharmacy's
// expired strips go to the "Damage/Expiry" warehouse, and are written off later with a stock
// adjustment (step 13, reason expired).
//
// A line comes back from a line of a posted challan, or on its own:
//   a challan line   deliveryLineId: it comes back at the cost per unit it left at, so the cost of
//                    goods sold is reversed exactly, with the challan line's batch and some of its
//                    serial numbers. If the challan line was not billed yet, the invoice bills less
//                    and the order can deliver it again; if it was, a credit note gives the money
//                    back.
//   on its own       goods that left before the system was used. They come back at the average cost
//                    on the return's date.

// Why the goods came back. It decides nothing in the books; the list shows it, and the Mushak 6.7
// (later) prints it. unsold: a retailer sends back what did not sell (common with medicines and
// fast-moving goods).
export const RETURN_REASONS = [
  'damaged',
  'expired',
  'wrong_item',
  'quality',
  'unsold',
  'other',
] as const;
export type ReturnReason = (typeof RETURN_REASONS)[number];

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// What the API sends

export const salesReturnSummarySchema = z.object({
  id: z.uuid(),
  // null while a draft: given when it is posted, so posted numbers have no gaps
  number: z.string().nullable(),
  date: z.iso.date(),
  customer: partyRefSchema,
  // Where the goods came back into
  warehouseId: z.uuid(),
  // z.string(): the rule of every list the server may grow
  reason: z.string(),
  status: z.enum(STOCK_DOCUMENT_STATUSES),
  note: z.string().nullable(),
  lineCount: z.number().int(),
  postedAt: z.iso.datetime().nullable(),
  version: z.number().int(),
  updatedAt: z.iso.datetime(),
});
export type SalesReturnSummary = z.infer<typeof salesReturnSummarySchema>;

export const salesReturnLineSchema = stockLineSchema.extend({
  // The challan line the goods left on, and its challan's number; null for a line on its own
  deliveryLineId: z.uuid().nullable(),
  deliveryNumber: z.string().nullable(),
  // Whether a posted invoice had billed that challan line when the return was posted. true: the
  // customer paid for the goods, so a credit note gives the money back. false: the invoice bills
  // less instead, and nothing needs crediting. Always false for a draft and for a line on its own.
  billed: z.boolean(),
  // The invoice line that billed it, when billed: what a credit note for this line credits
  invoiceLineId: z.uuid().nullable(),
  invoiceId: z.uuid().nullable(),
  invoiceNumber: z.string().nullable(),
  // What posted credit note lines already gave back for this line, in the base unit
  creditedQuantity: z.string(),
  // What the goods came back at, once posted (step 14's value); null for a draft, and without
  // inventory.stock.value
  value: z.string().nullable(),
});
export type SalesReturnLine = z.infer<typeof salesReturnLineSchema>;

export const salesReturnSchema = salesReturnSummarySchema.extend({
  lines: z.array(salesReturnLineSchema),
  // The challans its lines came back from
  deliveries: z.array(documentRefSchema),
  // The credit notes written for it (drafts too, so nobody writes a second one by mistake)
  creditNotes: z.array(documentRefSchema),
  // The entry that put the cost back; null for a draft, or when the goods cost nothing
  entry: entryRefSchema.nullable(),
});
export type SalesReturn = z.infer<typeof salesReturnSchema>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// What the form sends

interface ReturnLineFields {
  deliveryLineId: string | null;
  batchId: string | null;
}

// A line from a challan comes back with the challan line's own batch (a challan line has one batch,
// step 15b), so it names none. A line on its own names the batch printed on the goods.
function returnLineRules<T extends ReturnLineFields>(line: T, ctx: z.RefinementCtx<T>): void {
  if (line.deliveryLineId !== null && line.batchId !== null) {
    ctx.addIssue({
      code: 'custom',
      path: ['batchId'],
      message: errorCode('return_batch_not_allowed'),
    });
  }
}

const salesReturnLineInputSchema = stockLineFieldsSchema
  .extend({
    // '' = a line on its own
    deliveryLineId: optionalIdSchema,
  })
  .superRefine((line, ctx) => {
    stockLineRules(line, ctx);
    returnLineRules(line, ctx);
  });
export type SalesReturnLineInput = z.infer<typeof salesReturnLineInputSchema>;
export type SalesReturnLineFormValues = z.input<typeof salesReturnLineInputSchema>;

const salesReturnFieldsSchema = z.object({
  customerId: z.uuid(errorCode('sales_customer_required')),
  date: z.iso.date(errorCode('stock_date_required')),
  warehouseId: z.uuid(errorCode('stock_warehouse_invalid')),
  reason: z.enum(RETURN_REASONS),
  note: optionalText(300),
  lines: z
    .array(salesReturnLineInputSchema)
    .min(1, errorCode('stock_lines_required'))
    .max(MAX_STOCK_LINES),
  // true = "Post": save and post in one step, or nothing at all
  post: z.boolean(),
});

type SalesReturnRuleInput = z.output<typeof salesReturnFieldsSchema>;

// A challan line once per return: it has one batch, so a second line for it has no reason to exist,
// and how much can still come back is easier to read on one line
function salesReturnRules(input: SalesReturnRuleInput, ctx: z.RefinementCtx<SalesReturnRuleInput>) {
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  input.lines.forEach((line, index) => {
    if (line.deliveryLineId === null) return;
    if (seen.has(line.deliveryLineId)) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: 'custom',
        path: ['lines', index, 'deliveryLineId'],
        message: errorCode('return_line_twice'),
      });
    }
    seen.add(line.deliveryLineId);
  });
  documentSerialRules(input, ctx);
}

export const salesReturnInputSchema = salesReturnFieldsSchema.superRefine(salesReturnRules);
export type SalesReturnInput = z.infer<typeof salesReturnInputSchema>;

export const updateSalesReturnInputSchema = salesReturnFieldsSchema
  .extend({ version: versionSchema })
  .superRefine(salesReturnRules);
export type UpdateSalesReturnInput = z.infer<typeof updateSalesReturnInputSchema>;
export type SalesReturnFormValues = z.input<typeof updateSalesReturnInputSchema>;

export const salesReturnVersionInputSchema = z.object({ version: versionSchema });

export const deleteSalesReturnQuerySchema = z.object({
  version: z.coerce.number<number>().int().min(1),
});

export const salesReturnListQuerySchema = pageQuerySchema.extend({
  status: z.enum(STOCK_DOCUMENT_STATUSES).optional(),
  customerId: z.uuid().optional(),
  warehouseId: z.uuid().optional(),
});
export type SalesReturnListQuery = z.input<typeof salesReturnListQuerySchema>;

export const salesReturnPageSchema = pageOf(salesReturnSummarySchema);
export type SalesReturnPage = z.infer<typeof salesReturnPageSchema>;

const salesReturnParamsSchema = z.object({ id: z.uuid() });

// Reading needs no permission, like every stock document. Writing and posting need
// sales.return.manage: the store keeper who takes the goods back in.
export const salesReturnRoutes = {
  list: defineRoute({
    method: 'GET',
    path: '/sales-returns',
    summary: 'Sales returns, newest date first',
    auth: 'bearer',
    status: 200,
    query: salesReturnListQuerySchema,
    response: salesReturnPageSchema,
  }),
  get: defineRoute({
    method: 'GET',
    path: '/sales-returns/:id',
    summary: 'One sales return with its lines',
    auth: 'bearer',
    status: 200,
    params: salesReturnParamsSchema,
    response: salesReturnSchema,
  }),
  create: defineRoute({
    method: 'POST',
    path: '/sales-returns',
    summary: 'Write a sales return as a draft, or write and post it in one step',
    auth: 'bearer',
    permission: 'sales.return.manage',
    status: 201,
    body: salesReturnInputSchema,
    response: salesReturnSchema,
  }),
  update: defineRoute({
    method: 'PUT',
    path: '/sales-returns/:id',
    summary: 'Change a draft sales return, and optionally post it',
    auth: 'bearer',
    permission: 'sales.return.manage',
    status: 200,
    params: salesReturnParamsSchema,
    body: updateSalesReturnInputSchema,
    response: salesReturnSchema,
  }),
  remove: defineRoute({
    method: 'DELETE',
    path: '/sales-returns/:id',
    summary: 'Delete a draft sales return',
    auth: 'bearer',
    permission: 'sales.return.manage',
    status: 204,
    params: salesReturnParamsSchema,
    query: deleteSalesReturnQuerySchema,
    response: z.void(),
  }),
  post: defineRoute({
    method: 'POST',
    path: '/sales-returns/:id/post',
    summary:
      'Post a draft sales return: it gets its number, puts the stock back and books its cost',
    auth: 'bearer',
    permission: 'sales.return.manage',
    status: 200,
    params: salesReturnParamsSchema,
    body: salesReturnVersionInputSchema,
    response: salesReturnSchema,
  }),
};
```

- **A return moves stock, never money.** You chose two documents. The return is the challan the other way round, and
  the credit note is the invoice the other way round. So a pharmacy can take back expired strips today (the store
  keeper) and the accountant can write the credit note tomorrow, or never, if the goods were not billed yet.
- **One warehouse for the whole return.** You chose "everything goes back into stock". The person picks where:
  usually a "Damage/Expiry" warehouse. Expired goods leave stock later with a stock adjustment (reason `expired`),
  which books the loss to the expired-stock account of step 14. So each document does one job.
- **`RETURN_REASONS` decides nothing in the books.** It is there for the list and for reports ("how much came back
  as expired this year"), and the Mushak 6.7 prints a reason. `unsold` is the common case in medicine and
  fast-moving goods: the shop sends back what it did not sell.
- **A line from a challan, or on its own.** A line from a challan comes back at the cost per unit it left at (you
  chose this), so the cost of goods sold goes back to exactly what it was. A line on its own is for goods that left
  before the company used Omnivo; there is no challan to read a cost from, so it comes back at the average cost on
  the return's date.
- **`billed` on the line.** It answers one question: did the customer already pay for these goods? It is fixed when
  the return is posted, because the answer can change later (the challan line may be billed tomorrow). If the line
  was not billed, the invoice simply bills less and nothing needs crediting. If it was, the return page offers a
  credit note for it. A draft says `false`; the server works it out at posting.
- **`invoiceLineId` and `creditedQuantity`.** The return page's "Make credit note" button needs the invoice line to
  credit, and how much of the line is already credited, so it never offers to credit the same goods twice.
- **`creditNotes` lists drafts too.** If someone already started a credit note for this return, the page shows it,
  and the next person opens that draft instead of writing a second one.
- **`value` is null without `inventory.stock.value`.** The same rule as the challan (step 15b): what goods cost is
  only shown to people allowed to see it.
- **No batch on a challan line (`return_batch_not_allowed`).** A challan line takes from one batch (15b splits two
  batches into two lines), so the batch that comes back is known. Asking for it again could only be wrong. A line on
  its own names the batch printed on the goods; the server asks for it on a batch product (`stock_batch_required`,
  step 13).
- **Serial numbers are still sent.** A challan line of 10 phones may get 2 back, and the IMEIs say which 2. The
  server checks each one left on that challan line (`return_serial_invalid`).
- **One challan line once per return (`return_line_twice`).** Two lines for one challan line could only differ in
  quantity, so they are one line typed twice. One line also makes the cap easy to read: "45 can still come back".
  The error sits on the second line, so the first one stays clean.
- **`documentSerialRules`** from step 13: one IMEI on two lines is a scanning slip, on a return as on a challan.

### `credit-notes.ts` (new)

```ts
import { z } from 'zod';

import { errorCode } from './errors.js';
import { optionalText, versionSchema } from './fields.js';
import { defineRoute } from './http.js';
import { MAX_INVOICE_LINES, type Invoice } from './invoices.js';
import { entryRefSchema, partyRefSchema } from './journal.js';
import { isZeroMoney } from './money.js';
import { pageOf, pageQuerySchema } from './pagination.js';
import { plainQuantity } from './quantities.js';
import {
  type AllocationCodes,
  allocationsSchemaFor,
  receiptAllocationSchema,
  uniqueInvoiceRules,
} from './receipts.js';
import {
  defaultLineDescription,
  salesLineFieldsSchema,
  salesLineRules,
  salesLineSchema,
} from './sales.js';
import { optionalIdSchema } from './stock.js';

// A credit note (CN-2026-27-0001) takes back part or all of a posted invoice: goods that came back
// on a sales return, a price cut after the sale, a billing mistake. Posting it books the sale back:
// Dr Sales returns (the account chosen in Settings → Sales, or Sales itself) for the net / Dr Output
// VAT for the VAT / Cr Accounts receivable (with the customer) for the total.
//
// It is always for ONE posted invoice, and each line credits one of that invoice's lines, at that
// line's VAT rate. The Mushak 6.7 (later) names the original invoice, and the VAT taken back must be
// the VAT that was charged, so a credit note without an invoice would not be a VAT credit note.
//
// Its money (you chose this) is first applied to its own invoice, up to what the invoice still owes;
// the rest is the customer's advance, which can be applied to a later invoice or paid back with a
// refund (refunds.ts). The allocations work like a money receipt's.
//
// A draft can be changed or deleted. A posted credit note is never changed: there is no void.

export const CREDIT_NOTE_STATUSES = ['draft', 'posted'] as const;
export type CreditNoteStatus = (typeof CREDIT_NOTE_STATUSES)[number];

// Why it was written. goods_returned is what the form starts with when it is made from a return.
export const CREDIT_NOTE_REASONS = [
  'goods_returned',
  'price_adjustment',
  'billing_error',
  'other',
] as const;
export type CreditNoteReason = (typeof CREDIT_NOTE_REASONS)[number];

// '2026-08-31' + 6 → '2027-02-28': the day of the month, or the month's last day when it is shorter.
// UTC arithmetic, so no time zone can move the day (the rule of shiftIsoDate in journal.ts).
function addMonths(isoDate: string, months: number): string {
  const year = Number(isoDate.slice(0, 4));
  const month = Number(isoDate.slice(5, 7)) - 1 + months;
  const day = Number(isoDate.slice(8, 10));
  const lastDay = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month + 1, 0)).getUTCDate();
  return new Date(Date.UTC(year, month, Math.min(day, lastDay))).toISOString().slice(0, 10);
}

// VAT law lets a credit note reduce output VAT only within 6 months of the supply. You chose a
// warning, not a block: the form shows a notice, and saving and posting still work.
export function creditNoteIsLate(invoiceDate: string, date: string): boolean {
  return date > addMonths(invoiceDate, 6);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// What the API sends

// The invoice it credits. Posted, so it has a number.
export const creditedInvoiceSchema = z.object({
  id: z.uuid(),
  number: z.string(),
  date: z.iso.date(),
});
export type CreditedInvoice = z.infer<typeof creditedInvoiceSchema>;

export const creditNoteSummarySchema = z.object({
  id: z.uuid(),
  // null while a draft
  number: z.string().nullable(),
  date: z.iso.date(),
  customer: partyRefSchema,
  invoice: creditedInvoiceSchema,
  // The invoice's branch: every line of its entry carries it, so the sale comes off where it was made
  branchId: z.uuid(),
  // z.string(): the rule of every list the server may grow
  reason: z.string(),
  status: z.enum(CREDIT_NOTE_STATUSES),
  net: z.string(),
  vat: z.string(),
  total: z.string(),
  // What is applied to invoices, and what refunds paid back. unappliedOf() (receipts.ts) is the
  // customer's advance that is left.
  applied: z.string(),
  refunded: z.string(),
  lineCount: z.number().int(),
  postedAt: z.iso.datetime().nullable(),
  version: z.number().int(),
  updatedAt: z.iso.datetime(),
});
export type CreditNoteSummary = z.infer<typeof creditNoteSummarySchema>;

export const creditNoteLineSchema = salesLineSchema.extend({
  // The invoice line it credits: the item and the VAT rate come from there
  invoiceLineId: z.uuid(),
  // The return line it gives the money back for, and that return's number; null for a price cut
  returnLineId: z.uuid().nullable(),
  returnNumber: z.string().nullable(),
});
export type CreditNoteLine = z.infer<typeof creditNoteLineSchema>;

export const creditNoteSchema = creditNoteSummarySchema.extend({
  // The invoice's own setting: the credit note works its lines out the same way, so crediting a line
  // in full gives back exactly what the line charged
  pricesIncludeVat: z.boolean(),
  discount: z.string(),
  note: z.string().nullable(),
  lines: z.array(creditNoteLineSchema),
  // The invoices its money is applied to (its own first)
  allocations: z.array(receiptAllocationSchema),
  // null for a draft, and for a credit note of ৳0
  entry: entryRefSchema.nullable(),
});
export type CreditNote = z.infer<typeof creditNoteSchema>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// What the form sends

// A line names the invoice line it credits. No item and no VAT rate: both are the invoice line's.
// The unit may be any of the item's units (3 strips back from a line of 2 boxes). A price cut is a
// line with the quantity it applies to and the cut per unit: 100 pcs at ৳2.
const creditNoteLineInputSchema = salesLineFieldsSchema
  .omit({ variantId: true, taxRateId: true })
  .extend({
    invoiceLineId: z.uuid(errorCode('credit_note_line_invalid')),
    // '' = not for a return line
    returnLineId: optionalIdSchema,
  })
  .superRefine(salesLineRules);
export type CreditNoteLineInput = z.infer<typeof creditNoteLineInputSchema>;
export type CreditNoteLineFormValues = z.input<typeof creditNoteLineInputSchema>;

const creditNoteFieldsSchema = z.object({
  invoiceId: z.uuid(errorCode('credit_note_invoice_required')),
  // Not before the invoice's date (credit_note_date, checked by the server: only it reads the
  // invoice for sure)
  date: z.iso.date(errorCode('sales_date_required')),
  reason: z.enum(CREDIT_NOTE_REASONS),
  note: optionalText(500),
  lines: z
    .array(creditNoteLineInputSchema)
    .min(1, errorCode('sales_lines_required'))
    .max(MAX_INVOICE_LINES),
  // true = "Post": save and post in one step, or nothing at all
  post: z.boolean(),
});

type CreditNoteRuleInput = z.output<typeof creditNoteFieldsSchema>;

// A return line once: two lines for it would give its money back twice. Two lines may credit one
// invoice line (a price cut and a return), so that one is not checked here; the server checks the
// sum against what the line charged.
function creditNoteRules(input: CreditNoteRuleInput, ctx: z.RefinementCtx<CreditNoteRuleInput>) {
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  input.lines.forEach((line, index) => {
    if (line.returnLineId === null) return;
    if (seen.has(line.returnLineId)) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: 'custom',
        path: ['lines', index, 'returnLineId'],
        message: errorCode('credit_note_return_twice'),
      });
    }
    seen.add(line.returnLineId);
  });
}

export const creditNoteInputSchema = creditNoteFieldsSchema.superRefine(creditNoteRules);
export type CreditNoteInput = z.infer<typeof creditNoteInputSchema>;

export const updateCreditNoteInputSchema = creditNoteFieldsSchema
  .extend({ version: versionSchema })
  .superRefine(creditNoteRules);
export type UpdateCreditNoteInput = z.infer<typeof updateCreditNoteInputSchema>;
export type CreditNoteFormValues = z.input<typeof updateCreditNoteInputSchema>;

export const creditNoteVersionInputSchema = z.object({ version: versionSchema });

const CREDIT_NOTE_ALLOCATION_CODES = {
  invoice: 'credit_note_allocation_invalid',
  required: 'credit_note_amount_required',
  twice: 'credit_note_invoice_twice',
} as const satisfies AllocationCodes;

// Apply its money again, like a receipt's (receiptAllocationsInputSchema). The server checks the
// total against the credit note's own, less what refunds paid back (credit_note_over_allocated).
export const creditNoteAllocationsInputSchema = z
  .object({
    version: versionSchema,
    allocations: allocationsSchemaFor(CREDIT_NOTE_ALLOCATION_CODES),
  })
  .superRefine(uniqueInvoiceRules(CREDIT_NOTE_ALLOCATION_CODES.twice));
export type CreditNoteAllocationsInput = z.infer<typeof creditNoteAllocationsInputSchema>;
export type CreditNoteAllocationsFormValues = z.input<typeof creditNoteAllocationsInputSchema>;

// "Credit whole invoice" (you chose this): every line of the invoice, as it was billed. The app
// saves these as a draft in one click. Worked out the same way as the invoice (the invoice's own
// pricesIncludeVat), each line gives back exactly what it charged, to the paisa. Only while no
// posted credit note exists for the invoice (canCreditWhole): after one, the full amounts would be
// more than is left to credit.
// The values are the form's, like the app's toFormLine() (15b): the API sends 4 decimals
// ("8.0000"), and the discount box takes at most 2, so trailing zeros go; a description that is
// just the product's name stays empty, so the server writes it the same way.
export function wholeInvoiceCreditLines(
  invoice: Pick<Invoice, 'lines'>,
): CreditNoteLineFormValues[] {
  return invoice.lines.map((line) => ({
    invoiceLineId: line.id,
    returnLineId: '',
    unitId: line.unitId,
    quantity: plainQuantity(line.quantity),
    description: line.description === defaultLineDescription(line) ? '' : line.description,
    unitPrice: line.unitPrice,
    discountType: line.discountType,
    discount: isZeroMoney(line.discount) ? '' : plainQuantity(line.discount),
  }));
}

export function canCreditWhole(invoice: Pick<Invoice, 'status' | 'creditNotes'>): boolean {
  return invoice.status === 'posted' && invoice.creditNotes.length === 0;
}

export const deleteCreditNoteQuerySchema = z.object({
  version: z.coerce.number<number>().int().min(1),
});

export const creditNoteListQuerySchema = pageQuerySchema.extend({
  status: z.enum(CREDIT_NOTE_STATUSES).optional(),
  customerId: z.uuid().optional(),
  invoiceId: z.uuid().optional(),
});
export type CreditNoteListQuery = z.input<typeof creditNoteListQuerySchema>;

export const creditNotePageSchema = pageOf(creditNoteSummarySchema);
export type CreditNotePage = z.infer<typeof creditNotePageSchema>;

const creditNoteParamsSchema = z.object({ id: z.uuid() });

// Reading needs no permission, like the invoices. Writing, posting and applying need
// sales.credit_note.manage: usually the accountant.
export const creditNoteRoutes = {
  list: defineRoute({
    method: 'GET',
    path: '/credit-notes',
    summary: 'Credit notes, newest date first',
    auth: 'bearer',
    status: 200,
    query: creditNoteListQuerySchema,
    response: creditNotePageSchema,
  }),
  get: defineRoute({
    method: 'GET',
    path: '/credit-notes/:id',
    summary: 'One credit note with its lines and where its money went',
    auth: 'bearer',
    status: 200,
    params: creditNoteParamsSchema,
    response: creditNoteSchema,
  }),
  create: defineRoute({
    method: 'POST',
    path: '/credit-notes',
    summary: 'Write a credit note as a draft, or write and post it in one step',
    auth: 'bearer',
    permission: 'sales.credit_note.manage',
    status: 201,
    body: creditNoteInputSchema,
    response: creditNoteSchema,
  }),
  update: defineRoute({
    method: 'PUT',
    path: '/credit-notes/:id',
    summary: 'Change a draft credit note, and optionally post it',
    auth: 'bearer',
    permission: 'sales.credit_note.manage',
    status: 200,
    params: creditNoteParamsSchema,
    body: updateCreditNoteInputSchema,
    response: creditNoteSchema,
  }),
  remove: defineRoute({
    method: 'DELETE',
    path: '/credit-notes/:id',
    summary: 'Delete a draft credit note',
    auth: 'bearer',
    permission: 'sales.credit_note.manage',
    status: 204,
    params: creditNoteParamsSchema,
    query: deleteCreditNoteQuerySchema,
    response: z.void(),
  }),
  post: defineRoute({
    method: 'POST',
    path: '/credit-notes/:id/post',
    summary:
      'Post a draft credit note: it gets its number, books the sale back and applies its money',
    auth: 'bearer',
    permission: 'sales.credit_note.manage',
    status: 200,
    params: creditNoteParamsSchema,
    body: creditNoteVersionInputSchema,
    response: creditNoteSchema,
  }),
  allocate: defineRoute({
    method: 'PUT',
    path: '/credit-notes/:id/allocations',
    summary: "Change which invoices a credit note's money is applied to",
    auth: 'bearer',
    permission: 'sales.credit_note.manage',
    status: 200,
    params: creditNoteParamsSchema,
    body: creditNoteAllocationsInputSchema,
    response: creditNoteSchema,
  }),
};
```

- **Always for one posted invoice.** The Mushak 6.7 names the original invoice, and VAT law lets a credit note take
  back only the VAT that was charged on it. A credit note without an invoice could not say which VAT it reverses.
  So `invoiceId` is required, and the customer, the branch and `pricesIncludeVat` all come from the invoice: the
  form never asks for them, so they can never disagree with it.
- **Each line credits one invoice line, at its VAT rate.** The line sends no item and no VAT rate. Both come from the
  invoice line on the server. If the NBR changes a rate between the invoice and the credit note, the credit note still
  reverses the old rate, which is what the law asks.
- **Any unit of the item.** A line billed as 2 boxes of 24 may get 3 strips back. The quantity cap is checked in the
  base unit, so the unit does not matter to the server.
- **Two caps, one in quantity and one in money.** A line may not credit more pieces than the invoice line billed,
  and all the credit note lines on one invoice line together may not take back more money than it charged. Why money
  and not quantity for the sum: a price cut of ৳2 on all 100 pieces, and later a return of 10 pieces, are both real.
  Counted in pieces, the price cut would use up all 100 and the return could not be credited. Counted in money, both
  fit, up to what was billed.
- **A price cut is an ordinary line.** The quantity it applies to and the cut per piece: 100 pcs at ৳2. So it prints
  like any line, and its VAT is worked out by the same `lineAmounts()` as the invoice.
- **`creditNoteIsLate()` is a warning only.** You chose not to block. VAT law gives 6 months; the form shows a `warn`
  notice after that, and the accountant decides. Months are counted on the calendar: 31 August plus 6 months is
  the last day of February, the same rule people use. The arithmetic runs in UTC, like `shiftIsoDate()`, so no time
  zone can move the day.
- **`creditNoteRules()` checks only the return line.** One return line on two credit lines would give its money back
  twice. Two lines on one invoice line are fine (a price cut and a return); the server checks their sum.
- **The allocations reuse the receipt's code.** `allocationsSchemaFor()` and `uniqueInvoiceRules()` (below, in
  `receipts.ts`) build the same table with the credit note's own error codes. The money is applied to its own invoice
  at posting; this route moves it later, like a receipt's.
- **`wholeInvoiceCreditLines()`** is the "Credit whole invoice" button you chose. It needs no route: the app turns
  every invoice line into a credit line and saves a draft. The values are the form's, like the app's `toFormLine()`
  (15b): the API sends `8.0000`, the discount box takes 2 decimals, so trailing zeros go. Worked out with the
  invoice's own `pricesIncludeVat`, each line gives back exactly what it charged, to the paisa; the test proves it.
- **`canCreditWhole()`.** After one posted credit note, the full amounts would be more than is left to credit, and
  posting would fail on the money cap. So the button only shows while there is none. A draft does not count: it may
  never be posted.
- **No void.** A posted credit note is final. If it was wrong, a new invoice bills the amount again, and both stay in
  the books, which is what an auditor wants to see.

### `refunds.ts` (new)

```ts
import { z } from 'zod';

import { errorCode } from './errors.js';
import { optionalText } from './fields.js';
import { defineRoute } from './http.js';
import { entryRefSchema, partyRefSchema } from './journal.js';
import { pageOf, pageQuerySchema } from './pagination.js';
import {
  PAYMENT_METHODS,
  positiveAmountSchema,
  RECEIPT_STATUSES,
  voidReceiptInputSchema,
} from './receipts.js';
import { optionalIdSchema } from './stock.js';

// A refund (RF-2026-27-0001) is money paid back to a customer out of a cash, bank or wallet account
// (you chose this): Dr Accounts receivable (with the customer) / Cr the account. Like a money
// receipt, saving posts it, and a mistake is voided (its entry reversed on the void date).
//
// It pays back the customer's own advance, from ONE place: the money of a receipt or of a credit
// note that is not applied to an invoice. That money is then used up (receipts.refunded,
// credit_notes.refunded), so it cannot also be applied to an invoice later. Paying back from two
// places is two refunds. Because it only ever pays back what the customer already paid or was
// credited, it never needs a credit limit check.
//
//   posted  in the books
//   voided  reversed, and its money is the source's advance again
export const REFUND_STATUSES = RECEIPT_STATUSES;
export type RefundStatus = (typeof REFUND_STATUSES)[number];

// Where the money it pays back came from
export const REFUND_SOURCE_TYPES = ['receipt', 'credit_note'] as const;
export type RefundSourceType = (typeof REFUND_SOURCE_TYPES)[number];

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// What the API sends

export const refundSourceSchema = z.object({
  type: z.enum(REFUND_SOURCE_TYPES),
  id: z.uuid(),
  // A receipt is numbered when saved and a credit note pays back only once posted, so never null
  number: z.string(),
});
export type RefundSource = z.infer<typeof refundSourceSchema>;

export const refundSummarySchema = z.object({
  id: z.uuid(),
  number: z.string(),
  date: z.iso.date(),
  customer: partyRefSchema,
  amount: z.string(),
  method: z.enum(PAYMENT_METHODS),
  // The cheque number, the bKash TrxID of the money sent
  reference: z.string().nullable(),
  // The money account it was paid out of
  accountId: z.uuid(),
  branchId: z.uuid(),
  source: refundSourceSchema,
  status: z.enum(REFUND_STATUSES),
  version: z.number().int(),
  updatedAt: z.iso.datetime(),
});
export type RefundSummary = z.infer<typeof refundSummarySchema>;

export const refundSchema = refundSummarySchema.extend({
  note: z.string().nullable(),
  entry: entryRefSchema,
  // The reversal that voided it, its date and why; null while posted
  voidEntry: entryRefSchema.nullable(),
  voidDate: z.iso.date().nullable(),
  voidReason: z.string().nullable(),
});
export type Refund = z.infer<typeof refundSchema>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// What the form sends

export const refundInputSchema = z
  .object({
    customerId: z.uuid(errorCode('sales_customer_required')),
    date: z.iso.date(errorCode('sales_date_required')),
    // Not more than the source has left (refund_over_source, checked by the server)
    amount: positiveAmountSchema('refund_amount_required'),
    accountId: z.uuid(errorCode('refund_account_invalid')),
    method: z.enum(PAYMENT_METHODS),
    reference: optionalText(60),
    branchId: z.uuid(errorCode('sales_branch_invalid')),
    note: optionalText(300),
    // Exactly one of the two: '' = not this kind
    receiptId: optionalIdSchema,
    creditNoteId: optionalIdSchema,
  })
  .superRefine((input, ctx) => {
    // Neither or both: the error sits on the first box, where the form shows the source picker
    if ((input.receiptId === null) === (input.creditNoteId === null)) {
      ctx.addIssue({ code: 'custom', path: ['receiptId'], message: errorCode('refund_source') });
    }
  });
export type RefundInput = z.infer<typeof refundInputSchema>;
export type RefundFormValues = z.input<typeof refundInputSchema>;

// The same as a receipt's: the day it turned out wrong, and why
export const voidRefundInputSchema = voidReceiptInputSchema;
export type VoidRefundInput = z.infer<typeof voidRefundInputSchema>;

export const refundListQuerySchema = pageQuerySchema.extend({
  status: z.enum(REFUND_STATUSES).optional(),
  customerId: z.uuid().optional(),
});
export type RefundListQuery = z.input<typeof refundListQuerySchema>;

export const refundPageSchema = pageOf(refundSummarySchema);
export type RefundPage = z.infer<typeof refundPageSchema>;

const refundParamsSchema = z.object({ id: z.uuid() });

// Reading needs no permission, like the receipts. Paying money out needs sales.refund.manage, its
// own key: taking money in (sales.receipt.manage) does not let anyone hand it out.
export const refundRoutes = {
  list: defineRoute({
    method: 'GET',
    path: '/refunds',
    summary: 'Refunds, newest date first',
    auth: 'bearer',
    status: 200,
    query: refundListQuerySchema,
    response: refundPageSchema,
  }),
  get: defineRoute({
    method: 'GET',
    path: '/refunds/:id',
    summary: 'One refund',
    auth: 'bearer',
    status: 200,
    params: refundParamsSchema,
    response: refundSchema,
  }),
  create: defineRoute({
    method: 'POST',
    path: '/refunds',
    summary: "Pay a customer's advance back; it is posted at once",
    auth: 'bearer',
    permission: 'sales.refund.manage',
    status: 201,
    body: refundInputSchema,
    response: refundSchema,
  }),
  void: defineRoute({
    method: 'POST',
    path: '/refunds/:id/void',
    summary: 'Void a refund: reverse its entry and give the money back to its source',
    auth: 'bearer',
    permission: 'sales.refund.manage',
    status: 200,
    params: refundParamsSchema,
    body: voidRefundInputSchema,
    response: refundSchema,
  }),
};
```

- **It pays back the customer's own money.** A refund takes money that is not applied to any invoice: what is left of
  a receipt (an overpayment, an advance) or of a credit note (goods returned after the customer paid). That money is
  then used up, so it cannot also be applied to an invoice later.
- **One source per refund.** `receiptId` or `creditNoteId`, exactly one (`refund_source`). Paying back from two
  places is two refunds. With one source, "how much is left to pay back" is a single number on one document, and the
  refund page can link straight to it.
- **No credit check.** A refund only gives back what the customer already paid or was credited, so it can never take
  the customer over the limit.
- **Saved means posted, and a mistake is voided.** The same rules as a receipt: the money already left the cash box.
  Voiding reverses the entry on the void date, and the money is the source's advance again.
- **`REFUND_STATUSES = RECEIPT_STATUSES`.** The same two states with the same meaning. One list means the app's pill
  and the API's check cannot drift apart.
- **`voidRefundInputSchema` is the receipt's.** The same two boxes (the date and why) with the same rules.

### `sales-accounts.ts` (new)

```ts
import { z } from 'zod';

import { defineRoute } from './http.js';
import { optionalIdSchema } from './stock.js';

// The account a credit note takes the sale back from (step 15d, you chose a setting): "Sales
// returns", an income account that sits under Revenue with a debit balance, so the profit and loss
// shows the sales and what came back as two numbers, and the return rate is plain to see. A
// setting the owner changes in Settings → Sales; the pharmacy and retail templates fill it with
// their 4120 Sales returns.
//   returns  null = no account chosen: a credit note takes the sale back from the Sales account
//            itself (the account with the 'sales' purpose), and the profit and loss shows net sales
// The server checks the account is an active income account that is not a group
// (sales_account_invalid), like the stock accounts of step 14.
export const salesAccountsSchema = z.object({
  returns: z.uuid().nullable(),
});
export type SalesAccounts = z.infer<typeof salesAccountsSchema>;

// The form's empty select sends '': back to the Sales account
export const updateSalesAccountsInputSchema = z.object({
  returns: optionalIdSchema,
});
export type UpdateSalesAccountsInput = z.infer<typeof updateSalesAccountsInputSchema>;
export type SalesAccountsFormValues = z.input<typeof updateSalesAccountsInputSchema>;

export const salesAccountRoutes = {
  // Reading needs no permission: the settings page shows it to everyone who opens it
  get: defineRoute({
    method: 'GET',
    path: '/sales-accounts',
    summary: 'The account credit notes take sales back from',
    auth: 'bearer',
    status: 200,
    response: salesAccountsSchema,
  }),
  update: defineRoute({
    method: 'PUT',
    path: '/sales-accounts',
    summary: 'Choose the account credit notes take sales back from',
    auth: 'bearer',
    permission: 'core.settings.manage',
    status: 200,
    body: updateSalesAccountsInputSchema,
    response: salesAccountsSchema,
  }),
};
```

- **Why a setting.** You chose "Settings-এ বাছাই করা account". A credit note can take the sale back from the Sales
  account itself (the profit and loss then shows net sales), or from a separate "Sales returns" account (it shows
  gross sales and returns, and the return rate is easy to read). Companies choose differently, so it is a setting.
- **null = the Sales account.** A workspace that never opens the setting still works: its credit notes debit Sales.
  The pharmacy and retail templates already have "4120 Sales returns", so their setup fills it in (15d.3), and a
  migration does the same for old workspaces (15d.2).
- **A separate resource, not a field on `/settings`.** `PUT /settings` takes the whole form. A new required field
  there would break every client that saves the company profile, and an optional one would be reset to null by any
  client that does not send it. `/stock-accounts` (step 14) already solved this with its own small route; this
  follows it.
- **An income account.** "Sales returns" is income with a debit balance (a contra account): it sits under Revenue,
  so the profit and loss subtracts it in the right place. The server checks the type (`sales_account_invalid`),
  because the form's data cannot be trusted for it.

  (15d.3) checks it, both with this one function.
- **`returnState` and `returns`.** The challan list shows "Partly returned" or "Returned", and the challan page links
  to the returns.
- **`invoiceState` skips a line that came back in full.** Such a line has nothing to bill. Without this, a challan
  whose one unbilled line came back would show "Partly invoiced" forever.
- **`return: 'returnable'`.** The return form asks for this customer's posted challans that still have something
  that can come back, and nothing else.

- **A credit settles an invoice like a payment.** You chose: the credit note's money goes to its invoice first. So an
  invoice of ৳1,150 with ৳1,000 paid and ৳150 credited owes nothing. `amountCredited` is that applied credit, kept
  next to `amountPaid`, and `amountDueOf()` is the one place that subtracts both.
- **`paymentStatusOf()` and `isOverdue()` count both.** An invoice settled by a credit note is not overdue: nobody
  should chase a customer for money the company gave back. Every caller of these two functions (the API's filters,
  the pills, the mocks) now passes `amountCredited`; the type check finds each one.
- **`creditNoteTotal` and `creditStateOf()`.** A credit note for an invoice that was already paid still credits it;
  its money becomes an advance. So "how much of this invoice was credited" is a different number from "how much
  credit was applied here". The "Credited" pill you chose reads the first one.
- **`credited` on each line.** What posted credit notes took back from that line, in money. The credit note form
  shows "৳1,000 of ৳1,150 left to credit" with it, and the server checks the same number.
- **`creditNotes` on the invoice.** The invoice page lists them, and `canCreditWhole()` reads it.

- **`refunded` and `unappliedOf()`.** A receipt's money can now go three ways: to invoices, back to the customer, or
  nowhere yet. `unappliedOf()` is what is left, and the same function works for a credit note, which has the same
  three columns.
- **`positiveAmountSchema()`, `allocationsSchemaFor()`, `uniqueInvoiceRules()`.** The receipt's amount box and
  allocation table, made into small factories that take the error codes. The receipt calls them with its old codes,
  so it behaves exactly as before (its tests still pass unchanged). Credit notes and refunds call them with theirs.
- **`uniqueInvoiceRules()` returns a generic function.** `superRefine` needs a function of the schema's own type. A
  generic arrow (`<T extends AllocationFields>(input: T, ctx) => …`) fits any schema with an `allocations` array,
  without a cast.

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import { billableQuantity } from './deliveries.js';
import { contractErrorMap } from './errors.js';
import { salesReturnInputSchema } from './sales-returns.js';

const CUSTOMER = '01920000-0000-7000-8000-000000000001';
const WAREHOUSE = '01920000-0000-7000-8000-000000000002';
const VARIANT = '01920000-0000-7000-8000-000000000003';
const UNIT = '01920000-0000-7000-8000-000000000004';
const DELIVERY_LINE = '01920000-0000-7000-8000-000000000005';
const BATCH = '01920000-0000-7000-8000-000000000006';

function returnLine(extra: object = {}) {
  return {
    variantId: VARIANT,
    unitId: UNIT,
    quantity: '3',
    batchId: '',
    serialNumbers: [],
    deliveryLineId: DELIVERY_LINE,
    ...extra,
  };
}

function salesReturn(extra: object = {}) {
  return {
    customerId: CUSTOMER,
    date: '2026-10-11',
    warehouseId: WAREHOUSE,
    reason: 'expired',
    note: '',
    lines: [returnLine()],
    post: false,
    ...extra,
  };
}

// The error codes where the form will show them: field path → code
function errorsOf(result: {
  success: boolean;
  error?: { issues: { path: PropertyKey[]; message: string }[] };
}) {
  return Object.fromEntries(
    (result.error?.issues ?? []).map((issue) => [issue.path.map(String).join('.'), issue.message]),
  );
}

describe('sales return input', () => {
  it('takes a line from a challan and a line on its own with its batch', () => {
    const parsed = salesReturnInputSchema.parse(
      salesReturn({
        lines: [returnLine(), returnLine({ deliveryLineId: '', batchId: BATCH })],
      }),
    );
    expect(parsed.lines.map((line) => [line.deliveryLineId, line.batchId])).toEqual([
      [DELIVERY_LINE, null],
      [null, BATCH],
    ]);
  });

  it("refuses a batch on a challan line: it comes back with the challan line's own", () => {
    const result = salesReturnInputSchema.safeParse(
      salesReturn({ lines: [returnLine({ batchId: BATCH })] }),
    );
    expect(errorsOf(result)).toEqual({ 'lines.0.batchId': 'return_batch_not_allowed' });
  });

  it('refuses one challan line twice, on the second line', () => {
    const result = salesReturnInputSchema.safeParse(
      salesReturn({ lines: [returnLine(), returnLine()] }),
    );
    expect(errorsOf(result)).toEqual({ 'lines.1.deliveryLineId': 'return_line_twice' });
  });

  it('refuses one serial number on two lines', () => {
    const result = salesReturnInputSchema.safeParse(
      salesReturn({
        lines: [
          returnLine({ quantity: '1', serialNumbers: ['356938035643809'] }),
          returnLine({ deliveryLineId: '', quantity: '1', serialNumbers: ['356938035643809'] }),
        ],
      }),
    );
    expect(errorsOf(result)).toEqual({ 'lines.1.serialNumbers.0': 'stock_serial_twice' });
  });

  it('marks every mistake at once', () => {
    const result = salesReturnInputSchema.safeParse(
      salesReturn({
        customerId: '',
        warehouseId: '',
        lines: [returnLine({ batchId: BATCH }), returnLine()],
      }),
      { error: contractErrorMap },
    );
    expect(errorsOf(result)).toEqual({
      customerId: 'sales_customer_required',
      warehouseId: 'stock_warehouse_invalid',
      'lines.0.batchId': 'return_batch_not_allowed',
      'lines.1.deliveryLineId': 'return_line_twice',
    });
  });
});

describe('billable quantity', () => {
  it('is what left less what came back before it was billed', () => {
    expect(billableQuantity({ baseQuantity: '48.0000', returnedQuantity: '0.0000' })).toBe(
      '48.0000',
    );
    expect(billableQuantity({ baseQuantity: '48.0000', returnedQuantity: '3.0000' })).toBe(
      '45.0000',
    );
    // All of it came back: nothing left to bill
    expect(billableQuantity({ baseQuantity: '48.0000', returnedQuantity: '48.0000' })).toBe(
      '0.0000',
    );
  });
});
```
