```ts
  );
}

// An invoice line as the API sends it: 2 cases at ৳504 less ৳8, VAT 15% added
function invoiceLine(extra: Partial<InvoiceLine> = {}): InvoiceLine {
  const amounts = lineAmounts(
    { quantity: '2', unitPrice: '504', discountType: 'amount', discount: '8', rate: '15.00' },
    false,
  );
  return {
    id: INVOICE_LINE,
    variantId: '01920000-0000-7000-8000-000000000010',
    productId: '01920000-0000-7000-8000-000000000011',
    productCode: 'P-00001',
    productName: 'Napa 500 mg',
    optionValues: [],
    sku: 'NAPA-500',
    baseUnitId: '01920000-0000-7000-8000-000000000012',
    productType: 'goods',
    tracking: 'batch',
    hasExpiry: true,
    units: [],
    unitId: UNIT,
    quantity: '2.0000',
    baseQuantity: '48.0000',
    description: 'Napa 500 mg',
    unitPrice: '504.0000',
    discountType: 'amount',
    discount: '8.0000',
    taxRate: {
      id: '01920000-0000-7000-8000-000000000013',
      name: 'VAT 15%',
      kind: 'standard',
      rate: '15.00',
    },
    net: amounts.net,
    vat: amounts.vat,
    total: amounts.total,
    deliveryLineId: null,
    orderLineId: null,
    deliveryNumber: null,
    orderNumber: null,
    batchId: null,
    lotNumber: null,
    expiresOn: null,
    serialNumbers: [],
    credited: '0.0000',
    ...extra,
  };
}

describe('credit note input', () => {
  it('takes a line for a return and a price cut on the same invoice line', () => {
    const parsed = creditNoteInputSchema.parse(
      creditNote({
        reason: 'price_adjustment',
        lines: [
          creditLine({ returnLineId: RETURN_LINE }),
          creditLine({ quantity: '48', unitPrice: '2' }),
        ],
      }),
    );
    expect(parsed.lines.map((line) => line.returnLineId)).toEqual([RETURN_LINE, null]);
  });

  it('refuses one return line twice, on the second line', () => {
    const result = creditNoteInputSchema.safeParse(
      creditNote({
        lines: [
          creditLine({ returnLineId: RETURN_LINE }),
          creditLine({ returnLineId: RETURN_LINE }),
        ],
      }),
    );
    expect(errorsOf(result)).toEqual({ 'lines.1.returnLineId': 'credit_note_return_twice' });
  });

  it('never takes back more than the line: the 15b discount rule', () => {
    const result = creditNoteInputSchema.safeParse(
      creditNote({ lines: [creditLine({ discountType: 'amount', discount: '2000' })] }),
    );
    expect(errorsOf(result)).toEqual({ 'lines.0.discount': 'sales_discount_too_large' });
  });

  it('marks every mistake at once', () => {
    const result = creditNoteInputSchema.safeParse(
      creditNote({
        invoiceId: '',
        lines: [
          creditLine({ invoiceLineId: '', returnLineId: RETURN_LINE }),
          creditLine({ returnLineId: RETURN_LINE }),
        ],
      }),
      { error: contractErrorMap },
    );
    expect(errorsOf(result)).toEqual({
      invoiceId: 'credit_note_invoice_required',
      'lines.0.invoiceLineId': 'credit_note_line_invalid',
      'lines.1.returnLineId': 'credit_note_return_twice',
    });
  });
});

describe('credit whole invoice', () => {
  it('gives back exactly what each line charged, to the paisa', () => {
    const line = invoiceLine();
    const [credit] = creditNoteInputSchema.parse(
      creditNote({ lines: wholeInvoiceCreditLines({ lines: [line] }) }),
    ).lines;
    expect(credit).toBeDefined();
    if (!credit) return;
    expect(lineAmounts({ ...credit, rate: line.taxRate.rate }, false)).toMatchObject({
      net: line.net,
      vat: line.vat,
      total: line.total,
    });
  });

  it('is offered only for a posted invoice with no posted credit note', () => {
    expect(canCreditWhole({ status: 'posted', creditNotes: [] })).toBe(true);
    expect(canCreditWhole({ status: 'draft', creditNotes: [] })).toBe(false);
    expect(
      canCreditWhole({
        status: 'posted',
        creditNotes: [
          { id: INVOICE, number: 'CN-2026-27-0001', date: '2026-10-11', total: '100.0000' },
        ],
      }),
    ).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe('the 6-month VAT window', () => {
  it('warns only after six months, counting calendar months', () => {
    expect(creditNoteIsLate('2026-04-11', '2026-10-11')).toBe(false);
    expect(creditNoteIsLate('2026-04-11', '2026-10-12')).toBe(true);
    // 31 August + 6 months is the last day of February
    expect(creditNoteIsLate('2026-08-31', '2027-02-28')).toBe(false);
    expect(creditNoteIsLate('2026-08-31', '2027-03-01')).toBe(true);
  });
});

describe('credit note allocations', () => {
  it('uses its own error codes', () => {
    const result = creditNoteAllocationsInputSchema.safeParse({
      version: 1,
      allocations: [
        { invoiceId: OTHER_INVOICE, amount: '0' },
        { invoiceId: OTHER_INVOICE, amount: '10' },
      ],
    });
    expect(errorsOf(result)).toEqual({
      'allocations.0.amount': 'credit_note_amount_required',
      'allocations.1.invoiceId': 'credit_note_invoice_twice',
    });
  });
});
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import { unappliedOf } from './receipts.js';
import { refundInputSchema } from './refunds.js';

const CUSTOMER = '01920000-0000-7000-8000-000000000001';
const BRANCH = '01920000-0000-7000-8000-000000000002';
const ACCOUNT = '01920000-0000-7000-8000-000000000003';
const RECEIPT = '01920000-0000-7000-8000-000000000004';
const CREDIT_NOTE = '01920000-0000-7000-8000-000000000005';

function refund(extra: object = {}) {
  return {
    customerId: CUSTOMER,
    date: '2026-10-11',
    amount: '5000',
    accountId: ACCOUNT,
    method: 'mobile_wallet',
    reference: 'BKS 9F3K2L1M',
    branchId: BRANCH,
    note: '',
    receiptId: '',
    creditNoteId: CREDIT_NOTE,
    ...extra,
  };
}

// The error codes where the form will show them: field path → code
function errorsOf(result: {
  success: boolean;
  error?: { issues: { path: PropertyKey[]; message: string }[] };
}) {
  return Object.fromEntries(
    (result.error?.issues ?? []).map((issue) => [issue.path.map(String).join('.'), issue.message]),
  );
}

describe('refund input', () => {
  it("pays back a credit note's money or a receipt's", () => {
    expect(refundInputSchema.parse(refund())).toMatchObject({
      receiptId: null,
      creditNoteId: CREDIT_NOTE,
    });
    expect(refundInputSchema.parse(refund({ receiptId: RECEIPT, creditNoteId: '' }))).toMatchObject(
      { receiptId: RECEIPT, creditNoteId: null },
    );
  });

  it('needs exactly one source', () => {
    for (const source of [
      { receiptId: '', creditNoteId: '' },
      { receiptId: RECEIPT, creditNoteId: CREDIT_NOTE },
    ]) {
      expect(errorsOf(refundInputSchema.safeParse(refund(source)))).toEqual({
        receiptId: 'refund_source',
      });
    }
  });

  it('needs an amount above zero, with its own error code', () => {
    for (const amount of ['', '0', '0.00']) {
      expect(errorsOf(refundInputSchema.safeParse(refund({ amount })))).toEqual({
        amount: 'refund_amount_required',
      });
    }
  });
});

describe('unapplied money', () => {
  it('is the amount less what is applied and what refunds paid back', () => {
    expect(
      unappliedOf({ amount: '50000.0000', applied: '30000.0000', refunded: '5000.0000' }),
    ).toBe('15000.0000');
  });
});
```

- **The 15c payment tests now pass `amountCredited`.** A new test checks that a credit counts like a payment, and
  one more line in the overdue test proves an invoice settled by a credit note is not overdue.
- **"Gives back exactly what each line charged".** The fixture is a line with an amount discount and VAT added, the
  case where a paisa could go astray. The credit line built by `wholeInvoiceCreditLines()` is parsed by the real
  schema and worked out by `lineAmounts()`, and must match the invoice line's net, VAT and total. This test is how
  the 4-decimal discount problem above was found: the first version copied `8.0000` into a box that takes 2
  decimals.
- **The 6-month window on 31 August.** The test that pins the calendar-month rule: 28 February is still inside, 1
  March is not.
- **"Marks every mistake at once"**, in each document's spec, as in 15c: Zod 4 runs the document's rules even when a
  field failed, so the form marks everything on the first save.
- **The refund's source** is tested both ways that are wrong (neither, both), with the error on one box.

### Check this part

```bash
pnpm --filter @omnivo/contracts typecheck
pnpm --filter @omnivo/contracts test          # 159 tests, 20 new
pnpm lint
```

`pnpm typecheck` for the whole repo **fails** after this part, and that is expected. The next parts fix it:
`packages/db` needs a description for each new permission (15d.2), the API must send the new fields
(`returnState`, `returnedQuantity`, `amountCredited`, `credited`, `refunded`) and use the new enum values
(15d.3), `packages/i18n` needs the new error codes and labels (15d.5), and the app's pills, pages and mocks need the
new fields (15d.6, 15d.7).

## 15d.2 — `packages/db`: returns, credit notes, refunds and the rules on them

The contract has returns, credit notes and refunds; this part gives them six tables. Three new schema files mirror
the contract: `sales-returns.ts` (returns and their lines), `credit-notes.ts` (credit notes, their lines and the
allocations that apply their money) and `refunds.ts`. Some 15b and 15c tables get a column each: a challan line
learns how much came back, an invoice and its lines learn how much was credited, a receipt learns how much was paid
back. The settings row gets the sales returns account, the journal's document check learns the three new sources,
and the permission catalog describes the three new permissions. Migration 0031 is generated from the schema; 0032
is written by hand: row-level security, the triggers that decide what may change when, the two triggers that keep
the money sums, and the returns account for workspaces that already exist.

One rule runs through this part, the same as in 15b and 15c: **a number that only a posting changes is written by
the API, and a number that several actions change is kept by a trigger.** `returned_quantity`, `credited` and
`credit_note_total` change in one place only (a posting, which is never undone), like 15b's `delivered_quantity`.
`amount_credited`, `applied` and `refunded` change when a credit note is posted, applied again, or paid back, and
when a refund is voided, like 15c's `amount_paid`. Either way, a check constraint on the column is the last word.

### `schema/sales-documents.ts`: what a return writes on a challan line

- **`returned_quantity` in the base unit**, like `delivered_quantity`. The return form shows "45 can still come
  back" from it, and the invoice bills `base_quantity − returned_quantity` (`billableQuantity()`, 15d.1). It is a
  stored sum because the cap check needs it under a lock: two people returning the last carton of one line at the
  same moment must not both succeed (see 0032 and "What we checked").
- **`delivery_lines_returned_check`.** Between 0 and what left on the line. The API answers
  `return_over_delivered` first, with the line; this check is the one that still holds when two returns are posted
  at once.
- **`delivery_lines_to_invoice_idx` drops a line that all came back.** Such a line has nothing to bill, so the
  invoice form's challan picker must not offer it. The index is still partial and small. A partial index may compare
  two columns of its row, as 15c's open-invoice indexes do.
- **No index for "returnable".** The return form's picker (`return=returnable`) lists challan lines that did not
  all come back. That is almost every line, so a partial index would be nearly as big as the table and save nothing.
  The picker always filters by customer first, which `deliveries_customer_idx` already serves.

- **`amount_credited` next to `amount_paid`.** You chose that a credit note's money settles its invoice first. So
  "what is still due" is `total − amount_paid − amount_credited`, the contract's `amountDueOf()`. It is kept by the
  allocations' trigger (0032, section 5), exactly like `amount_paid`, because it changes on several paths: posting
  the credit note, applying its money again, moving it to another invoice.
- **`credit_note_total` is a different number.** It is what posted credit notes took back from this invoice,
  wherever their money went. A credit note for an invoice that was already paid credits it in full, but its money
  becomes an advance: `amount_credited` stays 0 and `credit_note_total` grows. The "Credited" pill reads this one.
  It is stored because the invoice list shows the pill on every row, and a sum per row would cost a join for each.
- **`credited` on each invoice line, in money.** What posted credit note lines took back from that line. The money
  cap of 15d.1 ("never more than the line charged") is checked against it. A price cut on all 100 pieces and a
  later return of 10 pieces both fit, up to what the line billed.
- **Who writes `credit_note_total` and `credited`.** The credit note's posting, under a lock on the invoice, and
  nothing else: a credit note is never undone, so these only grow. The guards in 0032 refuse any other change.
- **`invoices_paid_check` now counts both.** Receipts and credit notes together never settle more than the total,
  and a draft is never settled. This is the last word on `receipt_over_invoice` and `credit_note_over_invoice`, and
  the one that holds when a receipt and a credit note settle the same invoice at the same moment. We tried exactly
  that (see "What we checked").
- **`invoices_credited_check`.** Credit notes never take back more than the total, and a draft invoice has none.
  The second half means a credit note for a draft invoice can never be posted, whatever the API checked.
- **`invoice_lines_credited_check`** is the last word on `credit_note_over_line`.
- **The open indexes count both too.** An invoice settled by a credit note leaves the receipt form's list and the
  overdue list, like a paid one. That is the point of `isOverdue()` taking `amountCredited` (15d.1): nobody chases a
  customer for money the company gave back.
- **`invoice_lines_invoice_id_idx` (tenant, invoice, id) is unique.** It adds no rule of its own; it is the target
  of the credit note line's FK and the return line's FK, which include the invoice. See below for why.

```diff
@@ -78,16 +84,17 @@ export const receipts = pgTable(
       columns: [table.tenantId, table.branchId],
       foreignColumns: [branches.tenantId, branches.id],
     }),
-    // A receipt of ৳0 moved no money, and its money is never applied twice over
+    // A receipt of ৳0 moved no money, and its money is never used twice over: applied to
+    // invoices and paid back together, never more than came in
     check(
       'receipts_amount_check',
-      sql`${table.amount} > 0 AND ${table.applied} >= 0 AND ${table.applied} <= ${table.amount}`,
+      sql`${table.amount} > 0 AND ${table.applied} >= 0 AND ${table.refunded} >= 0 AND ${table.applied} + ${table.refunded} <= ${table.amount}`,
     ),
-    // Voided ⇔ a void date and a reason. A voided receipt paid nothing: its allocations are
-    // removed before it is voided.
+    // Voided ⇔ a void date and a reason. A voided receipt paid nothing and paid nothing back: its
+    // allocations are removed before it is voided, and its refunds voided (receipt_has_refunds).
     check(
       'receipts_void_check',
-      sql`(${table.status} = 'voided') = (${table.voidDate} IS NOT NULL AND ${table.voidReason} IS NOT NULL) AND (${table.status} = 'posted' OR ${table.applied} = 0) AND (${table.voidDate} IS NULL OR ${table.voidDate} >= ${table.date})`,
+      sql`(${table.status} = 'voided') = (${table.voidDate} IS NOT NULL AND ${table.voidReason} IS NOT NULL) AND (${table.status} = 'posted' OR (${table.applied} = 0 AND ${table.refunded} = 0)) AND (${table.voidDate} IS NULL OR ${table.voidDate} >= ${table.date})`,
     ),
   ],
 );
```

- **`refunded`, kept by the refunds' trigger** (0032, section 6). A receipt's money now goes three ways: applied to
  invoices, paid back, or not used yet. `amount − applied − refunded` is what is left (`unappliedOf()`, 15d.1).
- **`receipts_amount_check`: applied and paid back together, never more than came in.** The last word on
  `receipt_over_allocated` (applying money that was paid back) and `refund_over_source` (paying back money that is
  applied).
- **`receipts_void_check`: a voided receipt paid nothing back.** This is `receipt_has_refunds` in the database. If
  a cheque bounced after part of it was refunded, voiding the receipt alone would leave a refund of money that never
  came in. The refund is voided first, and only then the receipt.
- **`receipts_unapplied_idx`** now leaves out a receipt whose money was all paid back. The refund form uses the same
  list to offer what can be paid back.

### `schema/sales-returns.ts` (new): the return

```ts
import { RETURN_REASONS, STOCK_DOCUMENT_STATUSES } from '@omnivo/contracts';
import { sql } from 'drizzle-orm';
import {
  check,
  date,
  foreignKey,
  index,
  numeric,
  pgTable,
  text,
  timestamp,
  uniqueIndex,
  uuid,
} from 'drizzle-orm/pg-core';
import { baseColumns } from '../base-columns.js';
import { batches } from './batches.js';
import { invoiceLines } from './invoices.js';
import { parties } from './parties.js';
import { productVariants } from './products.js';
import { deliveryLines } from './sales-documents.js';
import { stockLineColumns } from './stock-documents.js';
import { tenants } from './tenants.js';
import { units } from './units.js';
import { warehouses } from './warehouses.js';

// Step 15d: sales returns, goods a customer sent back. Shaped like a delivery: a draft is changed
// freely; posting numbers it, puts the stock back and books its cost back. From then on only what
// credit notes gave back for its lines (credited_quantity) moves. The rules live in migration 0032.

export const salesReturns = pgTable(
  'sales_returns',
  {
    // deleted_at is not used: a draft is deleted for real, a posted return never
    ...baseColumns(),
    tenantId: uuid('tenant_id')
      .notNull()
      .references(() => tenants.id),
    // Given when posted ('sales.return'), so posted numbers have no gaps
    number: text('number'),
    date: date('date', { mode: 'string' }).notNull(),
    customerId: uuid('customer_id').notNull(),
    // Where every line comes back into (a "Damage/Expiry" warehouse, often)
    warehouseId: uuid('warehouse_id').notNull(),
    // Decides nothing in the books: the list and the reports show it
    reason: text('reason', { enum: RETURN_REASONS }).notNull(),
    note: text('note'),
    status: text('status', { enum: STOCK_DOCUMENT_STATUSES }).notNull().default('draft'),
    postedAt: timestamp('posted_at', { withTimezone: true }),
    postedBy: uuid('posted_by'),
  },
  (table) => [
    uniqueIndex('sales_returns_tenant_id_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.id),
    uniqueIndex('sales_returns_tenant_number_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.number),
    // The list: newest date first, keyset on (date, id)
    index('sales_returns_tenant_date_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.date, table.id),
    // One customer's returns (the list's filter), and the customer FK's check on delete
    index('sales_returns_customer_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.customerId, table.date, table.id),
    // The list's warehouse filter
    index('sales_returns_warehouse_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.warehouseId),
    // No ON DELETE: a customer with a return cannot be deleted (customer_in_use)
    foreignKey({
      name: 'sales_returns_customer_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.customerId],
      foreignColumns: [parties.tenantId, parties.id],
    }),
    foreignKey({
      name: 'sales_returns_warehouse_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.warehouseId],
      foreignColumns: [warehouses.tenantId, warehouses.id],
    }),
    // Posted ⇔ a number and a posting time, like a delivery
    check(
      'sales_returns_posted_check',
      sql`(${table.status} = 'posted') = (${table.number} IS NOT NULL AND ${table.postedAt} IS NOT NULL)`,
    ),
  ],
);
```

- **Shaped like a delivery.** A draft has no number; posting gives it one (SR-2026-27-0001), and
  `sales_returns_posted_check` says posted ⇔ a number and a posting time. Posted numbers have no gaps.
- **One `warehouse_id` for the whole return.** You chose that everything goes back into one warehouse the person
  picks. The stock movements of all lines go there.
- **`reason` decides nothing in the books.** It is a column, not a free text, so a report can count "how much came
  back as expired this year" (15d.1).
- **`sales_returns_warehouse_idx`.** The return list filters by warehouse (the store keeper of the Damage warehouse
  looks at what came in). Warehouses are archived, never deleted, so the index is for the list, not for the FK.
- **No `entry_id`.** Like a delivery's, the return's journal entry points at the return (`document_id`, source
  `sales_return`), and `journal_entries_document_idx` finds it.

### The return's lines

```ts
export const salesReturnLines = pgTable(
  'sales_return_lines',
  {
    ...stockLineColumns(),
    returnId: uuid('return_id').notNull(),
    // The challan line the goods left on; NULL for a line on its own (goods that left before the
    // workspace used Omnivo)
    deliveryLineId: uuid('delivery_line_id'),
    // The invoice line that had billed that challan line when the return was posted, and its
    // invoice. Set by the posting and never again: NULL = not billed then (the invoice bills less
    // instead), and always NULL on a draft and on a line on its own. The contract's `billed`.
    invoiceId: uuid('invoice_id'),
    invoiceLineId: uuid('invoice_line_id'),
    // What the goods came back at (step 14's value): the challan line's cost, or the average cost
    // for a line on its own. NULL while a draft.
    value: numeric('value', { precision: 19, scale: 4 }),
    // In the base unit: what posted credit note lines gave back for this line. Written by the
    // credit note's posting; it only grows (migration 0032).
    creditedQuantity: numeric('credited_quantity', { precision: 19, scale: 4 })
      .notNull()
      .default('0'),
  },
  (table) => [
    uniqueIndex('sales_return_lines_line_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.returnId, table.lineNo),
    // The target of the credit note line's FK: a return line that THIS invoice line billed
    uniqueIndex('sales_return_lines_invoice_line_id_idx').on(
      table.tenantId,
      table.invoiceLineId,
      table.id,
    ),
    index('sales_return_lines_variant_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.productId, table.variantId),
    // A challan's returns (its page), the sum already returned before posting, and the FK's check
    index('sales_return_lines_delivery_line_idx')
      .on(table.tenantId, table.deliveryLineId)
      .where(sql`${table.deliveryLineId} IS NOT NULL`),
    foreignKey({
      name: 'sales_return_lines_return_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.returnId],
      foreignColumns: [salesReturns.tenantId, salesReturns.id],
    }).onDelete('cascade'),
    // No ON DELETE on the next two: a posted challan's lines and a posted invoice's lines are
    // never deleted anyway
    foreignKey({
      name: 'sales_return_lines_delivery_line_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.deliveryLineId],
      foreignColumns: [deliveryLines.tenantId, deliveryLines.id],
    }),
    // invoice_id is in the key: the invoice line is a line of that invoice
    foreignKey({
      name: 'sales_return_lines_invoice_line_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.invoiceId, table.invoiceLineId],
      foreignColumns: [invoiceLines.tenantId, invoiceLines.invoiceId, invoiceLines.id],
    }),
    foreignKey({
      name: 'sales_return_lines_variant_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.productId, table.variantId],
      foreignColumns: [productVariants.tenantId, productVariants.productId, productVariants.id],
    }),
    foreignKey({
      name: 'sales_return_lines_unit_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.unitId],
      foreignColumns: [units.tenantId, units.id],
    }),
    foreignKey({
      name: 'sales_return_lines_batch_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.variantId, table.batchId],
      foreignColumns: [batches.tenantId, batches.variantId, batches.id],
    }),
    check(
      'sales_return_lines_quantity_check',
      sql`${table.quantity} > 0 AND ${table.factor} > 0 AND ${table.baseQuantity} > 0`,
    ),
    check('sales_return_lines_value_check', sql`${table.value} IS NULL OR ${table.value} >= 0`),
    // Billed only through a challan line, and the invoice and its line come together
    check(
      'sales_return_lines_billed_check',
      sql`(${table.invoiceId} IS NULL) = (${table.invoiceLineId} IS NULL) AND (${table.invoiceLineId} IS NULL OR ${table.deliveryLineId} IS NOT NULL)`,
    ),
    // Never credited past what came back, and only a billed line is credited at all: the last
    // word on credit_note_over_return
    check(
      'sales_return_lines_credited_check',
      sql`${table.creditedQuantity} BETWEEN 0 AND ${table.baseQuantity} AND (${table.invoiceLineId} IS NOT NULL OR ${table.creditedQuantity} = 0)`,
    ),
  ],
);
```

- **`stockLineColumns()`**, like a challan line: the item, the unit, the quantity in that unit and in the base unit,
  the batch and the serial numbers. A return is a stock document.
- **`delivery_line_id` is optional.** A line from a challan points at it; a line on its own (goods that left before
  the workspace used Omnivo) does not. The FK has no `ON DELETE`: a posted challan's lines are never deleted anyway,
  and the API only accepts lines of posted challans (`return_delivery_line_invalid`).
- **`invoice_id` and `invoice_line_id` instead of a `billed` flag.** The contract's `billed` answers "had a posted
  invoice billed this challan line when the return was posted?". Storing the invoice line that billed it answers the
  same question (`invoice_line_id IS NOT NULL`) and also tells the credit note which line to credit. Two columns that
  could disagree (a flag and an id) would be one too many. Both are set by the posting, never later: a challan line
  that is billed tomorrow does not change what this return meant today.
- **`sales_return_lines_billed_check`.** The invoice and its line come together, and only a line from a challan can
  have been billed.
- **`invoice_id` is in the invoice line FK.** `(tenant, invoice_id, invoice_line_id)` points at
  `invoice_lines (tenant, invoice_id, id)`, so the stored invoice is the line's own invoice. Without it, a bug could
  store a line of INV-7 with the id of INV-8, and the return page would link to the wrong invoice.
- **`value`**, set by the posting: the challan line's cost for a line from a challan (you chose this), the average
  cost for a line on its own. The same column and the same `NULL` while a draft as on a challan line.
- **`credited_quantity` in the base unit**, written by a credit note's posting. The return page's "Make credit
  note" button offers only what is not credited yet, and the cap `credit_note_over_return` is checked against it.
  `sales_return_lines_credited_check` is the last word: never more than came back, and nothing at all on a line that
  was not billed (there is nothing to give back for it).
- **`sales_return_lines_invoice_line_id_idx` (tenant, invoice line, id) is unique.** It is the target of the credit
  note line's return FK, below. It is a full index, not a partial one, because Postgres only accepts a full unique
  index as the target of a foreign key.
- **`sales_return_lines_delivery_line_idx`.** "Which returns brought back goods from this challan?" (the challan
  page's `returns`), the sum of what came back before, and Postgres's own check of the FK.

### `schema/credit-notes.ts` (new): the credit note

```ts
import { CREDIT_NOTE_REASONS, CREDIT_NOTE_STATUSES } from '@omnivo/contracts';
import { sql } from 'drizzle-orm';
import {
  check,
  date,
  foreignKey,
  index,
  numeric,
  pgTable,
  text,
  timestamp,
  uniqueIndex,
  uuid,
} from 'drizzle-orm/pg-core';
import { baseColumns } from '../base-columns.js';
import { invoiceLines, invoices } from './invoices.js';
import { parties } from './parties.js';
import { productVariants } from './products.js';
import { salesLineColumns, totalColumns } from './sales-documents.js';
import { salesReturnLines } from './sales-returns.js';
import { taxRates } from './tax-rates.js';
import { tenants } from './tenants.js';
import { units } from './units.js';

// Step 15d: credit notes, and the invoices their money is applied to. A credit note is always for
// one posted invoice. A draft is changed freely; posting numbers it and books the sale back. From
// then on only its allocations (applied) and the refunds paid out of it (refunded) move; it is
// never voided. The rules live in migration 0032.

export const creditNotes = pgTable(
  'credit_notes',
  {
    // deleted_at is not used: a draft is deleted for real, a posted credit note never
    ...baseColumns(),
    tenantId: uuid('tenant_id')
      .notNull()
      .references(() => tenants.id),
    // Given when posted ('sales.credit_note'), so posted numbers have no gaps
    number: text('number'),
    date: date('date', { mode: 'string' }).notNull(),
    // The invoice's customer: it is in the invoice FK, so the two can never disagree
    customerId: uuid('customer_id').notNull(),
    // The invoice it credits. Its branch and its prices_include_vat are read from it, not copied:
    // a posted invoice never changes.
    invoiceId: uuid('invoice_id').notNull(),
    reason: text('reason', { enum: CREDIT_NOTE_REASONS }).notNull(),
    status: text('status', { enum: CREDIT_NOTE_STATUSES }).notNull().default('draft'),
    note: text('note'),
    ...totalColumns(),
    // The sum of its allocations, kept by their trigger (migration 0032) like receipts.applied
    applied: numeric('applied', { precision: 19, scale: 4 }).notNull().default('0'),
    // What posted refunds paid back out of it, kept by the refunds' trigger (migration 0032).
    // total − applied − refunded is the customer's advance that is left (contracts' unappliedOf).
    refunded: numeric('refunded', { precision: 19, scale: 4 }).notNull().default('0'),
    postedAt: timestamp('posted_at', { withTimezone: true }),
    postedBy: uuid('posted_by'),
  },
  (table) => [
    uniqueIndex('credit_notes_tenant_id_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.id),
    // The target of the allocation's and the refund's FKs: a credit note of THIS customer
    uniqueIndex('credit_notes_customer_id_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.customerId, table.id),
    // The target of the line's FK: a credit note of THIS invoice. Also an invoice's credit notes
    // (its page), and the invoice FK's check.
    uniqueIndex('credit_notes_invoice_id_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.invoiceId, table.id),
    uniqueIndex('credit_notes_tenant_number_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.number),
    // The list: newest date first, keyset on (date, id)
    index('credit_notes_tenant_date_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.date, table.id),
    // One customer's credit notes (the list's filter), and the customer FK's check on delete
    index('credit_notes_customer_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.customerId, table.date, table.id),
    // A customer's credit that is not used yet (advances), like receipts_unapplied_idx
    index('credit_notes_unapplied_idx')
      .on(table.tenantId, table.customerId, table.date, table.id)
      .where(
        sql`${table.status} = 'posted' AND ${table.applied} + ${table.refunded} < ${table.total}`,
      ),
    // No ON DELETE: a customer with a credit note cannot be deleted (customer_in_use)
    foreignKey({
      name: 'credit_notes_customer_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.customerId],
      foreignColumns: [parties.tenantId, parties.id],
    }),
    // customer_id is in both keys: a credit note's invoice is an invoice of the same customer
    foreignKey({
      name: 'credit_notes_invoice_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.customerId, table.invoiceId],
      foreignColumns: [invoices.tenantId, invoices.customerId, invoices.id],
    }),
    // Posted ⇔ a number and a posting time, like an invoice
    check(
      'credit_notes_posted_check',
      sql`(${table.status} = 'posted') = (${table.number} IS NOT NULL AND ${table.postedAt} IS NOT NULL)`,
    ),
    check(
      'credit_notes_totals_check',
      sql`${table.discount} >= 0 AND ${table.net} >= 0 AND ${table.vat} >= 0 AND ${table.total} = ${table.net} + ${table.vat}`,
    ),
    // Its money is never used twice over (applied and paid back together, never more than the
    // total), and a draft has no money to use: the last word on credit_note_over_allocated,
    // credit_note_not_posted and refund_over_source
    check(
      'credit_notes_money_check',
      sql`${table.applied} >= 0 AND ${table.refunded} >= 0 AND ${table.applied} + ${table.refunded} <= ${table.total} AND (${table.status} = 'posted' OR (${table.applied} = 0 AND ${table.refunded} = 0))`,
    ),
  ],
);
```

- **Always for one invoice.** `invoice_id` is `NOT NULL`, and the FK `(tenant, customer_id, invoice_id)` points at
  `invoices_customer_id_idx` from 15c. So the credit note's customer is always the invoice's customer: a credit note
  of Lazz Pharma cannot credit an invoice of Tamanna Pharmacy, whatever the API sends. This is the trick of 15b's
  `deliveries_order_fk` again.
- **No `branch_id` and no `prices_include_vat`.** The contract sends both, and both are the invoice's. A posted
  invoice never changes, so the API reads them from it. Copying them would add two columns that could only ever
  disagree with the invoice by mistake. The customer is the one exception: it must be on the row, because two FKs
  use it.
- **`totalColumns()`**, like an invoice: the sums of the lines, worked out by the same contract functions.
- **`applied` and `refunded`**, the receipt's two columns with the same meaning, kept by the same kind of trigger.
  A credit note's money is used like a receipt's: applied to invoices, paid back, or left as an advance.
- **`credit_notes_money_check`.** Three rules in one: nothing negative; applied and paid back together never more
  than the total; a draft has no money to use. The last one is the database's `credit_note_not_posted`: applying or
  refunding a draft's money fails here even if the API forgot to check.
- **Three unique indexes on (tenant, …, id).** `credit_notes_tenant_id_idx` is the usual one.
  `credit_notes_customer_id_idx` is the target of the allocation's and the refund's FKs (both include the customer),
  like the receipt's. `credit_notes_invoice_id_idx` is the target of the line's FK (it includes the invoice) and
  also answers "this invoice's credit notes" for the invoice page.
- **`credit_notes_unapplied_idx`**, like `receipts_unapplied_idx`: a customer's credit that is not used yet. The
  receipt and refund forms offer it.

### The credit note's lines

```ts
export const creditNoteLines = pgTable(
  'credit_note_lines',
  {
    // The item, the unit and the VAT snapshot are the invoice line's, copied by the API
    ...salesLineColumns(),
    creditNoteId: uuid('credit_note_id').notNull(),
    // The credit note's invoice, again: it is in both FKs below
    invoiceId: uuid('invoice_id').notNull(),
    // The invoice line it credits
    invoiceLineId: uuid('invoice_line_id').notNull(),
    // The return line it gives the money back for; NULL for a price cut or a billing mistake
    returnLineId: uuid('return_line_id'),
  },
  (table) => [
    uniqueIndex('credit_note_lines_line_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.creditNoteId, table.lineNo),
    index('credit_note_lines_variant_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.productId, table.variantId),
    // The invoice line FK's check when a draft invoice's lines are replaced
    index('credit_note_lines_invoice_line_idx').on(
      table.tenantId,
      table.invoiceId,
      table.invoiceLineId,
    ),
    // A return's credit notes (its page), and the return line FK's check
    index('credit_note_lines_return_line_idx')
      .on(table.tenantId, table.returnLineId)
      .where(sql`${table.returnLineId} IS NOT NULL`),
    // invoice_id is in the key of all three: the line belongs to a credit note of that invoice,
    // credits a line of that invoice, and names a return line that line billed
    foreignKey({
      name: 'credit_note_lines_credit_note_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.invoiceId, table.creditNoteId],
      foreignColumns: [creditNotes.tenantId, creditNotes.invoiceId, creditNotes.id],
    }).onDelete('cascade'),
    foreignKey({
      name: 'credit_note_lines_invoice_line_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.invoiceId, table.invoiceLineId],
      foreignColumns: [invoiceLines.tenantId, invoiceLines.invoiceId, invoiceLines.id],
    }),
    foreignKey({
      name: 'credit_note_lines_return_line_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.invoiceLineId, table.returnLineId],
      foreignColumns: [
        salesReturnLines.tenantId,
        salesReturnLines.invoiceLineId,
        salesReturnLines.id,
      ],
    }),
    foreignKey({
      name: 'credit_note_lines_variant_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.productId, table.variantId],
      foreignColumns: [productVariants.tenantId, productVariants.productId, productVariants.id],
    }),
    foreignKey({
      name: 'credit_note_lines_unit_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.unitId],
      foreignColumns: [units.tenantId, units.id],
    }),
    foreignKey({
      name: 'credit_note_lines_tax_rate_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.taxRateId],
      foreignColumns: [taxRates.tenantId, taxRates.id],
    }),
    check(
      'credit_note_lines_quantity_check',
      sql`${table.quantity} > 0 AND ${table.factor} > 0 AND ${table.baseQuantity} > 0`,
    ),
    check(
      'credit_note_lines_amounts_check',
      sql`${table.unitPrice} >= 0 AND ${table.discount} >= 0 AND (${table.discountType} = 'amount' OR ${table.discount} <= 100) AND ${table.net} >= 0 AND ${table.vat} >= 0 AND ${table.total} = ${table.net} + ${table.vat}`,
    ),
    check(
      'credit_note_lines_tax_rate_check',
      sql`${table.taxRate} >= 0 AND ${table.taxRate} < 100`,
    ),
  ],
);
```

- **`salesLineColumns()`**, like an invoice line. The item, the unit and the VAT snapshot are the invoice line's,
  copied by the API (15d.1: the form sends no item and no VAT rate). With the same columns, `lineAmounts()` works the
  line out the same way, and the print shows it the same way.
- **`invoice_id` on the line, in all three FKs.** This is the heart of the table:
  - the header FK `(tenant, invoice_id, credit_note_id)` → `credit_notes (tenant, invoice_id, id)`: the line's
    `invoice_id` is its credit note's invoice;
  - the invoice line FK `(tenant, invoice_id, invoice_line_id)` → `invoice_lines (tenant, invoice_id, id)`: the line
    credits a line of that invoice;
  - the return line FK `(tenant, invoice_line_id, return_line_id)` → `sales_return_lines (tenant, invoice_line_id,
    id)`: the return line was billed by exactly this invoice line.

  Together they make `credit_note_line_invalid` and `credit_note_return_invalid` impossible to store. A credit line
  cannot take VAT back from another invoice's line, and cannot give money back for goods that were never billed
  (an unbilled return line has `invoice_line_id` `NULL`, so nothing matches). We tried each one (see "What we
  checked").
- **`ON DELETE CASCADE` on the header FK only.** A draft credit note is deleted with its lines. The other FKs have no
  `ON DELETE`: a posted invoice's lines and a posted return's lines are never deleted.
- **`credit_note_lines_invoice_line_idx`.** A draft invoice's lines are replaced when it is saved. Without this
  index, each of those deletes would read the whole credit note lines table to check the FK.
- **`credit_note_lines_return_line_idx`** is partial: most credit lines are price cuts with no return line. It answers
  "this return's credit notes" for the return page.
- **No `credited` column here.** What a line gave back is its `total`. The invoice line and the return line keep the
  running sums (`credited`, `credited_quantity`), because that is where the caps are checked.

### The credit note's allocations

```ts
// The money of one credit note put on one invoice, like a receipt's allocation (receipts.ts).
// Posting puts it on its own invoice first; changing how it is applied replaces its rows.
export const creditNoteAllocations = pgTable(
  'credit_note_allocations',
  {
    id: baseColumns().id,
    tenantId: uuid('tenant_id')
      .notNull()
      .references(() => tenants.id),
    creditNoteId: uuid('credit_note_id').notNull(),
    // The customer of both: it is in both FKs, so a credit note settles only its own customer's
    // invoices
    customerId: uuid('customer_id').notNull(),
    invoiceId: uuid('invoice_id').notNull(),
    amount: numeric('amount', { precision: 19, scale: 4 }).notNull(),
  },
  (table) => [
    uniqueIndex('credit_note_allocations_pair_idx').on(
      table.tenantId,
      table.creditNoteId,
      table.invoiceId,
    ),
    // An invoice's credits (its page), and the invoice FK's check
    index('credit_note_allocations_invoice_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.invoiceId),
    foreignKey({
      name: 'credit_note_allocations_credit_note_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.customerId, table.creditNoteId],
      foreignColumns: [creditNotes.tenantId, creditNotes.customerId, creditNotes.id],
    }),
    foreignKey({
      name: 'credit_note_allocations_invoice_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.customerId, table.invoiceId],
      foreignColumns: [invoices.tenantId, invoices.customerId, invoices.id],
    }),
    check('credit_note_allocations_amount_check', sql`${table.amount} > 0`),
  ],
);
```

- **`receipt_allocations` with the credit note's names.** The same columns, the same customer-in-both-FKs trick, the
  same unique pair, the same index for the invoice page. Posting puts the money on its own invoice (up to what is
  due); `PUT /credit-notes/:id/allocations` replaces the rows, like a receipt's.
- **A separate table, not a `source` column on `receipt_allocations`.** One table with two kinds of source would need
  two nullable FKs and a check that exactly one is set, and every query on receipts would have to filter the credit
  notes out. Two small tables keep each FK simple, and the invoice page reads both with two indexed queries.

### `schema/refunds.ts` (new): the refund

```ts
import { PAYMENT_METHODS, REFUND_STATUSES } from '@omnivo/contracts';
import { sql } from 'drizzle-orm';
import {
  check,
  date,
  foreignKey,
  index,
  numeric,
  pgTable,
  text,
  uniqueIndex,
  uuid,
} from 'drizzle-orm/pg-core';
import { baseColumns } from '../base-columns.js';
import { branches } from './branches.js';
import { creditNotes } from './credit-notes.js';
import { ledgerAccounts } from './ledger-accounts.js';
import { parties } from './parties.js';
import { receipts } from './receipts.js';
import { tenants } from './tenants.js';

// Step 15d: refunds, money paid back to a customer out of a cash, bank or wallet account. Like a
// money receipt, saving posts it, and a mistake is voided; it never changes otherwise. Its amount
// is added to its source's `refunded` by a trigger (migration 0032).

export const refunds = pgTable(
  'refunds',
  {
    // deleted_at is not used: a refund is never deleted, a mistake is voided
    ...baseColumns(),
    tenantId: uuid('tenant_id')
      .notNull()
      .references(() => tenants.id),
    // Given when it is saved ('sales.refund'): saved means posted
    number: text('number').notNull(),
    date: date('date', { mode: 'string' }).notNull(),
    customerId: uuid('customer_id').notNull(),
    amount: numeric('amount', { precision: 19, scale: 4 }).notNull(),
    // The money account it was paid out of (the API checks it holds money, like a receipt's)
    accountId: uuid('account_id').notNull(),
    method: text('method', { enum: PAYMENT_METHODS }).notNull(),
    reference: text('reference'),
    branchId: uuid('branch_id').notNull(),
    note: text('note'),
    // Where the money it pays back came from: exactly one of the two
    receiptId: uuid('receipt_id'),
    creditNoteId: uuid('credit_note_id'),
    status: text('status', { enum: REFUND_STATUSES }).notNull().default('posted'),
    // Set when voided, like a receipt's
    voidDate: date('void_date', { mode: 'string' }),
    voidReason: text('void_reason'),
  },
  (table) => [
    uniqueIndex('refunds_tenant_id_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.id),
    uniqueIndex('refunds_tenant_number_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.number),
    index('refunds_tenant_date_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.date, table.id),
    index('refunds_customer_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.customerId, table.date, table.id),
    // The account FK's check when an account is deleted, like receipts_account_idx
    index('refunds_account_idx').on(table.tenantId, table.accountId),
    // A receipt's refunds and a credit note's (their pages; receipt_has_refunds)
    index('refunds_receipt_idx')
      .on(table.tenantId, table.receiptId)
      .where(sql`${table.receiptId} IS NOT NULL`),
    index('refunds_credit_note_idx')
      .on(table.tenantId, table.creditNoteId)
      .where(sql`${table.creditNoteId} IS NOT NULL`),
    // No ON DELETE: a customer with a refund cannot be deleted (customer_in_use)
    foreignKey({
      name: 'refunds_customer_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.customerId],
      foreignColumns: [parties.tenantId, parties.id],
    }),
    // customer_id is in both keys: a refund pays back only its own customer's money
    foreignKey({
      name: 'refunds_receipt_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.customerId, table.receiptId],
      foreignColumns: [receipts.tenantId, receipts.customerId, receipts.id],
    }),
    foreignKey({
      name: 'refunds_credit_note_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.customerId, table.creditNoteId],
      foreignColumns: [creditNotes.tenantId, creditNotes.customerId, creditNotes.id],
    }),
    foreignKey({
      name: 'refunds_account_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.accountId],
      foreignColumns: [ledgerAccounts.tenantId, ledgerAccounts.id],
    }),
    foreignKey({
      name: 'refunds_branch_fk',
      columns: [table.tenantId, table.branchId],
      foreignColumns: [branches.tenantId, branches.id],
    }),
    check('refunds_amount_check', sql`${table.amount} > 0`),
    // Exactly one source: the last word on refund_source
    check(
      'refunds_source_check',
      sql`(${table.receiptId} IS NULL) <> (${table.creditNoteId} IS NULL)`,
    ),
    // Voided ⇔ a void date and a reason, not before its own date, like a receipt
    check(
      'refunds_void_check',
      sql`(${table.status} = 'voided') = (${table.voidDate} IS NOT NULL AND ${table.voidReason} IS NOT NULL) AND (${table.voidDate} IS NULL OR ${table.voidDate} >= ${table.date})`,
    ),
  ],
);
```

- **A money receipt the other way round.** The same columns (number given when saved, the money account, the
  method and reference, the branch) and the same void columns and rules. `number` is `NOT NULL`: saved means posted.
- **`receipt_id` or `credit_note_id`, exactly one.** `refunds_source_check` is the database's `refund_source`. Two
  nullable columns with their own FKs, not one "source id" column: a foreign key can only point at one table.
- **The customer is in both source FKs.** `(tenant, customer_id, receipt_id)` points at `receipts_customer_id_idx`,
  `(tenant, customer_id, credit_note_id)` at `credit_notes_customer_id_idx`. A refund can only pay back its own
  customer's money.
- **No `refunded` check here.** How much is left to pay back is a rule about the source, so it lives on the source:
  `receipts_amount_check` and `credit_notes_money_check`. The trigger in 0032 adds the refund to its source in the
  same statement, and the source's check decides.
- **`refunds_account_idx`**, for the same reason as `receipts_account_idx`: an unused account can be deleted, and
  this FK's check must not read the whole table.
- **`refunds_receipt_idx`, `refunds_credit_note_idx`.** "This receipt's refunds" and "this credit note's refunds" for
  their pages, and the FK checks. Partial, because each refund has only one of the two.

- **The three new sources join the document check.** A return's, a credit note's and a refund's entry point at
  their document. The list is the contract's `DOCUMENT_JOURNAL_SOURCES`; a check constraint cannot import it, so
  the comment says where it comes from. Adding the constraint again checks every entry, which passes: no entry has
  a new source yet.

  `document_type` on `number_series` are `text` with a TypeScript enum only (Drizzle writes no check for
  `text(…, { enum })`). The contract's new values reach them through the types.

### Migration 0031 (generated — then move the indexes up)

Run `pnpm --filter @omnivo/db generate --name returns-credit-notes`. As in every step since 9, `drizzle-kit` writes
the foreign keys before the unique indexes they point at (`invoice_lines_invoice_id_idx`,
`sales_return_lines_invoice_line_id_idx`, `credit_notes_customer_id_idx`, `credit_notes_invoice_id_idx`), and the
migration fails with "there is no unique constraint matching given keys". Move every `CREATE INDEX` and
`CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` up, before the first `ADD CONSTRAINT … FOREIGN KEY`. The result:
