- **Six new tables, six new columns, four changed constraints, four rebuilt indexes.** The new columns have constant
  defaults, so no existing row is rewritten, and the guards of 0028 and 0030 do not fire (adding a column is not an
  `UPDATE`).
- **The changed checks pass on existing rows.** Every existing invoice has `amount_credited = 0` and every receipt
  `refunded = 0`, so the new `invoices_paid_check`, `receipts_amount_check` and `receipts_void_check` say exactly
  what the old ones said.
- The snapshot (`meta/0031_snapshot.json`) and `_journal.json` are written by `drizzle-kit`; commit them as they are.

### Migration 0032 (custom): RLS, what may change when, the sums, the returns account

Run `pnpm --filter @omnivo/db generate --custom --name returns-credit-notes-rules`, then fill the file:

```sql
-- Custom SQL migration file, put your code below! --
-- 1) The six new tenant tables: ENABLE + FORCE RLS + tenant_isolation (with NULLIF, as in 0002)
DO $$
DECLARE
  t text;
BEGIN
  FOR t IN
    SELECT unnest(ARRAY[
      'sales_returns', 'sales_return_lines', 'credit_notes', 'credit_note_lines',
      'credit_note_allocations', 'refunds'
    ])
  LOOP
    EXECUTE format('ALTER TABLE %I ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY', t);
    EXECUTE format('ALTER TABLE %I FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY', t);
    EXECUTE format(
      'CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON %I
         USING (tenant_id = NULLIF(current_setting(''app.tenant_id'', true), '''')::uuid)
         WITH CHECK (tenant_id = NULLIF(current_setting(''app.tenant_id'', true), '''')::uuid)',
      t
    );
  END LOOP;
END $$;

-- 2) A sales return is a delivery the other way round (0028): a draft is changed and deleted
--    freely, a posted one never changes, because what came back into the warehouse came back.
CREATE FUNCTION sales_returns_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF OLD.status = 'posted' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'sales return % is posted and cannot be changed or deleted', OLD.id
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'sales_returns_posted_immutable';
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
    RETURN OLD;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;

CREATE TRIGGER sales_returns_guard
  BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON sales_returns
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sales_returns_guard();

-- The lines: only while the return is a draft, like a delivery's lines. So posting writes the
-- lines first (the value, the batch of a challan line, the invoice line that billed it) and sets
-- the return to posted last. One change is allowed on a posted return's line: a credit note's
-- posting adds to credited_quantity, with nothing else. It only grows: a credit note is never
-- undone. When a draft is deleted its lines cascade; the header is gone by then, so the lookup
-- finds nothing and lets them go.
CREATE FUNCTION sales_return_lines_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND NEW.credited_quantity > OLD.credited_quantity
     AND to_jsonb(NEW) - 'credited_quantity' = to_jsonb(OLD) - 'credited_quantity' THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF (TG_OP <> 'INSERT' AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM sales_returns
         WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.return_id AND status = 'posted'))
     OR (TG_OP <> 'DELETE' AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM sales_returns
         WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.return_id AND status = 'posted')) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'the lines of a posted sales return cannot be changed'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'sales_return_lines_posted_immutable';
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
    RETURN OLD;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;

CREATE TRIGGER sales_return_lines_guard
  BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON sales_return_lines
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sales_return_lines_guard();

-- 3) A draft credit note is changed and deleted freely. A posted one is in the books and in the
--    customer's file: it is never deleted and never voided. Only its money moves: applied (section
--    5's trigger, when it is applied again; the API bumps the version) and refunded (section 6's,
--    when a refund pays some of it back).
CREATE FUNCTION credit_notes_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF OLD.status = 'draft' THEN
    IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
      RETURN OLD;
    END IF;
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE'
     AND to_jsonb(NEW) - ARRAY['applied', 'refunded', 'version', 'updated_at', 'updated_by']
         = to_jsonb(OLD) - ARRAY['applied', 'refunded', 'version', 'updated_at', 'updated_by'] THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  RAISE EXCEPTION 'credit note % is posted and cannot be changed or deleted', OLD.id
    USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'credit_notes_posted_immutable';
END $$;

CREATE TRIGGER credit_notes_guard
  BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON credit_notes
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION credit_notes_guard();

-- The lines: only while the credit note is a draft, like an invoice's lines (0030)
CREATE FUNCTION credit_note_lines_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF (TG_OP <> 'INSERT' AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM credit_notes
         WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.credit_note_id AND status = 'posted'))
     OR (TG_OP <> 'DELETE' AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM credit_notes
         WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.credit_note_id AND status = 'posted')) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'the lines of a posted credit note cannot be changed'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'credit_note_lines_posted_immutable';
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
    RETURN OLD;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;

CREATE TRIGGER credit_note_lines_guard
  BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON credit_note_lines
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION credit_note_lines_guard();

-- 4) A refund is never deleted: like a receipt, its number is on paper. While posted it may be
--    voided (status, the void date and reason), nothing else. A voided refund never changes again.
CREATE FUNCTION refunds_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND OLD.status = 'posted' AND NEW.status = 'voided'
     AND to_jsonb(NEW) - ARRAY['status', 'void_date', 'void_reason', 'version', 'updated_at',
                               'updated_by']
         = to_jsonb(OLD) - ARRAY['status', 'void_date', 'void_reason', 'version', 'updated_at',
                                 'updated_by'] THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  RAISE EXCEPTION 'refund % can only be voided', OLD.id
    USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'refunds_immutable';
END $$;

CREATE TRIGGER refunds_guard
  BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON refunds
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION refunds_guard();

-- 5) invoices.amount_credited and credit_notes.applied are the sums of the credit note
--    allocations: 0030's receipt_allocations_apply with the credit note's names. The table checks
--    refuse what must not happen: settling an invoice past its total by receipts and credit notes
--    together, or a draft at all (invoices_paid_check); applying more than the credit note has
--    left, or anything of a draft (credit_notes_money_check). The UPDATE locks the invoice row,
--    so a receipt and a credit note settling its last ৳5,000 at the same moment run one after the
--    other, and the second one fails on the check.
CREATE FUNCTION credit_note_allocations_apply() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP <> 'INSERT' THEN
    UPDATE invoices SET amount_credited = amount_credited - OLD.amount
     WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.invoice_id;
    UPDATE credit_notes SET applied = applied - OLD.amount
     WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.credit_note_id;
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP <> 'DELETE' THEN
    UPDATE invoices SET amount_credited = amount_credited + NEW.amount
     WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.invoice_id;
    UPDATE credit_notes SET applied = applied + NEW.amount
     WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.credit_note_id;
  END IF;
  RETURN NULL;
END $$;

CREATE TRIGGER credit_note_allocations_apply
  AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON credit_note_allocations
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION credit_note_allocations_apply();

-- 6) receipts.refunded and credit_notes.refunded are the sums of the POSTED refunds paid out of
--    them. A new refund adds its amount to its source; voiding it takes the amount off again, so
--    the money is the source's advance once more. Section 4's guard means nothing else ever
--    changes on a refund, but the trigger handles any update the same way: take the old row off
--    if it counted, put the new row on if it counts. Only one of the two UPDATEs finds a row (a
--    refund has one source). The checks refuse paying back more than the source has left
--    (receipts_amount_check, credit_notes_money_check), from a draft credit note
--    (credit_notes_money_check) and from a voided receipt (its guard).
CREATE FUNCTION refunds_apply() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND OLD.status = 'posted' THEN
    UPDATE receipts SET refunded = refunded - OLD.amount
     WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.receipt_id;
    UPDATE credit_notes SET refunded = refunded - OLD.amount
     WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.credit_note_id;
  END IF;
  IF NEW.status = 'posted' THEN
    UPDATE receipts SET refunded = refunded + NEW.amount
     WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.receipt_id;
    UPDATE credit_notes SET refunded = refunded + NEW.amount
     WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.credit_note_id;
  END IF;
  RETURN NULL;
END $$;

CREATE TRIGGER refunds_apply
  AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON refunds
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION refunds_apply();

-- 7) 0030's invoice guard, with what credit notes write. A posted invoice may still have its money
--    settled (amount_paid by receipts, amount_credited by credit notes) and its credited total
--    grow (credit_note_total, written by a credit note's posting through Drizzle, which also sets
--    updated_at and may set updated_by). Nothing else, and the credited total never goes down: a
--    credit note is never undone.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION invoices_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF OLD.status = 'draft' THEN
    IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
      RETURN OLD;
    END IF;
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND NEW.credit_note_total >= OLD.credit_note_total
     AND to_jsonb(NEW) - ARRAY['amount_paid', 'amount_credited', 'credit_note_total',
                               'updated_at', 'updated_by']
         = to_jsonb(OLD) - ARRAY['amount_paid', 'amount_credited', 'credit_note_total',
                                 'updated_at', 'updated_by'] THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  RAISE EXCEPTION 'invoice % is posted and cannot be changed or deleted', OLD.id
    USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'invoices_posted_immutable';
END $$;

-- The lines: one change is allowed on a posted invoice's line, a credit note's posting adding to
-- credited, with nothing else. Never down.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION invoice_lines_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND NEW.credited > OLD.credited
     AND to_jsonb(NEW) - 'credited' = to_jsonb(OLD) - 'credited' THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF (TG_OP <> 'INSERT' AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM invoices
         WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.invoice_id AND status = 'posted'))
     OR (TG_OP <> 'DELETE' AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM invoices
         WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.invoice_id AND status = 'posted')) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'the lines of a posted invoice cannot be changed'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'invoice_lines_posted_immutable';
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
    RETURN OLD;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;

-- 8) 0030's receipt guard, with refunds. While posted, a receipt may have its money applied again
--    or paid back (applied and refunded move, by their triggers), or be voided. Voiding does not
--    list refunded: receipts_void_check wants it at zero, so a receipt with a posted refund cannot
--    be voided (receipt_has_refunds) until the refund is voided first.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION receipts_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND OLD.status = 'posted' AND (
       (NEW.status = 'posted'
        AND to_jsonb(NEW) - ARRAY['applied', 'refunded', 'version', 'updated_at', 'updated_by']
            = to_jsonb(OLD) - ARRAY['applied', 'refunded', 'version', 'updated_at', 'updated_by'])
       OR (NEW.status = 'voided'
        AND to_jsonb(NEW) - ARRAY['status', 'applied', 'void_date', 'void_reason', 'version',
                                  'updated_at', 'updated_by']
            = to_jsonb(OLD) - ARRAY['status', 'applied', 'void_date', 'void_reason', 'version',
                                    'updated_at', 'updated_by'])) THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  RAISE EXCEPTION 'receipt % can only have its money applied or be voided', OLD.id
    USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'receipts_immutable';
END $$;

-- 9) 0030's delivery line guard, with returns. Two changes are allowed on a posted challan's
--    line, each on its own: it becomes invoiced (false → true, once), or a return's posting adds
--    to returned_quantity (only up: a posted return is never undone). Both with nothing else.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION delivery_lines_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND NOT OLD.invoiced AND NEW.invoiced
     AND to_jsonb(NEW) - 'invoiced' = to_jsonb(OLD) - 'invoiced' THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND NEW.returned_quantity > OLD.returned_quantity
     AND to_jsonb(NEW) - 'returned_quantity' = to_jsonb(OLD) - 'returned_quantity' THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF (TG_OP <> 'INSERT' AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM deliveries
         WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.delivery_id AND status = 'posted'))
     OR (TG_OP <> 'DELETE' AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM deliveries
         WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.delivery_id AND status = 'posted')) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'the lines of a posted delivery cannot be changed'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'delivery_lines_posted_immutable';
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
    RETURN OLD;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;

-- 10) A return before invoicing gives the order its goods back (you chose this): the order line's
--     delivered quantity goes down, and a delivered order is confirmed again, so a replacement can
--     go out on the same order, or the order is closed. 0028's order guard, with that one new move:
--     delivered → confirmed, only the status changing. It keeps its confirmation time: it was
--     confirmed then, and still is.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sales_orders_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
    IF OLD.status <> 'draft' OR OLD.number IS NOT NULL THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'sales order % has a number and cannot be deleted; cancel it instead', OLD.id
        USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'sales_orders_numbered_immutable';
    END IF;
    RETURN OLD;
  END IF;

  IF OLD.status = 'draft' AND NEW.status IN ('draft', 'confirmed') THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF OLD.status = 'confirmed'
     AND to_jsonb(NEW) - ARRAY['status', 'confirmed_at', 'confirmed_by', 'shipping_address_id',
                               'version', 'updated_at', 'updated_by']
         = to_jsonb(OLD) - ARRAY['status', 'confirmed_at', 'confirmed_by', 'shipping_address_id',
                                 'version', 'updated_at', 'updated_by'] THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF OLD.status = 'delivered' AND NEW.status = 'confirmed'
     AND to_jsonb(NEW) - ARRAY['status', 'version', 'updated_at', 'updated_by']
         = to_jsonb(OLD) - ARRAY['status', 'version', 'updated_at', 'updated_by'] THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF NEW.shipping_address_id IS NULL
     AND to_jsonb(NEW) - 'shipping_address_id' = to_jsonb(OLD) - 'shipping_address_id' THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  RAISE EXCEPTION 'sales order % is % and cannot be changed this way', OLD.id, OLD.status
    USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'sales_orders_confirmed_immutable';
END $$;

-- The lines: 0030's guard, and on a delivered or closed order the delivered quantity may now go
-- down. Never up: a delivered order is confirmed again before it delivers more, and a closed one
-- delivers nothing more.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sales_order_lines_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
  v_status text;
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN
    SELECT status INTO v_status
      FROM sales_orders WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.order_id;
    -- NULL: no such order — the foreign key gives that error
    IF v_status IS NOT NULL AND v_status <> 'draft' THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'lines cannot be added to a sales order that is not a draft'
        USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'sales_order_lines_confirmed_immutable';
    END IF;
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;

  SELECT status INTO v_status
    FROM sales_orders WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.order_id;
  IF v_status IS NULL OR (v_status = 'draft' AND OLD.invoiced_quantity = 0) THEN
    IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
      RETURN OLD;
    END IF;
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND v_status = 'confirmed'
     AND to_jsonb(NEW) - ARRAY['delivered_quantity', 'invoiced_quantity']
         = to_jsonb(OLD) - ARRAY['delivered_quantity', 'invoiced_quantity'] THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND v_status IN ('delivered', 'closed')
     AND NEW.delivered_quantity <= OLD.delivered_quantity
     AND to_jsonb(NEW) - ARRAY['delivered_quantity', 'invoiced_quantity']
         = to_jsonb(OLD) - ARRAY['delivered_quantity', 'invoiced_quantity'] THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  RAISE EXCEPTION 'the lines of a confirmed sales order cannot be changed, except what was delivered and invoiced'
    USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'sales_order_lines_confirmed_immutable';
END $$;

-- 11) The sales returns account of the workspaces that already exist: what setup (15d.3) fills in
--     for a new one. The pharmacy and retail templates have "4120 Sales returns"; in the other
--     templates 4120 is something else ("Local sales", "Trade discounts", "Service income"), so the
--     code alone is not enough: the name must match too, and the account must still be an active
--     income account that takes postings. A workspace that renamed or moved it picks it in
--     Settings → Sales. Like 0030, each workspace is updated with its own app.tenant_id: FORCE RLS
--     applies to this migration's role too.
DO $$
DECLARE
  t uuid;
BEGIN
  FOR t IN SELECT id FROM tenants LOOP
    PERFORM set_config('app.tenant_id', t::text, true);
    UPDATE tenant_settings s
       SET sales_returns_account_id = a.id
      FROM ledger_accounts a
     WHERE s.tenant_id = t
       AND s.sales_returns_account_id IS NULL
       AND a.tenant_id = t
       AND a.code = '4120'
       AND a.name = 'Sales returns'
       AND a.type = 'income'
       AND NOT a.is_group
       AND a.archived_at IS NULL;
  END LOOP;
  PERFORM set_config('app.tenant_id', '', true);
END $$;
```

Part by part:

1. **RLS on the six new tables**, exactly like 0022 to 0030. The tenant-leak suite's RLS coverage test fails if a
   table with a `tenant_id` lacks `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`.
2. **The return guards.** A posted return never changes, like a posted challan: what came back came back. The line
   guard allows one change on a posted return: `credited_quantity` grows, with nothing else. It is the delivery
   line guard of 0030 with the return's names, and it sets the same order of writes for 15d.3: the lines first (the
   value, the batch, the invoice line), the header last.
3. **The credit note guards.** A draft is free. A posted credit note is never deleted and never voided (you chose no
   void). Only its money moves: `applied` and `refunded` by their triggers, and the version the API bumps when a
   person applies its money again (a person's edit can race another person's, as on a receipt). The line guard is
   0030's invoice line guard with the credit note's names.
4. **The refund guard.** A refund is never deleted (its number is on paper) and only changes once: posted to voided,
   with the void date and reason. A voided refund never changes again, so it can never be "un-voided" by mistake.
5. **The credit note allocation trigger** is 0030's `receipt_allocations_apply` with two other columns:
   `invoices.amount_credited` and `credit_notes.applied`.
   - **It checks nothing itself**, like the receipt's. Its `UPDATE`s meet `invoices_paid_check` (settled past the
     total by receipts and credit notes together, or a draft at all) and `credit_notes_money_check` (more than the
     credit note has left, or anything of a draft).
   - **A receipt and a credit note at the same moment.** Both triggers update the same invoice row, so both take the
     same row lock. The second one waits, then sees the first one's sum and fails the check if the two together are
     too much. We tried it (below).
6. **The refund trigger** keeps `receipts.refunded` and `credit_notes.refunded`.
   - **Only posted refunds count.** A new refund adds its amount; voiding takes it off again, so the money is the
     source's advance once more and can be applied or paid back again.
   - **Two `UPDATE`s, one of which finds nothing.** A refund has exactly one source, and `WHERE id = NULL` matches no
     row. This is simpler than an `IF` on which column is set, and just as cheap.
   - **"Take the old row off if it counted, put the new row on if it counts."** The guard means only one update ever
     happens (posted → voided), but the trigger does not depend on that.
   - **The source decides.** Paying back more than is left fails on the source's own check, a draft credit note fails
     `credit_notes_money_check`, and a voided receipt fails its guard (a voided receipt never changes again).
7. **The invoice guards, again.** `CREATE OR REPLACE` swaps 0030's functions; the triggers stay.
   - **A posted invoice** may now change `amount_credited` (by section 5) and `credit_note_total` (by the credit
     note's posting), besides `amount_paid`. `credit_note_total` may only go up: a credit note is never undone.
   - **`updated_at` and `updated_by` may change with them.** `credit_note_total` is written by the API through
     Drizzle, which sets `updated_at` on every update (`$onUpdate` in `baseColumns()`). Without these two in the
     list, every credit note posting would fail here. `version` is not in the list: a credit note does not edit the
     invoice, so it must not make an open invoice page look out of date.
   - **A posted invoice's line** may now have `credited` go up, with nothing else.
8. **The receipt guard, again.** While posted, `refunded` may move too (by section 6). The void branch does not list
   `refunded`: `receipts_void_check` wants it at zero, so the void fails while a refund is posted.
9. **The delivery line guard, again.** Two changes are allowed on a posted challan's line, each on its own:
   `invoiced` goes from false to true (15c), or `returned_quantity` goes up. Each must come with nothing else, so a
   bug cannot slip a quantity change in with them. Never down: a posted return is never undone.
10. **The order guards, again.** You chose that a return before invoicing gives the order its goods back.
    - **Delivered → confirmed** is a new move, with only the status changing. The order keeps its `confirmed_at`: it
      was confirmed then, and still is. A replacement can now go out on the same order, or someone closes it.
    - **On a delivered or closed order, `delivered_quantity` may go down**, never up. The API lowers it only for
      challan lines that were not billed (after billing, the sale stands and a credit note corrects the money), so
      `invoiced_quantity` never ends up above `delivered_quantity`.
    - **15d.3 sets the order of writes** however it likes: on a confirmed order both quantities may change, and on a
      delivered one the delivered quantity may go down, so the lines can be lowered before or after the order goes
      back to confirmed.
11. **The returns account of existing workspaces.** New workspaces get it from setup (15d.3).
    - **By code and name: "4120" and "Sales returns".** Only the pharmacy and retail templates have that account. In
      the garments template 4120 is "Local sales" (next to "4110 Export sales"), in the distribution template "Trade
      discounts", in the "other" template "Service income". Matching the code alone would point a garments company's
      credit notes at "Local sales", and the profit and loss would quietly net returns against the wrong line. We
      tried a workspace with "4120 Local sales": it stayed empty.
    - **Only an active income account that takes postings**, and only where nothing is chosen yet, so running it
      twice changes nothing.
    - **`set_config('app.tenant_id', …)` per workspace**, like 0030: `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` applies to the
      migration's own role too. We ran this block as `omnivo_migrator`.

> **What we checked.** On a throwaway database with every migration up to 0032, as `omnivo_app` (83 checks, plus two
> races in two sessions). A challan line refused a returned quantity above what left, going back down, and a change
> together with the value or the invoiced flag. A draft return was changed and deleted with its lines. A return line
> refused an invoice line without its invoice, an invoice line on a line on its own, an invoice line of another
> invoice, and a credited quantity on a line that was not billed. Posting lowered a delivered order's delivered
> quantity, refused raising it again, sent the order back to confirmed (refused with any other change, and refused
> back to draft), and on a closed order allowed lowering only. A posted return refused edits, going back to draft,
> deletion, and changes to its lines other than a growing credited quantity. A credit note for another customer's
> invoice failed; a credit line for another invoice's line, under another invoice's credit note, or for an unbilled
> return line failed on its FK; a credit line for the billed return line was accepted. Applying a draft's money
> failed. Posting two credit notes and applying one: the invoice showed ৳115 credited and ৳161 credited in total.
> A credited total on a draft invoice, credit on a line above its total, either number going down, and either
> number with another change all failed; the invoice's version was frozen, its `updated_at` was not. A posted credit
> note refused edits, going back to draft, deletion, and line changes. Moving an allocation moved the credit. A
> receipt that would settle INV-1 past its total next to the credit failed, and so did a credit after the receipt.
> Refunds added to their receipt and credit note; paying back too much (both kinds), applying money that was paid
> back, refunding a draft credit note, two sources, no source, another customer's receipt and a second RF number
> all failed. A refund refused edits, deletion, a void without a reason or before its date, and going back to
> posted. A receipt with a refund could not be voided; after the refund was voided it could, and then no refund
> could come from it. A journal entry of each new source without a document failed. Deleting a customer with a
> return, an account with a refund and the chosen returns account failed on their FKs. Another workspace saw none of
> the six tables, could not write into them and could not change them. Section 11 set 4120 "Sales returns" in one
> workspace and left "4120 Local sales" alone, as `omnivo_migrator`. Two returns of the last piece of one challan line
> at once: the second waited and failed on `delivery_lines_returned_check`. A receipt and a credit note settling a
> ৳115 invoice with ৳100 each at once: the second waited and failed on `invoices_paid_check`. `drizzle-kit generate`
> then reports no schema changes.

### Check this part

```bash
pnpm --filter @omnivo/db typecheck
pnpm lint
```

`pnpm typecheck` for the whole repo still fails, as expected after 15d.1, but in fewer places. The `packages/db`
error (the permission descriptions) is gone. The API still has to send the new fields (`returnState`,
`returnedQuantity`, `amountCredited`, `creditNoteTotal`, `refunded`, …) and serve the new routes (15d.3);
`packages/i18n` needs the new keys (15d.5); and the app's pills and mocks need the new fields (15d.6, 15d.7).

Then run `pnpm db:migrate` against your dev database. It applies 0031 and 0032, fills the sales returns account where
your chart has "4120 Sales returns", and writes the three permissions.

## 15d.3 — `apps/api`: returns, credit notes, refunds and the sales returns account

The contract and the tables are ready; this part writes the server. Six new files hold the new work:
`sales-returns.service.ts`, `credit-notes.service.ts` and `refunds.service.ts` (one service per document),
`sales-accounts.service.ts` and its controller (Settings → Sales), and `allocations.ts`, the check a receipt and a
credit note now share. Existing files change where 15d touches them: a challan shows what came back, an invoice shows
what was credited and bills what is left, a receipt can be paid back, the books learn three new entries, setup
chooses the returns account for a new pharmacy or shop, and an account, a customer or a product that a new document
holds on to cannot be deleted.

The design follows 15b and 15c on purpose. A sales return is written and posted like a challan, the other way round.
A credit note is written and posted like an invoice, and its money is applied like a receipt's. A refund is saved and
voided like a receipt. If you know those three, most of this part will look familiar; the prose below points out
where it is different, and why.

One more rule runs through every posting here: **the locks are always taken in the same order.** Challans before
orders, orders before products, products before the number series, and the stock rows last (15b and 15c already do
it this way). A return and an invoice of the same challan line, or two credit notes of one invoice, then wait for
each other in a line, never in a circle.

### `sales/allocations.ts` (new): one check for the money of a receipt and a credit note

```ts
import { amountDueOf, compareMoney, type ErrorCode, sumMoney } from '@omnivo/contracts';
import { invoices } from '@omnivo/db';
import { and, asc, eq, inArray } from 'drizzle-orm';

import { diff } from '../common/audit/audit.js';
import { getTenantId } from '../common/tenant/tenant-context.js';
import type { Transaction } from '../common/tenant/with-tenant.js';
import { type LineIssue, linesError } from '../inventory/stock-lines.js';

// What money receipts (step 15c) and credit notes (step 15d) do the same way: put some money on a
// customer's invoices, each row no more than what the invoice still owes. Each document keeps its
// own rows (receipt_allocations, credit_note_allocations) and its own error codes; the check and
// the audit snapshot are here once.

export interface Allocation {
  invoiceId: string;
  amount: string;
}

// The document's own words for the two problems a row can have
export interface AllocationErrors {
  // Not a posted invoice of this customer
  invoice: ErrorCode;
  // More than the invoice still owes
  over: ErrorCode;
}

// An allocation's problem, under its own row of the form: allocations.2.amount
export function allocationPath(index: number, field: string): string {
  return `allocations.${String(index)}.${field}`;
}

// Checks `wanted` before it replaces `current` (the document's rows now). Every invoice of both
// lists is locked in id order before anything is read, so two documents paying one invoice take
// turns, and the second sees what the first applied. FOR NO KEY UPDATE, not FOR UPDATE: a credit
// note's own insert already holds a KEY SHARE lock on its invoice (the foreign key), and FOR UPDATE
// would wait for every other credit note being saved for that invoice, while they wait for us. Each wanted row must name a
// posted invoice of the customer and fit what it still owes after receipts and credit notes
// (amountDueOf), where this document's own current row counts as owed again: it is being replaced.
// All problems come back at once, each under its row.
export async function checkAllocations(
  tx: Transaction,
  input: {
    customerId: string;
    current: readonly Allocation[];
    wanted: readonly Allocation[];
    errors: AllocationErrors;
  },
): Promise<void> {
  const invoiceIds = [
    ...new Set([...input.current, ...input.wanted].map((allocation) => allocation.invoiceId)),
  ];
  const rows =
    invoiceIds.length === 0
      ? []
      : await tx
          .select({
            id: invoices.id,
            customerId: invoices.customerId,
            status: invoices.status,
            total: invoices.total,
            amountPaid: invoices.amountPaid,
            amountCredited: invoices.amountCredited,
          })
          .from(invoices)
          .where(and(eq(invoices.tenantId, getTenantId()), inArray(invoices.id, invoiceIds)))
          .orderBy(asc(invoices.id))
          .for('no key update');
  const byId = new Map(rows.map((row) => [row.id, row]));
  const had = new Map(input.current.map((allocation) => [allocation.invoiceId, allocation.amount]));

  const issues: LineIssue[] = [];
  input.wanted.forEach((allocation, index) => {
    const invoice = byId.get(allocation.invoiceId);
    if (invoice?.customerId !== input.customerId || invoice.status !== 'posted') {
      issues.push({ path: allocationPath(index, 'invoiceId'), code: input.errors.invoice });
      return;
    }
    const due = sumMoney([amountDueOf(invoice), had.get(allocation.invoiceId) ?? '0']);
    if (compareMoney(allocation.amount, due) > 0) {
      issues.push({ path: allocationPath(index, 'amount'), code: input.errors.over });
    }
  });
  if (issues.length > 0) throw linesError(issues);
}

// Invoice number → amount
function allocationSnapshot(
  allocations: readonly { invoiceNumber: string | null; amount: string }[],
): Record<string, string> {
  return Object.fromEntries(
    allocations.map((allocation) => [allocation.invoiceNumber ?? '', allocation.amount]),
  );
}

// What the audit log shows of the allocations: one row per invoice number, with the amount before
// and after. diff() walks the new list only, so an invoice the money was taken off is added with
// null; without that, the log would not show where the money came from.
export function allocationChanges(
  before: readonly { invoiceNumber: string | null; amount: string }[],
  after: readonly { invoiceNumber: string | null; amount: string }[],
) {
  const from = allocationSnapshot(before);
  const to: Record<string, string | null> = allocationSnapshot(after);
  for (const invoiceNumber of Object.keys(from)) to[invoiceNumber] ??= null;
  return diff(from, to);
}
```

- **Why a new file.** 15c's receipt checked its allocations inside `ReceiptsService`. A credit note applies its money
  the same way, with its own error codes. Copying the check would mean two places that must stay the same forever, so
  it moved here and both services call it.
- **`amountDueOf()`** is the contract's function (15d.1): total − paid − credited. 15c's check read only
  `amountPaid`. With credit notes, an invoice of ৳1,000 with ৳300 paid and ৳200 credited owes ৳500, not ৳700; the
  old check would have let a receipt pay ৳700 and the database would have refused it with a 500.
- **`AllocationErrors`.** The receipt says `receipt_over_invoice`, the credit note `credit_note_over_invoice`. The
  words on the form are almost the same, but "this receipt pays more than…" would be wrong under a credit note.
- **The locks**: every invoice of the old and the new list, in id order, before anything is read. A receipt and a
  credit note settling the last ৳5,000 of one invoice take turns, and the second one is refused under its row.
- **`FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, where 15c had `FOR UPDATE`.** A credit note's own insert already holds a `KEY SHARE` lock on
  its invoice (the foreign key `credit_notes_invoice_fk` takes one), and so does every other credit note being saved
  for that invoice at the same moment. `FOR UPDATE` conflicts with `KEY SHARE`, so two credit notes would each wait
  for the other: Postgres finds the deadlock and kills one with a 500. `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` does not conflict with
  `KEY SHARE`, but it still conflicts with itself, so two writers still take turns. It is the lock an `UPDATE` of a
  column that no foreign key points at takes anyway. The tests of 15d.4 found this (see there).
- **`allocationChanges()`** moved here unchanged from `receipts.service.ts`, for `credit_note.allocated`.

### `sales/sales-lines.ts`: the money account check, shared

```diff
@@ -5,13 +5,21 @@ import {
   isQuantity,
   type LineAmounts,
   lineAmounts,
+  moneyAccountIds,
   type PartyRef,
   type SalesLine,
   type SalesLineInput,
   type TaxRateKind,
   toBaseQuantity,
 } from '@omnivo/contracts';
-import { branches, parties, partyAddresses, taxRates, tenantSettings } from '@omnivo/db';
+import {
+  branches,
```

- **`assertMoneyAccount()`** is 15c's private receipt check, moved here with one new parameter: the error code. A
  receipt's money goes *into* the account, a refund's comes *out of* it, and each form says so in its own words
  (`receipt_account_invalid`, `refund_account_invalid`). The rule is the same: a cash, bank or wallet account, read
  with the contract's `moneyAccountIds()`, the same function the forms use for their lists.

- **`refunded`** goes into every receipt the API sends (15d.1's contract). The refunds' trigger keeps it (15d.2).
- **The allocate cap is `amount − refunded`.** Money that was paid back to the customer is gone. A receipt of
  ৳990 with ৳200 refunded can apply ৳790 at most; the database's `receipts_amount_check` agrees.
- **Void checks for refunds first** (`receipt_has_refunds`). A bounced cheque that was partly paid back in cash
  would leave the company out of that cash with nothing in the books to say why. The person voids the refund first,
  then the receipt. The receipt's own lock makes a new refund of it wait (`RefundsService` locks the receipt too), so
  the query sees every posted refund there is.
- **`apply()` calls `checkAllocations()`**, and the receipt's own copies of the check, the path helper, the audit
  snapshot and the money account check are gone (moved, not changed).
- **The race message** now names credit notes too: a receipt can lose the last taka of an invoice to a credit note
  as well as to another receipt.

- **The credit note's entry** is the invoice's entry the other way round: Dr the sales returns account (net) / Dr
  Output VAT (VAT) / Cr Accounts receivable with the customer (total). Every line carries the *invoice's* branch, so
  the sale comes off the branch that made it, even if the credit note is written at head office. A credit note of
  ৳0 has no entry, and a line of ৳0 (an exempt item has no VAT) is left out, like an invoice's.
- **`returnsAccount()`.** You chose a setting (decision 7). `null` means "none chosen", and the credit note debits
  the Sales account itself. A chosen account that cannot be used anymore (archived, or turned into a group) would
  otherwise be refused deep inside the journal under a line nobody sees; here it is `sales_account_invalid` with a
  message that sends the person to Settings → Sales. In practice it cannot happen: `AccountsService` refuses to
  archive or delete the chosen account (below). `FOR SHARE`, like the other accounts: postings to it run in parallel,
  only an archive waits.
- **The refund's entry** is a receipt the other way round: Dr Accounts receivable with the customer / Cr the money
  account. The customer's advance was a credit balance on the receivable; paying it out brings the balance back to
  zero.
- **`reverse()`** did not change: a voided refund is reversed exactly like a voided receipt. Only the comments now
  say so.

- **Dr Inventory / Cr Cost of goods sold**, the delivery's entry the other way round, at what the goods cost.
- **Two branches.** The stock comes back into the return's warehouse, so Inventory takes *that* warehouse's branch.
  The cost comes off cost of goods sold where the challan booked it: the branch of the warehouse the goods *left*
  from. A pharmacy chain that sends every return to the head office's "Damage/Expiry" warehouse then sees the cost of
  goods sold go down in the branch that sold the strips, not at the head office. A line on its own has no challan, so
  it takes the return warehouse's branch on both sides.
- **`costs` per line, summed by `write()`.** Ten lines from one challan become one credit line, as with every stock
  entry.

- **`lineToInvoice` now also needs `returned_quantity < base_quantity`.** A line that all came back before it was
  billed has nothing left to bill. Without this, a challan whose only unbilled line came back in full would stay
  "partly invoiced" forever, and the invoice form would keep offering it. The condition is the one the partial
  index `delivery_lines_to_invoice_idx` has since 15d.2, so the index is still used.
- **`returnState`** is worked out in the list query, like `invoiceState`: no line returned → `none`, a line that
  can still come back → `partly_returned`, every line back in full → `returned`. A draft took nothing out, so it is
  always `none`.
- **`returnFilter()`.** `returnable` is what the return form's challan picker asks for: posted, with a line that has
  not all come back.
- **`returnedQuantity`** on each line, and **`returns`** on the challan: the posted returns that brought some of it
  back, like `invoices`. A draft return brought nothing back yet, so it is not listed.

- **`isOpen` and the `paid` filter add `amount_credited`.** An invoice settled by a credit note is as settled as one
  paid by a receipt. `isOpen` is still written exactly like the two partial indexes (changed in 15d.2), so Postgres
  still uses them.
- **`amountCredited`, `creditNoteTotal` and each line's `credited`** go into the response (15d.1's contract).
- **A challan line is billed by its base quantity less what came back** (`billableQuantity()` from the contract).
  15c compared the unit and the quantity as typed: 2 cases billed 2 cases. After 10 of the 48 pieces came back
  before billing, the invoice must bill 38 pieces, which is not a whole number of cases, so the line may now be in any
  unit of the item (the form switches to the base unit when something came back, 15d.6). `baseQuantityOf()` turns the
  typed quantity into the base unit with the item's units, so 2 cases and 48 pcs are the same 48. A unit the item
  does not have gives `null`, and the line is refused as not matching its challan line.
- **`returned_quantity` is read after the challans' lock**, like `invoiced`. A return posting locks the same
  challans (`SalesReturnsService.challanLines()`), so whichever of the two posts second sees what the first did: an
  invoice of 48 after a return of 10 is refused (`invoice_delivery_line_invalid`), a return after the invoice is
  "billed" and goes to a credit note.
- **`creditNotes`** on the invoice page: the posted credit notes written for it, oldest first. The app's "Credit
  whole invoice" button (15d.6) is shown only while this list is empty (`canCreditWhole()`).
- **`returnedBeforeBilling()`.** A challan line of 3 phones, one sent back before the invoice: the invoice bills 2,
  so it must not print the third IMEI. A phone that came back *after* billing was billed (its money goes back on a
  credit note), so it stays on the invoice. The return line's `invoice_line_id` says which is which: `NULL` means it
  came back before it was billed (15d.2).

```ts
  variantId: string;
  unitId: string;
  quantity: string;
  batchId: string | null;
  serialNumbers: readonly string[];
}

// A challan line a return line comes back from, with what its challan says about it
interface ChallanLine {
  id: string;
  deliveryId: string;
  customerId: string;
  status: StockDocumentStatus;
  // The warehouse the goods left from: its branch booked their cost (15b), so the return takes the
  // cost off there
  warehouseId: string;
  variantId: string;
  baseQuantity: string;
  returnedQuantity: string;
  batchId: string | null;
  serialNumbers: string[];
  value: string | null;
  invoiced: boolean;
  orderLineId: string | null;
}

// The lines once checked: resolved like a stock document's (the batch of a challan line is the
// challan line's), with the challan lines they name
interface Checked {
  lines: ResolvedLine[];
  challans: Map<string, ChallanLine>;
}

// The invoice line that billed a challan line, and its invoice
interface Billing {
  invoiceId: string;
  invoiceLineId: string;
}

function notDraft(): AppError {
  return new AppError(
    409,
    'stock_not_draft',
    'Only a draft can be changed. A posted return is final: goods that go out again go on a delivery.',
  );
}

function toSummary(row: ReturnRow, customer: PartyRef, lines: number): SalesReturnSummary {
  return {
    id: row.id,
    number: row.number,
    date: row.date,
    customer,
    warehouseId: row.warehouseId,
    reason: row.reason,
    status: row.status,
    note: row.note,
    lineCount: lines,
    postedAt: row.postedAt?.toISOString() ?? null,
    version: row.version,
    updatedAt: row.updatedAt.toISOString(),
  };
}

// What `quantity` coming back from a challan line is worth: its share of what the line took out
// (you chose this: the cost of goods sold is reversed exactly). Counted over everything returned
// from the line so far, so a line that comes back in three goes gives back exactly its value, with
// no paisa left over by rounding.
function returnValue(challan: ChallanLine, quantity: string): string {
  if (challan.value === null) throw new Error(`Posted challan line ${challan.id} has no value`);
  const after = sumQuantity([challan.returnedQuantity, quantity]);
  return subtractMoney(
    prorateMoney(challan.value, after, challan.baseQuantity),
    prorateMoney(challan.value, challan.returnedQuantity, challan.baseQuantity),
  );
}

// StockPostingService asks for a cost (lines.2.unitCost) when an item has none yet: its first
// stock. A line on its own comes back at the average cost, and a return has no cost box, so the
// problem goes under the item with the return's own code: the item needs its opening stock first.
function noCostError(error: unknown): never {
  if (
    !(error instanceof AppError) ||
    error.code !== 'stock_cost_required' ||
    error.options.fieldErrors === undefined
  ) {
    throw error;
  }
  const fieldErrors = Object.fromEntries(
    Object.keys(error.options.fieldErrors).map((path) => [
      path.replace(/\.unitCost$/, '.variantId'),
      ['return_cost_unknown' as const satisfies ErrorCode],
    ]),
  );
  throw new AppError(
    409,
    'return_cost_unknown',
    'Some items have no cost yet. Bring in their opening stock first.',
    { fieldErrors },
  );
}

// The database's last word on a challan line (delivery_lines_returned_check): never more back than
// left. The locks in postAndLog() make it unreachable in practice; it still answers with the code
// the form knows.
function overDeliveredRace(error: unknown): unknown {
  if (isCheckViolation(error, 'delivery_lines_returned_check')) {
    return new AppError(
      409,
      'return_over_delivered',
      'Another return brought some of these goods back first. Reload and try again.',
    );
  }
  return error;
}
```

- **`LineRefs`** is what `checkLines()` reads. A form line and a stored line both have these fields, so the save
  and the posting run the same check, as in 15c's invoice.
- **`ChallanLine.warehouseId`** is the challan's warehouse: its branch booked the cost of goods sold (15b), so the
  return takes the cost off there.
- **`returnValue()`: the cost comes back exactly** (decision 2). Each return takes its share of the challan line's
  value, counted over everything returned from the line so far: `value × (before + now) ÷ base − value × before ÷
  base`, each rounded to the paisa. Example: a line of 3 pcs worth ৳10.00 comes back one piece at a time. A plain
  share would give back ৳3.33 three times, ৳9.99 in all, and leave one paisa in cost of goods sold forever. Counted
  this way the three returns give back ৳3.33, ৳3.34 and ৳3.33: exactly ৳10.00. This is the same idea as step 14's
  `outflowValue()`, where taking the last piece takes all the value.
- **`noCostError()`.** A line on its own comes back at the average cost (decision 2), and an item that never had
  any stock has no average. `StockPostingService` answers that with `stock_cost_required` under
  `lines.2.unitCost`, a box a return does not have, with words that say "enter what it cost". The return renames it
  to `return_cost_unknown` under the item: bring in its opening stock first.
- **`overDeliveredRace()`** turns the database's last word (`delivery_lines_returned_check`) into the form's code,
  *outside* the transaction, after its rollback (the pattern of step 6). The locks make it unreachable in practice.

```ts
// Sales returns (step 15d): goods a customer sent back, into the warehouse the return names. A
// draft is changed freely; "Post" numbers it, puts the stock back at what it cost, takes that cost
// off cost of goods sold, and counts it on the challan lines it names. It moves no money: a credit
// note does that.
@Injectable()
export class SalesReturnsService {
  constructor(
    @Inject(WITH_TENANT) private readonly withTenant: WithTenant,
    private readonly numbering: NumberingService,
    private readonly posting: StockPostingService,
    private readonly books: StockBooksService,
    private readonly access: ValueAccess,
  ) {}

  list(query: {
    limit: number;
    cursor?: string | undefined;
    status?: StockDocumentStatus | undefined;
    customerId?: string | undefined;
    warehouseId?: string | undefined;
  }): Promise<{ items: SalesReturnSummary[]; nextCursor: string | null }> {
    const after = decodeCursor(query.cursor, cursorSchema);
    return this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
      const rows = await this.rows(
        tx,
        and(
          query.status === undefined ? undefined : eq(salesReturns.status, query.status),
          query.customerId === undefined
            ? undefined
            : eq(salesReturns.customerId, query.customerId),
          query.warehouseId === undefined
            ? undefined
            : eq(salesReturns.warehouseId, query.warehouseId),
          after === undefined
            ? undefined
            : sql`(${salesReturns.date}, ${salesReturns.id}) < (${after[0]}::date, ${after[1]}::uuid)`,
        ),
        query.limit + 1,
      );
      const page = toPage(rows, query.limit, (last) => [
        last.salesReturn.date,
        last.salesReturn.id,
      ]);
      return {
        items: page.items.map((row) => toSummary(row.salesReturn, row.customer, row.lineCount)),
        nextCursor: page.nextCursor,
      };
    });
  }

  get(id: string): Promise<SalesReturn> {
    return this.withTenant((tx) => this.read(tx, id));
  }

  async create(input: SalesReturnInput): Promise<SalesReturn> {
    try {
      return await this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
        const customer = await assertCustomer(tx, input.customerId);
        await assertWarehousesActive(tx, [
          { field: 'warehouseId', warehouseId: input.warehouseId },
        ]);
        const checked = await this.checkLines(tx, customer.id, input.lines, false);
        const [row] = await tx
          .insert(salesReturns)
          .values({
            tenantId: getTenantId(),
            date: input.date,
            customerId: customer.id,
            warehouseId: input.warehouseId,
            reason: input.reason,
            note: input.note,
            createdBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
            updatedBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
          })
          .returning();
        if (!row) throw new Error('Sales return insert returned no row');
        await this.writeLines(tx, row.id, input.lines, checked.lines);
        await audit(tx, {
          action: 'sales_return.created',
          entityType: 'sales_return',
          entityId: row.id,
          changes: created(await this.snapshot(tx, row, customer, checked.lines.length)),
        });
        if (input.post) await this.postAndLog(tx, row);
        return this.read(tx, row.id);
      });
    } catch (error) {
      throw overDeliveredRace(error);
    }
  }

  async update(id: string, input: UpdateSalesReturnInput): Promise<SalesReturn> {
    try {
      return await this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
        const before = await this.lockDraft(tx, id, input.version);
        const linesBefore = await this.linesOf(tx, id);
        const customerBefore = await this.customerOf(tx, before.customerId);
        const customer = await assertCustomer(tx, input.customerId, before.customerId);
        await assertWarehousesActive(tx, [
          { field: 'warehouseId', warehouseId: input.warehouseId },
        ]);
        const checked = await this.checkLines(tx, customer.id, input.lines, false);
        const [updated] = await tx
          .update(salesReturns)
          .set({
            date: input.date,
            customerId: customer.id,
            warehouseId: input.warehouseId,
            reason: input.reason,
            note: input.note,
            version: sql`${salesReturns.version} + 1`,
            updatedBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
          })
          .where(and(eq(salesReturns.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(salesReturns.id, id)))
          .returning();
        if (!updated) throw notFound('Sales return');
        await this.writeLines(tx, id, input.lines, checked.lines);
        await audit(tx, {
          action: 'sales_return.updated',
          entityType: 'sales_return',
          entityId: id,
          changes: diff(
            await this.snapshot(tx, before, customerBefore, linesBefore.length),
            await this.snapshot(tx, updated, customer, checked.lines.length),
          ),
        });
        if (input.post) await this.postAndLog(tx, updated);
        return this.read(tx, id);
      });
    } catch (error) {
      throw overDeliveredRace(error);
    }
  }

  remove(id: string, version: number): Promise<void> {
    return this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
      const before = await this.lockDraft(tx, id, version);
      const lines = await this.linesOf(tx, id);
      const customer = await this.customerOf(tx, before.customerId);
      // The lines go with it (ON DELETE CASCADE). A draft brought nothing back: nothing to undo.
      await tx
        .delete(salesReturns)
        .where(and(eq(salesReturns.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(salesReturns.id, id)));
      const snapshot = await this.snapshot(tx, before, customer, lines.length);
      await audit(tx, {
        action: 'sales_return.deleted',
        entityType: 'sales_return',
        entityId: id,
        changes: diff(
          snapshot,
          Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(snapshot).map((field) => [field, null])),
        ),
      });
    });
  }

  async post(id: string, version: number): Promise<SalesReturn> {
    try {
      return await this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
        const draft = await this.lockDraft(tx, id, version);
        await this.postAndLog(tx, draft);
        return this.read(tx, id);
      });
    } catch (error) {
      throw overDeliveredRace(error);
    }
  }
```

- **The usual shape of a document**: a list newest first with a keyset cursor, `create` and `update` that check,
  write, log and (with `post: true`) post in one transaction, and `remove` for a draft only. "Save and post" does both
  or nothing.
- **`update` keeps an archived customer** on a draft that already has it (`assertCustomer(…, before.customerId)`),
  like every 15b draft.
- **The race mapping wraps the whole transaction.** `create`, `update` and `post` can all post, so all three catch
  the database's last word after the rollback.

```ts
  // Every rule of a line the contract cannot check. A line from a challan: a line of a posted
  // challan of this customer, of the same item (in any of its units), with its batch, no more than
  // what left on it less what came back already, and only serial numbers that left on it. A line on
  // its own: an item of this workspace with an existing batch, like a stock line that goes out
  // (resolveLines in 'out' mode: an archived item can still come back). All problems at once, under
  // each line. lock: true when posting (the challans are locked FOR UPDATE, see challanLines()).
  private async checkLines(
    tx: Transaction,
    customerId: string,
    lines: readonly LineRefs[],
    lock: boolean,
  ): Promise<Checked> {
    const challans = await this.challanLines(
      tx,
      lines.flatMap((line) => (line.deliveryLineId === null ? [] : [line.deliveryLineId])),
      lock,
    );
    const challanOf = (line: LineRefs) =>
      line.deliveryLineId === null ? undefined : challans.get(line.deliveryLineId);

    const issues: LineIssue[] = [];
    lines.forEach((line, index) => {
      if (line.deliveryLineId === null) return;
      const challan = challanOf(line);
      if (
        challan?.customerId !== customerId ||
        challan.status !== 'posted' ||
        challan.variantId !== line.variantId
      ) {
        issues.push({
          path: linePath(index, 'deliveryLineId'),
          code: 'return_delivery_line_invalid',
        });
      }
    });
    if (issues.length > 0) throw linesError(issues);

    // A challan line's goods come back in its own batch: the form sends none (the contract refuses
    // one), and a stored draft line keeps the one written when it was saved
    const resolved = await resolveLines(
      tx,
      lines.map((line) => ({
        variantId: line.variantId,
        unitId: line.unitId,
        quantity: line.quantity,
        batchId: challanOf(line)?.batchId ?? line.batchId,
        serialNumbers: [...line.serialNumbers],
      })),
      'out',
      { lock },
    );

    resolved.forEach((line, index) => {
      const typed = lines[index];
      const challan = typed === undefined ? undefined : challanOf(typed);
      if (challan === undefined) return;
      const left = subtractQuantity(challan.baseQuantity, challan.returnedQuantity);
      if (compareQuantity(line.baseQuantity, left) > 0) {
        issues.push({ path: linePath(index, 'quantity'), code: 'return_over_delivered' });
      }
      const sent = new Set(challan.serialNumbers);
      if (line.serialNumbers.some((serial) => !sent.has(serial))) {
        issues.push({ path: linePath(index, 'serialNumbers'), code: 'return_serial_invalid' });
      }
    });
    if (issues.length > 0) throw linesError(issues);
    return { lines: resolved, challans };
  }

  // The challan lines some return lines name, with their challan's customer, status and
  // warehouse. lock: the challans are locked FOR UPDATE in id order first, then the lines are read,
  // so returned_quantity and invoiced are what the last posting committed. An invoice posting
  // locks the same challans (InvoicesService.challanLines), so a return and an invoice of one
  // challan line take turns: whichever is second sees the first.
  private async challanLines(
    tx: Transaction,
    ids: readonly string[],
    lock: boolean,
  ): Promise<Map<string, ChallanLine>> {
    const tenantId = getTenantId();
    if (ids.length === 0) return new Map();
    const owners = await tx
      .selectDistinct({ deliveryId: deliveryLines.deliveryId })
      .from(deliveryLines)
      .where(and(eq(deliveryLines.tenantId, tenantId), inArray(deliveryLines.id, [...ids])));
    const query = tx
      .select({
        id: deliveries.id,
        customerId: deliveries.customerId,
        status: deliveries.status,
        warehouseId: deliveries.warehouseId,
      })
      .from(deliveries)
      .where(
        and(
          eq(deliveries.tenantId, tenantId),
          inArray(
            deliveries.id,
            owners.map((owner) => owner.deliveryId),
          ),
        ),
      )
      .orderBy(asc(deliveries.id));
    const challans = lock ? await query.for('update') : await query;
    const byId = new Map(challans.map((challan) => [challan.id, challan]));
    const rows = await tx
      .select({
        id: deliveryLines.id,
        deliveryId: deliveryLines.deliveryId,
        variantId: deliveryLines.variantId,
        baseQuantity: deliveryLines.baseQuantity,
        returnedQuantity: deliveryLines.returnedQuantity,
        batchId: deliveryLines.batchId,
        serialNumbers: deliveryLines.serialNumbers,
        value: deliveryLines.value,
        invoiced: deliveryLines.invoiced,
        orderLineId: deliveryLines.orderLineId,
      })
      .from(deliveryLines)
      .where(and(eq(deliveryLines.tenantId, tenantId), inArray(deliveryLines.id, [...ids])));
    return new Map(
      rows.flatMap((row) => {
        const challan = byId.get(row.deliveryId);
        return challan === undefined
          ? []
          : [
              [
                row.id,
                {
                  ...row,
                  customerId: challan.customerId,
                  status: challan.status,
                  warehouseId: challan.warehouseId,
                },
              ] as const,
            ];
      }),
    );
  }
```

- **Three steps, in this order.** First the challan lines themselves: a posted challan of this customer, of the same
  item. If that fails, the check stops there: without a real challan line there is no batch to bring back, and the
  next step would add a confusing `stock_batch_required` to the real problem. Then `resolveLines()`, the stock
  documents' own check, which works out the base quantity. Then the two checks that need the base quantity: not more
  than left less what came back, and only serial numbers that left on that line.
- **`'out'` mode for a return that brings stock in.** It sounds backwards, but it is what a return needs. `'in'`
  asks for a lot number and makes a new batch; a return names an *existing* batch (the challan line's, or for a line
  on its own the one printed on the strip). `'in'` also refuses an archived item, and goods sold before an item was
  archived must still be able to come back.
- **A challan line's batch is the challan line's.** The form sends none (the contract refuses one), and a draft
  stores it when saved, so the draft page shows the lot.
- **A serial number that already came back** is in stock again, so the stock posting refuses it
  (`stock_serial_in_stock`). The check here only makes sure it left on *this* challan line.
- **`challanLines()` locks the challans when posting**, `FOR UPDATE`, in id order, and reads their lines after the
  lock. That is the lock 15c's invoice posting takes on the same challans. Saving a draft takes no lock: a draft
  holds nothing.

```ts
  // Posting, in the caller's transaction, in the order migration 0032 needs: the lines are written
  // while the return is still a draft (their values, and the invoice line of a billed challan
  // line), then the challan lines and the orders, and the return becomes posted last. A refused
  // step leaves nothing: no number used, no stock moved.
  private async postAndLog(tx: Transaction, draft: ReturnRow): Promise<void> {
    const tenantId = getTenantId();
    // Open period, and not in the future: tomorrow's goods cannot come back today
    await this.posting.assertDate(tx, draft.date);
    await assertWarehousesActive(tx, [{ field: 'warehouseId', warehouseId: draft.warehouseId }]);
    const stored = await this.linesOf(tx, draft.id);
    // Again, under the locks: another return may have brought the same goods back since the draft
    // was saved, or an invoice may have billed them
    const { lines, challans } = await this.checkLines(tx, draft.customerId, stored, true);
    const challanOf = (index: number) => {
      const id = stored[index]?.deliveryLineId ?? null;
      return id === null ? undefined : challans.get(id);
    };

    // Not billed yet, and from an order: the order can deliver them again (you chose this)
    const unbilled = lines.flatMap((line, index) => {
      const challan = challanOf(index);
      return challan === undefined || challan.invoiced || challan.orderLineId === null
        ? []
        : [{ orderLineId: challan.orderLineId, quantity: line.baseQuantity }];
    });
    const orders = await this.lockOrders(
      tx,
      unbilled.map((line) => line.orderLineId),
    );
    // Billed already: a credit note gives the money back for this invoice line
    const billing = await this.billingOf(
      tx,
      [...challans.values()].filter((challan) => challan.invoiced).map((challan) => challan.id),
    );

    const number = await this.numbering.next(tx, 'sales.return', draft.date);
    let values: string[];
    try {
      values = await this.posting.post(tx, {
        date: draft.date,
        kind: 'sales_return',
        direction: 'in',
        documentId: draft.id,
        documentNumber: number,
        moves: lines.map((line, index) => {
          const challan = challanOf(index);
          return {
            line: index,
            warehouseId: draft.warehouseId,
            variant: line.variant,
            batchId: line.batchId,
            quantity: line.baseQuantity,
            serialNumbers: line.serialNumbers,
            // A challan line's cost; a line on its own at the average cost (null)
            value: challan === undefined ? null : returnValue(challan, line.baseQuantity),
          };
        }),
      });
    } catch (error) {
      noCostError(error);
    }

    // Still a draft here: the lines may change, and take their values and their billing
    await this.writeLines(tx, draft.id, stored, lines, {
      values,
      billing: stored.map((line) =>
        line.deliveryLineId === null ? null : (billing.get(line.deliveryLineId) ?? null),
      ),
    });
    // What came back, on each challan line, in id order (the order every posting locks rows in).
    // Only up: migration 0032 refuses anything else on a posted challan's line.
    const back = lines
      .flatMap((line, index) => {
        const challan = challanOf(index);
        return challan === undefined ? [] : [{ id: challan.id, quantity: line.baseQuantity }];
      })
      .toSorted((a, b) => a.id.localeCompare(b.id));
    for (const line of back) {
      await tx
        .update(deliveryLines)
        .set({
          returnedQuantity: sql`${deliveryLines.returnedQuantity} + ${line.quantity}::numeric`,
        })
        .where(and(eq(deliveryLines.tenantId, tenantId), eq(deliveryLines.id, line.id)));
    }
    await this.returnOnOrders(tx, orders, unbilled);
    await tx
      .update(salesReturns)
      .set({
        status: 'posted',
        number,
        postedAt: new Date(),
        postedBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
        version: sql`${salesReturns.version} + 1`,
        updatedBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
      })
      .where(and(eq(salesReturns.tenantId, tenantId), eq(salesReturns.id, draft.id)));

    // The books (you chose this): Dr Inventory / Cr Cost of goods sold, at what the goods cost
    const entry = await this.books.salesReturn(
      tx,
      { id: draft.id, number, date: draft.date },
      {
        warehouseId: draft.warehouseId,
        costs: values.map((value, index) => ({
          warehouseId: challanOf(index)?.warehouseId ?? draft.warehouseId,
          value,
        })),
      },
    );
    await audit(tx, {
      action: 'sales_return.posted',
      entityType: 'sales_return',
      entityId: draft.id,
      changes: created({ number, entry: entry?.number ?? null }),
    });
  }
```

- **The order of posting is the order migration 0032 needs.** The return's lines can change only while it is a
  draft, so they are written with their values and their billing first. Then the challan lines and the orders, and
  the return becomes posted last. A refusal at any step rolls everything back: no number taken, no stock moved.
- **The date first.** `assertDate()` (step 13) refuses a closed period, and a date in the future: tomorrow's goods
  cannot come back today.
- **The checks run again under the locks.** Another return may have brought the same goods back since the draft was
  saved, or an invoice may have billed them.
- **Not billed, from an order** (`unbilled`): these go back onto the order (decision 8). **Billed**: the posting
  stores the invoice line that billed the challan line (`billingOf()`), and never changes it again. That is what makes
  `billed` on the return line a fact about the moment of posting: an invoice posted later bills less instead
  (`billableQuantity`), and does not turn this return into a credited one.
- **The stock comes in with a value for a challan line** (`returnValue()`), and with `null` for a line on its own,
  which `StockPostingService` prices at the average cost at that moment, like any stock coming in without a cost.
- **`returned_quantity` grows in id order**, the order every posting locks rows in. The guard of 0032 lets it only
  grow.
- **The books, then the audit row.** The entry's number goes into `sales_return.posted`, like a challan's.

```ts
  // The orders behind some order lines, locked FOR UPDATE in id order (after the challans, the
  // order every posting takes them in): a delivery of the same order waits, then sees what came
  // back. Returns order id → its status.
  private async lockOrders(
    tx: Transaction,
    orderLineIds: readonly string[],
  ): Promise<Map<string, string>> {
    const tenantId = getTenantId();
    if (orderLineIds.length === 0) return new Map();
    const owners = await tx
      .selectDistinct({ orderId: salesOrderLines.orderId })
      .from(salesOrderLines)
      .where(
        and(eq(salesOrderLines.tenantId, tenantId), inArray(salesOrderLines.id, [...orderLineIds])),
      );
    const rows = await tx
      .select({ id: salesOrders.id, status: salesOrders.status })
      .from(salesOrders)
      .where(
        and(
          eq(salesOrders.tenantId, tenantId),
          inArray(
            salesOrders.id,
            owners.map((owner) => owner.orderId),
          ),
        ),
      )
      .orderBy(asc(salesOrders.id))
      .for('update');
    return new Map(rows.map((row) => [row.id, row.status]));
  }

  // What came back before it was billed goes back onto its order lines (you chose this): their
  // delivered quantity comes down, and a delivered order is confirmed again, so a replacement can go
  // out on it or it can be closed. A confirmed order gets a new version (its page shows old
  // delivered quantities). A closed order keeps its status and its version: migration 0028 freezes
  // a closed order's header, and 0032 lets only its lines' delivered quantity come down.
  private async returnOnOrders(
    tx: Transaction,
    orders: ReadonlyMap<string, string>,
    lines: readonly { orderLineId: string; quantity: string }[],
  ): Promise<void> {
    const tenantId = getTenantId();
    const byOrderLine = new Map<string, string[]>();
    for (const line of lines) {
      byOrderLine.set(line.orderLineId, [
        ...(byOrderLine.get(line.orderLineId) ?? []),
        line.quantity,
      ]);
    }
    for (const [orderLineId, quantities] of byOrderLine) {
      await tx
        .update(salesOrderLines)
        .set({
          deliveredQuantity: sql`${salesOrderLines.deliveredQuantity} - ${sumQuantity(quantities)}::numeric`,
        })
        .where(and(eq(salesOrderLines.tenantId, tenantId), eq(salesOrderLines.id, orderLineId)));
    }
    for (const [orderId, status] of orders) {
      if (status !== 'delivered' && status !== 'confirmed') continue;
      await tx
        .update(salesOrders)
        .set({
          status: 'confirmed',
          version: sql`${salesOrders.version} + 1`,
          updatedBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
        })
        .where(and(eq(salesOrders.tenantId, tenantId), eq(salesOrders.id, orderId)));
    }
  }

  // Challan line → the posted invoice line that billed it. Read under the challans' lock, so the
  // `invoiced` flag and this agree.
  private async billingOf(
    tx: Transaction,
    deliveryLineIds: readonly string[],
  ): Promise<Map<string, Billing>> {
    if (deliveryLineIds.length === 0) return new Map();
    const rows = await tx
      .select({
        deliveryLineId: invoiceLines.deliveryLineId,
        invoiceId: invoiceLines.invoiceId,
        invoiceLineId: invoiceLines.id,
      })
      .from(invoiceLines)
      .innerJoin(
        invoices,
        and(eq(invoices.tenantId, invoiceLines.tenantId), eq(invoices.id, invoiceLines.invoiceId)),
      )
      .where(
        and(
          eq(invoiceLines.tenantId, getTenantId()),
          inArray(invoiceLines.deliveryLineId, [...deliveryLineIds]),
          eq(invoices.status, 'posted'),
        ),
      );
    const billing = new Map(
      rows.flatMap((row) =>
        row.deliveryLineId === null
          ? []
          : [[row.deliveryLineId, { invoiceId: row.invoiceId, invoiceLineId: row.invoiceLineId }]],
      ),
    );
    for (const id of deliveryLineIds) {
      if (!billing.has(id))
        throw new Error(`Invoiced challan line ${id} has no posted invoice line`);
    }
    return billing;
  }

  // The lines in the order they were written. posted: set when posting has priced them and found
  // the invoice lines that billed them.
  private async writeLines(
    tx: Transaction,
    returnId: string,
    typed: readonly LineRefs[],
    lines: readonly ResolvedLine[],
    posted?: { values: readonly string[]; billing: readonly (Billing | null)[] },
  ): Promise<void> {
    const tenantId = getTenantId();
    await tx
      .delete(salesReturnLines)
      .where(and(eq(salesReturnLines.tenantId, tenantId), eq(salesReturnLines.returnId, returnId)));
    await tx.insert(salesReturnLines).values(
      lines.map((line, index) => ({
        tenantId,
        returnId,
        lineNo: index + 1,
        productId: line.variant.productId,
        variantId: line.variant.variantId,
        unitId: line.unitId,
        quantity: line.quantity,
        factor: line.factor,
        baseQuantity: line.baseQuantity,
        batchId: line.batchId,
        serialNumbers: line.serialNumbers,
        deliveryLineId: typed[index]?.deliveryLineId ?? null,
        invoiceId: posted?.billing[index]?.invoiceId ?? null,
        invoiceLineId: posted?.billing[index]?.invoiceLineId ?? null,
        value: posted?.values[index] ?? null,
      })),
    );
  }
```

- **`lockOrders()`** comes after the challans, so a delivery of the same order (which locks the order) and this
  return never wait for each other in a circle.
- **`returnOnOrders()`: what you chose for a return before invoicing.** The order lines' delivered quantity comes
  down. A *delivered* order is confirmed again, so a replacement can go out on the same order, or the order is closed.
  A *confirmed* order gets a new version: its page shows old delivered quantities, and its next action must reload.
  A *closed* order is left alone: it stays closed (nothing more will be delivered on it), and migration 0028 freezes
  a closed order's header, so even its version cannot change. 0032 lets its lines' delivered quantity come down, and
  that is all that changes. The credit limit's "still to bill" of a closed order counts what it delivered, so it goes
  down with the return, as it should.
- **`billingOf()`** throws a plain `Error` if an invoiced challan line has no posted invoice line. That can only be a
  bug: `invoiced` is set by the invoice's posting, in the same transaction that posts the invoice.
- **`writeLines()`** deletes and inserts, like every document's lines. The line ids change on every save; nothing
  points at a draft's lines (a credit note line can only name a return line that an invoice line billed, which only a
  posting sets), so that is safe.

```ts
  // FOR UPDATE: two saves of one draft run one after the other, and a save never overlaps a post
  private async lockDraft(tx: Transaction, id: string, version: number): Promise<ReturnRow> {
    const [row] = await tx
      .select()
      .from(salesReturns)
      .where(and(eq(salesReturns.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(salesReturns.id, id)))
      .for('update');
    if (!row) throw notFound('Sales return');
    if (row.status !== 'draft') throw notDraft();
    if (row.version !== version) throw versionConflict();
    return row;
  }

  private linesOf(tx: Transaction, returnId: string): Promise<LineRow[]> {
    return tx
      .select()
      .from(salesReturnLines)
      .where(
        and(eq(salesReturnLines.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(salesReturnLines.returnId, returnId)),
      )
      .orderBy(asc(salesReturnLines.lineNo));
  }

  private rows(tx: Transaction, where: SQL | undefined, limit: number) {
    return tx
      .select({
        salesReturn: salesReturns,
        customer: { id: parties.id, code: parties.code, name: parties.name },
        lineCount,
      })
      .from(salesReturns)
      .innerJoin(
        parties,
        and(eq(parties.tenantId, salesReturns.tenantId), eq(parties.id, salesReturns.customerId)),
      )
      .where(and(eq(salesReturns.tenantId, getTenantId()), where))
      .orderBy(desc(salesReturns.date), desc(salesReturns.id))
      .limit(limit);
  }

  private async read(tx: Transaction, id: string): Promise<SalesReturn> {
    const tenantId = getTenantId();
    const [found] = await this.rows(tx, eq(salesReturns.id, id), 1);
    if (!found) throw notFound('Sales return');
    const { salesReturn: row } = found;
    const lines = await this.linesOf(tx, id);
    const deliveryLineIds = lines.flatMap((line) =>
      line.deliveryLineId === null ? [] : [line.deliveryLineId],
    );
    const invoiceIds = [
      ...new Set(lines.flatMap((line) => (line.invoiceId === null ? [] : [line.invoiceId]))),
    ];
    const [canSee, entries, variants, batches, challans, billed, credits] = await Promise.all([
      this.access.canSee(),
      this.books.entriesOf(tx, id),
      loadVariants(
        tx,
        lines.map((line) => line.variantId),
      ),
      batchesOf(
        tx,
        lines.map((line) => line.batchId),
      ),
      deliveryLineIds.length === 0
        ? []
        : tx
            .select({ lineId: deliveryLines.id, id: deliveries.id, number: deliveries.number })
            .from(deliveryLines)
            .innerJoin(
              deliveries,
              and(
                eq(deliveries.tenantId, deliveryLines.tenantId),
                eq(deliveries.id, deliveryLines.deliveryId),
              ),
            )
            .where(
              and(eq(deliveryLines.tenantId, tenantId), inArray(deliveryLines.id, deliveryLineIds)),
            )
            .orderBy(asc(deliveries.number)),
      invoiceIds.length === 0
        ? []
        : tx
            .select({ id: invoices.id, number: invoices.number })
            .from(invoices)
            .where(and(eq(invoices.tenantId, tenantId), inArray(invoices.id, invoiceIds))),
      // Drafts too: a second credit note for the same goods is then easy to spot
      tx
```
