```ts
        .selectDistinct({ id: creditNotes.id, number: creditNotes.number })
        .from(creditNoteLines)
        .innerJoin(
          creditNotes,
          and(
            eq(creditNotes.tenantId, creditNoteLines.tenantId),
            eq(creditNotes.id, creditNoteLines.creditNoteId),
          ),
        )
        .innerJoin(
          salesReturnLines,
          and(
            eq(salesReturnLines.tenantId, creditNoteLines.tenantId),
            eq(salesReturnLines.id, creditNoteLines.returnLineId),
          ),
        )
        .where(and(eq(creditNoteLines.tenantId, tenantId), eq(salesReturnLines.returnId, id)))
        .orderBy(asc(creditNotes.number)),
    ]);
    const challanOf = new Map(challans.map((challan) => [challan.lineId, challan]));
    const invoiceNumber = new Map(billed.map((invoice) => [invoice.id, invoice.number]));
    return {
      ...toSummary(row, found.customer, found.lineCount),
      lines: lines.flatMap((line) => {
        const variant = variants.get(line.variantId);
        // The FK keeps the variant while a line points at it
        if (!variant) return [];
        return [
          {
            ...toStockLine(
              line,
              variant,
              line.batchId === null ? undefined : batches.get(line.batchId),
            ),
            deliveryLineId: line.deliveryLineId,
            deliveryNumber:
              line.deliveryLineId === null
                ? null
                : (challanOf.get(line.deliveryLineId)?.number ?? null),
            billed: line.invoiceLineId !== null,
            invoiceLineId: line.invoiceLineId,
            invoiceId: line.invoiceId,
            invoiceNumber:
              line.invoiceId === null ? null : (invoiceNumber.get(line.invoiceId) ?? null),
            creditedQuantity: line.creditedQuantity,
            // Worked out from the books: needs inventory.stock.value (step 14)
            value: canSee ? line.value : null,
          },
        ];
      }),
      // Each challan once, by number (the query sorted them)
      deliveries: [
        ...new Map(
          challans.map((challan) => [challan.id, { id: challan.id, number: challan.number }]),
        ).values(),
      ],
      creditNotes: credits,
      entry: entries[0] ?? null,
    };
  }

  private async customerOf(tx: Transaction, customerId: string): Promise<PartyRef> {
    const customer = (await customerRefs(tx, [customerId])).get(customerId);
    if (!customer) throw new Error(`Customer ${customerId} is missing`);
    return customer;
  }

  // What the audit log shows: the header and the size, not every line
  private async snapshot(tx: Transaction, row: ReturnRow, customer: PartyRef, lines: number) {
    const [warehouse] = await tx
      .select({ code: warehouses.code })
      .from(warehouses)
      .where(and(eq(warehouses.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(warehouses.id, row.warehouseId)));
    return {
      date: row.date,
      customer: customer.code,
      warehouse: warehouse?.code ?? null,
      reason: row.reason,
      lines,
    };
  }
}
```

- **`read()`** sends `billed` as "has an invoice line", with the invoice's number for the page's link.
- **`value` is hidden without `inventory.stock.value`**, like a challan's (step 14): it is worked out from the books.
- **`creditNotes` lists drafts too.** Two people writing a credit note for the same return at the same time would
  each think the other had not. With the draft listed, the second person sees it.
- **`deliveries`** lists each challan once, by number. The query sorts by number, and a `Map` keeps the order its
  keys were first added in.

### `sales/credit-notes.service.ts` (new)

```ts
import { Inject, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import {
  amountDueOf,
  compareMoney,
  compareQuantity,
  type CreditNote,
  type CreditNoteAllocationsInput,
  type CreditNoteInput,
  type CreditNoteStatus,
  type CreditNoteSummary,
  defaultLineDescription,
  documentTotals,
  type ErrorCode,
  fitsDecimals,
  isQuantity,
  isZeroMoney,
  lineAmounts,
  overAllocated,
  type PartyRef,
  type SalesLineInput,
  subtractMoney,
  subtractQuantity,
  sumMoney,
  sumQuantity,
  toBaseQuantity,
  type UpdateCreditNoteInput,
} from '@omnivo/contracts';
import {
  creditNoteAllocations,
  creditNoteLines,
  creditNotes,
  invoiceLines,
  invoices,
  parties,
  salesReturnLines,
  salesReturns,
} from '@omnivo/db';
import { and, asc, desc, eq, inArray, type SQL, sql } from 'drizzle-orm';
import { z } from 'zod';

import { audit, created, diff } from '../common/audit/audit.js';
import { isCheckViolation } from '../common/db/pg-errors.js';
import { AppError, notFound, versionConflict } from '../common/http/app-error.js';
import { decodeCursor, toPage } from '../common/pagination/cursor.js';
import { currentPrincipal, getTenantId } from '../common/tenant/tenant-context.js';
import type { Transaction, WithTenant } from '../common/tenant/with-tenant.js';
import { WITH_TENANT } from '../infra/tokens.js';
import { type LineIssue, linePath, linesError, loadVariants } from '../inventory/stock-lines.js';
import { assertPeriodOpen } from '../journal/period-lock.service.js';
import { NumberingService } from '../numbering/numbering.service.js';
import { type Allocation, allocationChanges, checkAllocations } from './allocations.js';
import { SalesBooksService } from './sales-books.service.js';
import {
  assertCustomer,
  customerRefs,
  type ResolvedSalesLine,
  salesLineValues,
  toSalesLine,
  withVariants,
} from './sales-lines.js';

type CreditNoteRow = typeof creditNotes.$inferSelect;
type CreditLineRow = typeof creditNoteLines.$inferSelect;

const cursorSchema = z.tuple([z.iso.date(), z.uuid()]);

// By the table's name: inside this subquery a bare "id" would be the line's own
const lineCount = sql<number>`(
  SELECT count(*)::int FROM credit_note_lines l
   WHERE l.tenant_id = credit_notes.tenant_id AND l.credit_note_id = credit_notes.id
)`;

// The invoice a credit note credits, as far as the credit note needs it
interface InvoiceInfo {
  id: string;
  number: string;
  date: string;
  customerId: string;
  branchId: string;
  pricesIncludeVat: boolean;
  total: string;
  amountPaid: string;
  amountCredited: string;
}

// What a line names, as the form sends it and as the database keeps it
interface LineRefs {
  invoiceLineId: string;
  returnLineId: string | null;
  unitId: string;
  quantity: string;
  description: string | null;
  unitPrice: string;
  discountType: SalesLineInput['discountType'];
  discount: string;
}

function notDraft(): AppError {
  return new AppError(
    409,
    'sales_not_draft',
    'Only a draft credit note can be changed. A posted one is final: write another one.',
  );
}

function invoiceInvalid(): AppError {
  return new AppError(409, 'credit_note_invoice_invalid', 'Pick a posted invoice.', {
    fieldErrors: { invoiceId: ['credit_note_invoice_invalid'] },
  });
}

function overAllocatedError(): AppError {
  return new AppError(
    409,
    'credit_note_over_allocated',
    'More is applied than the credit note has. Lower the amounts on the invoices.',
    { fieldErrors: { allocations: ['credit_note_over_allocated'] } },
  );
}

function toSummary(
  row: CreditNoteRow,
  customer: PartyRef,
  invoice: { id: string; number: string; date: string; branchId: string },
  lines: number,
): CreditNoteSummary {
  return {
    id: row.id,
    number: row.number,
    date: row.date,
    customer,
    invoice: { id: invoice.id, number: invoice.number, date: invoice.date },
    branchId: invoice.branchId,
    reason: row.reason,
    status: row.status,
    net: row.net,
    vat: row.vat,
    total: row.total,
    applied: row.applied,
    refunded: row.refunded,
    lineCount: lines,
    postedAt: row.postedAt?.toISOString() ?? null,
    version: row.version,
    updatedAt: row.updatedAt.toISOString(),
  };
}

// A stored line as the check reads it again when the draft is posted
function storedRefs(line: CreditLineRow): LineRefs {
  return {
    invoiceLineId: line.invoiceLineId,
    returnLineId: line.returnLineId,
    unitId: line.unitId,
    quantity: line.quantity,
    description: line.description,
    unitPrice: line.unitPrice,
    discountType: line.discountType,
    discount: line.discount,
  };
}

// The database's last word, if two writers got past the checks: the invoice locks make these
// unreachable in practice, but each still answers with the code the form knows. A line credited
// past what it charged (invoice_lines_credited_check, and invoices_credited_check for the whole
// invoice), a return line past what came back, an invoice settled past its total by receipts and
// credit notes together, or a credit note applied and paid back past its total.
function moneyRace(error: unknown): unknown {
  if (
    isCheckViolation(error, 'invoice_lines_credited_check') ||
    isCheckViolation(error, 'invoices_credited_check')
  ) {
    return new AppError(
      409,
      'credit_note_over_line',
      'Another credit note took back some of these lines first. Reload and try again.',
    );
  }
  if (isCheckViolation(error, 'sales_return_lines_credited_check')) {
    return new AppError(
      409,
      'credit_note_over_return',
      'Another credit note gave the money back for these goods first. Reload and try again.',
    );
  }
  if (isCheckViolation(error, 'invoices_paid_check')) {
    return new AppError(
      409,
      'credit_note_over_invoice',
      'A receipt or another credit note settled one of these invoices first. Reload and try again.',
    );
  }
  if (isCheckViolation(error, 'credit_notes_money_check')) return overAllocatedError();
  return error;
}
```

- **`InvoiceInfo`** is what a credit note needs of its invoice: the customer and the branch (both are the invoice's,
  15d.1), the price setting, the date (a credit note is not dated before it) and the money (what it still
  owes, for the first allocation).
- **`storedRefs()`** turns a stored line back into what `resolve()` reads, so posting runs the same check as saving.
- **`moneyRace()`** maps each check constraint of 15d.2 that guards a credit note's money to the code the form
  knows. The invoice lock makes all of them unreachable in practice; they are the last word if anything slipped past.

```ts
// Credit notes (step 15d): part or all of a posted invoice taken back. A draft is changed freely;
// "Post" numbers it, books the sale back, counts it on the invoice and the return lines it names,
// and applies its money to its own invoice. Afterwards only its money moves (allocate, and refunds).
@Injectable()
export class CreditNotesService {
  constructor(
    @Inject(WITH_TENANT) private readonly withTenant: WithTenant,
    private readonly numbering: NumberingService,
    private readonly books: SalesBooksService,
  ) {}

  list(query: {
    limit: number;
    cursor?: string | undefined;
    status?: CreditNoteStatus | undefined;
    customerId?: string | undefined;
    invoiceId?: string | undefined;
  }): Promise<{ items: CreditNoteSummary[]; nextCursor: string | null }> {
    const after = decodeCursor(query.cursor, cursorSchema);
    return this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
      const rows = await this.rows(
        tx,
        and(
          query.status === undefined ? undefined : eq(creditNotes.status, query.status),
          query.customerId === undefined ? undefined : eq(creditNotes.customerId, query.customerId),
          query.invoiceId === undefined ? undefined : eq(creditNotes.invoiceId, query.invoiceId),
          after === undefined
            ? undefined
            : sql`(${creditNotes.date}, ${creditNotes.id}) < (${after[0]}::date, ${after[1]}::uuid)`,
        ),
        query.limit + 1,
      );
      const page = toPage(rows, query.limit, (last) => [last.creditNote.date, last.creditNote.id]);
      return {
        items: page.items.map((row) =>
          toSummary(row.creditNote, row.customer, this.invoiceRef(row.invoice), row.lineCount),
        ),
        nextCursor: page.nextCursor,
      };
    });
  }

  get(id: string): Promise<CreditNote> {
    return this.withTenant((tx) => this.read(tx, id));
  }

  async create(input: CreditNoteInput): Promise<CreditNote> {
    try {
      return await this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
        const fields = await this.check(tx, input, null);
        const [row] = await tx
          .insert(creditNotes)
          .values({
            tenantId: getTenantId(),
            ...fields.header,
            createdBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
            updatedBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
          })
          .returning();
        if (!row) throw new Error('Credit note insert returned no row');
        await this.writeLines(tx, row, input.lines, fields.lines);
        await audit(tx, {
          action: 'credit_note.created',
          entityType: 'credit_note',
          entityId: row.id,
          changes: created(
            this.snapshot(row, fields.customer, fields.invoice, fields.lines.length),
          ),
        });
        if (input.post) await this.postAndLog(tx, row);
        return this.read(tx, row.id);
      });
    } catch (error) {
      throw moneyRace(error);
    }
  }

  async update(id: string, input: UpdateCreditNoteInput): Promise<CreditNote> {
    try {
      return await this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
        const before = await this.lockDraft(tx, id, input.version);
        const linesBefore = await this.linesOf(tx, id);
        const customerBefore = await this.customerOf(tx, before.customerId);
        const invoiceBefore = await this.invoiceOf(tx, before.invoiceId, null);
        const fields = await this.check(tx, input, before);
        const [updated] = await tx
          .update(creditNotes)
          .set({
            ...fields.header,
            version: sql`${creditNotes.version} + 1`,
            updatedBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
          })
          .where(and(eq(creditNotes.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(creditNotes.id, id)))
          .returning();
        if (!updated) throw notFound('Credit note');
        await this.writeLines(tx, updated, input.lines, fields.lines);
        await audit(tx, {
          action: 'credit_note.updated',
          entityType: 'credit_note',
          entityId: id,
          changes: diff(
            this.snapshot(before, customerBefore, invoiceBefore, linesBefore.length),
            this.snapshot(updated, fields.customer, fields.invoice, fields.lines.length),
          ),
        });
        if (input.post) await this.postAndLog(tx, updated);
        return this.read(tx, id);
      });
    } catch (error) {
      throw moneyRace(error);
    }
  }

  remove(id: string, version: number): Promise<void> {
    return this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
      const before = await this.lockDraft(tx, id, version);
      const lines = await this.linesOf(tx, id);
      const customer = await this.customerOf(tx, before.customerId);
      const invoice = await this.invoiceOf(tx, before.invoiceId, null);
      // The lines go with it (ON DELETE CASCADE). A draft took nothing back: nothing to undo.
      await tx
        .delete(creditNotes)
        .where(and(eq(creditNotes.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(creditNotes.id, id)));
      const snapshot = this.snapshot(before, customer, invoice, lines.length);
      await audit(tx, {
        action: 'credit_note.deleted',
        entityType: 'credit_note',
        entityId: id,
        changes: diff(
          snapshot,
          Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(snapshot).map((field) => [field, null])),
        ),
      });
    });
  }

  async post(id: string, version: number): Promise<CreditNote> {
    try {
      return await this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
        const draft = await this.lockDraft(tx, id, version);
        await this.postAndLog(tx, draft);
        return this.read(tx, id);
      });
    } catch (error) {
      throw moneyRace(error);
    }
  }

  // The whole list as the person left it, like a receipt's: what is left of the credit after its
  // own invoice moved to another invoice of the customer, or taken off to pay it back. Nothing in
  // the books changes, only what each invoice still owes.
  async allocate(id: string, input: CreditNoteAllocationsInput): Promise<CreditNote> {
    try {
      return await this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
        const row = await this.lockPosted(tx, id, input.version);
        // What refunds paid back is gone: only the rest can be applied
        if (overAllocated(subtractMoney(row.total, row.refunded), input.allocations)) {
          throw overAllocatedError();
        }
        const before = await this.allocationsOf(tx, id);
        await this.apply(tx, row, input.allocations);
        await tx
          .update(creditNotes)
          .set({ version: sql`${creditNotes.version} + 1`, updatedBy: currentPrincipal().userId })
          .where(and(eq(creditNotes.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(creditNotes.id, id)));
        await audit(tx, {
          action: 'credit_note.allocated',
          entityType: 'credit_note',
          entityId: id,
          changes: allocationChanges(before, await this.allocationsOf(tx, id)),
        });
        return this.read(tx, id);
      });
    } catch (error) {
      throw moneyRace(error);
    }
  }
```

- **The list joins the invoice**: every row shows its invoice's number and its branch (the credit note has no branch
  of its own, 15d.2).
- **`allocate`** is the receipt's `allocate` with two differences: it needs a *posted* credit note
  (`credit_note_not_posted`: a draft has no money yet), and its cap is `total − refunded`.

```ts
  // Every rule of a save the contract cannot check, and the header it writes. `before`: the draft
  // being changed (null for a new one); its customer stays usable after it was archived, like every
  // draft. The customer is always the invoice's.
  private async check(tx: Transaction, input: CreditNoteInput, before: CreditNoteRow | null) {
    const invoice = await this.invoiceOf(tx, input.invoiceId, null);
    const customer = await assertCustomer(tx, invoice.customerId, before?.customerId ?? null);
    this.assertDate(input.date, invoice);
    const lines = await this.resolve(tx, invoice, input.lines);
    return {
      invoice,
      customer,
      header: {
        date: input.date,
        customerId: invoice.customerId,
        invoiceId: invoice.id,
        reason: input.reason,
        note: input.note,
        ...documentTotals(lines.map((line) => line.amounts)),
      },
      lines,
    };
  }

  // A credit note is written for something the invoice sold, so it is not dated before it. The
  // 6-month VAT rule (creditNoteIsLate) is only a warning on the form: you chose not to block it.
  private assertDate(date: string, invoice: InvoiceInfo): void {
    if (date < invoice.date) {
      throw new AppError(
        409,
        'credit_note_date',
        'A credit note cannot be dated before its invoice.',
        { fieldErrors: { date: ['credit_note_date'] } },
      );
    }
  }

  // The lines checked against the invoice and the returns they name, and worked out like the
  // invoice's lines: the invoice line's item, its VAT snapshot (VAT goes back at the rate it was
  // charged, even if the rate changed or was archived since) and the invoice's price setting, so
  // crediting a line in full gives back exactly what it charged. The caps: no line more than its
  // invoice line's quantity; the lines on one invoice line no more money than it charged less what
  // posted credit notes took back already (a price cut on all 100 pcs and a later return of 10 can
  // both be credited, up to what was billed); a return line's goods once. Drafts hold nothing, so
  // posting checks again under the invoice's lock. All problems at once, under each line.
  private async resolve(
    tx: Transaction,
    invoice: InvoiceInfo,
    lines: readonly LineRefs[],
  ): Promise<ResolvedSalesLine[]> {
    const tenantId = getTenantId();
    const invoiceLineRows = await tx
      .select()
      .from(invoiceLines)
      .where(and(eq(invoiceLines.tenantId, tenantId), eq(invoiceLines.invoiceId, invoice.id)));
    const invoiceLine = new Map(invoiceLineRows.map((row) => [row.id, row]));
    const variants = await loadVariants(
      tx,
      invoiceLineRows.map((row) => row.variantId),
    );
    const returnLineIds = lines.flatMap((line) =>
      line.returnLineId === null ? [] : [line.returnLineId],
    );
    const returnLineRows =
      returnLineIds.length === 0
        ? []
        : await tx
            .select({
              id: salesReturnLines.id,
              invoiceLineId: salesReturnLines.invoiceLineId,
              baseQuantity: salesReturnLines.baseQuantity,
              creditedQuantity: salesReturnLines.creditedQuantity,
              status: salesReturns.status,
            })
            .from(salesReturnLines)
            .innerJoin(
              salesReturns,
              and(
                eq(salesReturns.tenantId, salesReturnLines.tenantId),
                eq(salesReturns.id, salesReturnLines.returnId),
              ),
            )
            .where(
              and(
                eq(salesReturnLines.tenantId, tenantId),
                inArray(salesReturnLines.id, returnLineIds),
              ),
            );
    const returnLine = new Map(returnLineRows.map((row) => [row.id, row]));

    const issues: LineIssue[] = [];
    const resolved: ResolvedSalesLine[] = [];
    lines.forEach((line, index) => {
      const at = (field: string, code: ErrorCode) => {
        issues.push({ path: linePath(index, field), code });
      };
      const billed = invoiceLine.get(line.invoiceLineId);
      const variant = billed === undefined ? undefined : variants.get(billed.variantId);
      if (billed === undefined || variant === undefined) {
        at('invoiceLineId', 'credit_note_line_invalid');
        return;
      }
      // Any unit of the item: 3 strips back from a line of 2 boxes
      const unit =
        line.unitId === variant.baseUnitId
          ? { factor: '1', decimals: variant.baseDecimals }
          : variant.units.find((pack) => pack.unitId === line.unitId);
      if (unit === undefined) {
        at('unitId', 'stock_unit_invalid');
        return;
      }
      if (!fitsDecimals(line.quantity, unit.decimals)) {
        at('quantity', 'stock_quantity_decimals');
        return;
      }
      const baseQuantity = toBaseQuantity(line.quantity, unit.factor, variant.baseDecimals);
      if (!isQuantity(baseQuantity)) {
        at('quantity', 'quantity_format');
        return;
      }
      if (compareQuantity(baseQuantity, billed.baseQuantity) > 0) {
        at('quantity', 'credit_note_over_quantity');
      }
      if (line.returnLineId !== null) {
        const back = returnLine.get(line.returnLineId);
        // The return line this invoice line billed (its invoice_line_id), on a posted return
        if (back?.invoiceLineId !== billed.id || back.status !== 'posted') {
          at('returnLineId', 'credit_note_return_invalid');
        } else if (
          compareQuantity(
            baseQuantity,
            subtractQuantity(back.baseQuantity, back.creditedQuantity),
          ) > 0
        ) {
          at('quantity', 'credit_note_over_return');
        }
      }
      resolved.push({
        variant,
        unitId: line.unitId,
        quantity: line.quantity,
        factor: unit.factor,
        baseQuantity,
        description: line.description ?? defaultLineDescription(variant),
        unitPrice: line.unitPrice,
        discountType: line.discountType,
        discount: line.discount,
        taxRate: {
          id: billed.taxRateId,
          name: billed.taxRateName,
          kind: billed.taxRateKind,
          rate: billed.taxRate,
        },
        // The same function the form totals with, at the invoice's setting
        amounts: lineAmounts(
          {
            quantity: line.quantity,
            unitPrice: line.unitPrice,
            discountType: line.discountType,
            discount: line.discount,
            rate: billed.taxRate,
          },
          invoice.pricesIncludeVat,
        ),
      });
    });
    if (issues.length > 0) throw linesError(issues);

    // The money on each invoice line, all of this credit note's lines on it together
    const byInvoiceLine = new Map<string, string[]>();
    resolved.forEach((line, index) => {
      const id = lines[index]?.invoiceLineId;
      if (id === undefined) return;
      byInvoiceLine.set(id, [...(byInvoiceLine.get(id) ?? []), line.amounts.total]);
    });
    for (const [id, totals] of byInvoiceLine) {
      const billed = invoiceLine.get(id);
      if (billed === undefined) continue;
      const left = subtractMoney(billed.total, billed.credited);
      if (compareMoney(sumMoney(totals), left) <= 0) continue;
      // Under every line that takes from it: the person decides which one to lower
      lines.forEach((line, index) => {
        if (line.invoiceLineId === id) {
          issues.push({ path: linePath(index, 'unitPrice'), code: 'credit_note_over_line' });
        }
      });
    }
    if (issues.length > 0) throw linesError(issues);
    return resolved;
  }
```

- **The customer is always the invoice's.** The form does not send one, and the foreign key of 15d.2 would refuse
  any other. A draft keeps a customer archived since, like every draft; posting checks again without that exception.
- **`credit_note_date`.** A credit note dated before its invoice would take back a sale that did not exist yet. The
  6-month VAT rule is only a warning on the form (decision 6), so it is not checked here.
- **Why not `resolveSalesLines()`.** It reads each VAT rate from the `tax_rates` table *now*. A credit note must take
  VAT back at the rate the invoice *charged*: if the rate was changed or archived since, the Mushak 6.7 would no
  longer match the 6.3. So `resolve()` uses the invoice line's own snapshot (name, kind, rate), the invoice's item and
  the invoice's price setting. Crediting a line in full then gives back exactly what it charged, to the paisa.
- **Any unit of the item**: 3 strips back from a line billed in boxes. An unknown unit is `stock_unit_invalid` under
  the unit, like on every line.
- **The three caps.** No line more than its invoice line's quantity (`credit_note_over_quantity`). The lines on one
  invoice line no more *money* than it charged less what posted credit notes took back (`credit_note_over_line`): a
  cap on money, not quantity, so a price cut of ৳2 on all 100 pcs and a later return of 10 can both be credited, up to
  what was billed. And a return line's goods only once (`credit_note_over_return`), and only a return line this
  invoice line billed, on a posted return (`credit_note_return_invalid`).
- **The money cap goes under every line on that invoice line**, under the price, like `delivery_over_order` (15b):
  the person decides which line to lower.
- **Drafts hold nothing.** Two drafts may each credit the whole line; posting checks again under the invoice's lock,
  and the second one is refused.

```ts
  // Posting, in the caller's transaction. The invoice is locked first: two credit notes of one
  // invoice post one after the other, and the second sees what the first took back (every return
  // line belongs to one invoice line, so this lock covers the return lines too). FOR NO KEY UPDATE:
  // the draft's insert took a KEY SHARE lock on the invoice (credit_notes_invoice_fk), in this
  // transaction and in every other one saving a credit note for it. FOR UPDATE conflicts with
  // KEY SHARE, so two of them would each wait for the other (a deadlock, a 500); NO KEY UPDATE
  // does not, and two of them still take turns. The sums go up in the order migration 0032
  // allows (lines while the credit note is a draft, the header posted, then the allocation, which
  // a draft cannot have). A refused step leaves nothing.
  private async postAndLog(tx: Transaction, draft: CreditNoteRow): Promise<void> {
    const tenantId = getTenantId();
    // The date first: a closed period refuses before anything is locked
    await assertPeriodOpen(tx, draft.date);
    const invoice = await this.invoiceOf(tx, draft.invoiceId, 'no key update');
    // Active now: the journal will not book a receivable line for an archived customer
    await assertCustomer(tx, draft.customerId);
    this.assertDate(draft.date, invoice);
    const stored = await this.linesOf(tx, draft.id);
    // Again, under the lock: another credit note may have taken back the same lines since
    const lines = await this.resolve(tx, invoice, stored.map(storedRefs));
    const number = await this.numbering.next(tx, 'sales.credit_note', draft.date);

    // What this credit note takes back, on the invoice's lines and its return lines. Only up:
    // migration 0032 refuses anything else on a posted invoice or a posted return.
    const credited = new Map<string, string[]>();
    const returned = new Map<string, string[]>();
    stored.forEach((line, index) => {
      const amounts = lines[index];
      if (amounts === undefined) return;
      credited.set(line.invoiceLineId, [
        ...(credited.get(line.invoiceLineId) ?? []),
        amounts.amounts.total,
      ]);
      if (line.returnLineId !== null) {
        returned.set(line.returnLineId, [
          ...(returned.get(line.returnLineId) ?? []),
          amounts.baseQuantity,
        ]);
      }
    });
    for (const [id, totals] of [...credited].toSorted(([a], [b]) => a.localeCompare(b))) {
      const total = sumMoney(totals);
      if (isZeroMoney(total)) continue;
      await tx
        .update(invoiceLines)
        .set({ credited: sql`${invoiceLines.credited} + ${total}::numeric` })
        .where(and(eq(invoiceLines.tenantId, tenantId), eq(invoiceLines.id, id)));
    }
    for (const [id, quantities] of [...returned].toSorted(([a], [b]) => a.localeCompare(b))) {
      await tx
        .update(salesReturnLines)
        .set({
          creditedQuantity: sql`${salesReturnLines.creditedQuantity} + ${sumQuantity(quantities)}::numeric`,
        })
        .where(and(eq(salesReturnLines.tenantId, tenantId), eq(salesReturnLines.id, id)));
    }
    // The invoice keeps its version: migration 0032 lets a posted invoice change only its money,
    // and no invoice action decides anything on its credited total
    if (!isZeroMoney(draft.total)) {
      await tx
        .update(invoices)
        .set({ creditNoteTotal: sql`${invoices.creditNoteTotal} + ${draft.total}::numeric` })
        .where(and(eq(invoices.tenantId, tenantId), eq(invoices.id, invoice.id)));
    }

    // The books: the sale back, on the invoice's branch
    const entry = await this.books.creditNote(
      tx,
      { id: draft.id, number, date: draft.date },
      {
        customerId: draft.customerId,
        branchId: invoice.branchId,
        net: draft.net,
        vat: draft.vat,
        total: draft.total,
      },
    );
    const [posted] = await tx
      .update(creditNotes)
      .set({
        status: 'posted',
        number,
        postedAt: new Date(),
        postedBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
        version: sql`${creditNotes.version} + 1`,
        updatedBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
      })
      .where(and(eq(creditNotes.tenantId, tenantId), eq(creditNotes.id, draft.id)))
      .returning();
    if (!posted) throw notFound('Credit note');

    // Its money on its own invoice first (you chose this), up to what the invoice still owes; the
    // rest is the customer's advance. Read under the invoice's lock.
    const due = amountDueOf(invoice);
    const applied = compareMoney(draft.total, due) <= 0 ? draft.total : due;
    if (compareMoney(applied, '0') > 0) {
      await this.apply(tx, posted, [{ invoiceId: invoice.id, amount: applied }]);
    }
    await audit(tx, {
      action: 'credit_note.posted',
      entityType: 'credit_note',
      entityId: draft.id,
      changes: created({ number, entry: entry?.number ?? null, applied }),
    });
  }

  // Replaces the credit note's allocations with `wanted`, once checkAllocations() has locked every
  // invoice involved and checked each row. invoices.amount_credited and credit_notes.applied are
  // not written here: the allocations' trigger keeps them (migration 0032).
  private async apply(
    tx: Transaction,
    creditNote: CreditNoteRow,
    wanted: readonly Allocation[],
  ): Promise<void> {
    const tenantId = getTenantId();
    const current = await tx
      .select({
        invoiceId: creditNoteAllocations.invoiceId,
        amount: creditNoteAllocations.amount,
      })
      .from(creditNoteAllocations)
      .where(
        and(
          eq(creditNoteAllocations.tenantId, tenantId),
          eq(creditNoteAllocations.creditNoteId, creditNote.id),
        ),
      );
    await checkAllocations(tx, {
      customerId: creditNote.customerId,
      current,
      wanted,
      errors: { invoice: 'credit_note_allocation_invalid', over: 'credit_note_over_invoice' },
    });
    await tx
      .delete(creditNoteAllocations)
      .where(
        and(
          eq(creditNoteAllocations.tenantId, tenantId),
          eq(creditNoteAllocations.creditNoteId, creditNote.id),
        ),
      );
    if (wanted.length === 0) return;
    await tx.insert(creditNoteAllocations).values(
      wanted.map((allocation) => ({
        tenantId,
        creditNoteId: creditNote.id,
        customerId: creditNote.customerId,
        invoiceId: allocation.invoiceId,
        amount: allocation.amount,
      })),
    );
  }
```

- **The invoice is locked first.** Two credit notes of one invoice post one after the other, and the second sees
  what the first took back. Every return line belongs to one invoice line, so this one lock also covers the return
  lines' `credited_quantity`.
- **`FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, not `FOR UPDATE`.** By the time a credit note posts, its own insert has taken a `KEY SHARE`
  lock on the invoice (the foreign key), and so has any other credit note being saved for it. With `FOR UPDATE`, each
  would wait for the other's `KEY SHARE`: a deadlock, which Postgres ends by failing one of them with a 500. `FOR NO
  KEY UPDATE` does not wait for `KEY SHARE`, and two of them still wait for each other, which is all the lock is for.
  `checkAllocations()` locks the same invoice again for the first allocation, so it uses the same lock (above).
- **The counters only grow, and only when there is something to add.** The guards of 0032 accept a change to
  `invoice_lines.credited` only when the new value is *bigger*. A line of ৳0 (a free item credited at ৳0) would write
  the same value, and the guard would refuse it, so zero amounts are skipped.
- **The invoice keeps its version.** 0032 lets a posted invoice change only its money, and no action on the invoice
  decides anything on its credited total.
- **The books before the header**, then the header becomes posted, and only then the money is applied: a draft
  cannot have allocations (`credit_notes_money_check`).
- **Its own invoice first** (decision 4): `min(total, due)`, where `due` was read under the invoice's lock, before
  anything here touched it. The rest is the customer's advance: it shows as unapplied money, ready for a later
  invoice or a refund.

```ts
  // The invoice of a credit note: a posted invoice of this workspace. lock: 'no key update' when
  // posting (see postAndLog), null to read it
  private async invoiceOf(
    tx: Transaction,
    invoiceId: string,
    lock: 'no key update' | null,
  ): Promise<InvoiceInfo> {
    const query = tx
      .select({
        id: invoices.id,
        number: invoices.number,
        date: invoices.date,
        customerId: invoices.customerId,
        branchId: invoices.branchId,
        status: invoices.status,
        pricesIncludeVat: invoices.pricesIncludeVat,
        total: invoices.total,
        amountPaid: invoices.amountPaid,
        amountCredited: invoices.amountCredited,
      })
      .from(invoices)
      .where(and(eq(invoices.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(invoices.id, invoiceId)));
    const [row] = lock === null ? await query : await query.for(lock);
    // A posted invoice always has its number; the check narrows it for TypeScript
    if (row?.status !== 'posted' || row.number === null) throw invoiceInvalid();
    return { ...row, number: row.number };
  }

  // The lines as typed, with what the check found: the invoice line's item and VAT snapshot
  private async writeLines(
    tx: Transaction,
    creditNote: CreditNoteRow,
    typed: readonly LineRefs[],
    lines: readonly ResolvedSalesLine[],
  ): Promise<void> {
    const tenantId = getTenantId();
    await tx
      .delete(creditNoteLines)
      .where(
        and(
          eq(creditNoteLines.tenantId, tenantId),
          eq(creditNoteLines.creditNoteId, creditNote.id),
        ),
      );
    await tx.insert(creditNoteLines).values(
      lines.flatMap((line, index) => {
        const refs = typed[index];
        if (refs === undefined) return [];
        return [
          {
            ...salesLineValues(line, index),
            creditNoteId: creditNote.id,
            invoiceId: creditNote.invoiceId,
            invoiceLineId: refs.invoiceLineId,
            returnLineId: refs.returnLineId,
          },
        ];
      }),
    );
  }

  // FOR UPDATE: two saves of one draft run one after the other, and a save never overlaps a post
  private async lockDraft(tx: Transaction, id: string, version: number): Promise<CreditNoteRow> {
    const row = await this.lockRow(tx, id);
    if (row.status !== 'draft') throw notDraft();
    if (row.version !== version) throw versionConflict();
    return row;
  }

  // FOR UPDATE: an allocate and a refund of one credit note take turns (RefundsService locks it
  // too). A draft has no money to apply yet.
  private async lockPosted(tx: Transaction, id: string, version: number): Promise<CreditNoteRow> {
    const row = await this.lockRow(tx, id);
    if (row.status !== 'posted') {
      throw new AppError(
        409,
        'credit_note_not_posted',
        'Post the credit note before applying its money.',
      );
    }
    if (row.version !== version) throw versionConflict();
    return row;
  }

  private async lockRow(tx: Transaction, id: string): Promise<CreditNoteRow> {
    const [row] = await tx
      .select()
      .from(creditNotes)
      .where(and(eq(creditNotes.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(creditNotes.id, id)))
      .for('update');
    if (!row) throw notFound('Credit note');
    return row;
  }

  private linesOf(tx: Transaction, creditNoteId: string): Promise<CreditLineRow[]> {
    return tx
      .select()
      .from(creditNoteLines)
      .where(
        and(
          eq(creditNoteLines.tenantId, getTenantId()),
          eq(creditNoteLines.creditNoteId, creditNoteId),
        ),
      )
      .orderBy(asc(creditNoteLines.lineNo));
  }

  // The invoices its money is applied to, oldest due date first, like a receipt's
  private allocationsOf(tx: Transaction, creditNoteId: string) {
    return tx
      .select({
        invoiceId: invoices.id,
        invoiceNumber: invoices.number,
        invoiceDate: invoices.date,
        dueDate: invoices.dueDate,
        invoiceTotal: invoices.total,
        amount: creditNoteAllocations.amount,
      })
      .from(creditNoteAllocations)
      .innerJoin(
        invoices,
        and(
          eq(invoices.tenantId, creditNoteAllocations.tenantId),
          eq(invoices.id, creditNoteAllocations.invoiceId),
        ),
      )
      .where(
        and(
          eq(creditNoteAllocations.tenantId, getTenantId()),
          eq(creditNoteAllocations.creditNoteId, creditNoteId),
        ),
      )
      .orderBy(asc(invoices.dueDate), asc(invoices.id));
  }

  private rows(tx: Transaction, where: SQL | undefined, limit: number) {
    return tx
      .select({
        creditNote: creditNotes,
        customer: { id: parties.id, code: parties.code, name: parties.name },
        invoice: {
          id: invoices.id,
          number: invoices.number,
          date: invoices.date,
          branchId: invoices.branchId,
          pricesIncludeVat: invoices.pricesIncludeVat,
        },
        lineCount,
      })
      .from(creditNotes)
      .innerJoin(
        parties,
        and(eq(parties.tenantId, creditNotes.tenantId), eq(parties.id, creditNotes.customerId)),
      )
      .innerJoin(
        invoices,
        and(eq(invoices.tenantId, creditNotes.tenantId), eq(invoices.id, creditNotes.invoiceId)),
      )
      .where(and(eq(creditNotes.tenantId, getTenantId()), where))
      .orderBy(desc(creditNotes.date), desc(creditNotes.id))
      .limit(limit);
  }

  // The invoice of a listed credit note. Only a posted invoice can be credited, and a posted invoice
  // is never changed back, so it always has its number.
  private invoiceRef(invoice: {
    id: string;
    number: string | null;
    date: string;
    branchId: string;
  }) {
    if (invoice.number === null) throw new Error(`Credited invoice ${invoice.id} has no number`);
    return { ...invoice, number: invoice.number };
  }

  private async read(tx: Transaction, id: string): Promise<CreditNote> {
    const tenantId = getTenantId();
    const [found] = await this.rows(tx, eq(creditNotes.id, id), 1);
    if (!found) throw notFound('Credit note');
    const { creditNote: row } = found;
    const lines = await withVariants(tx, await this.linesOf(tx, id));
    const returnLineIds = lines.flatMap(({ row: line }) =>
      line.returnLineId === null ? [] : [line.returnLineId],
    );
    const [returns, allocations, entry] = await Promise.all([
      returnLineIds.length === 0
        ? []
        : tx
            .select({ lineId: salesReturnLines.id, number: salesReturns.number })
            .from(salesReturnLines)
            .innerJoin(
              salesReturns,
              and(
                eq(salesReturns.tenantId, salesReturnLines.tenantId),
                eq(salesReturns.id, salesReturnLines.returnId),
              ),
            )
            .where(
              and(
                eq(salesReturnLines.tenantId, tenantId),
                inArray(salesReturnLines.id, returnLineIds),
              ),
            ),
      this.allocationsOf(tx, id),
      row.status === 'posted' ? this.books.entryOf(tx, id, 'sales_credit_note') : null,
    ]);
    const returnNumber = new Map(returns.map((line) => [line.lineId, line.number]));
    return {
      ...toSummary(row, found.customer, this.invoiceRef(found.invoice), found.lineCount),
      pricesIncludeVat: found.invoice.pricesIncludeVat,
      discount: row.discount,
      note: row.note,
      lines: lines.map(({ row: line, variant }) => ({
        ...toSalesLine(line, variant),
        invoiceLineId: line.invoiceLineId,
        returnLineId: line.returnLineId,
        returnNumber:
          line.returnLineId === null ? null : (returnNumber.get(line.returnLineId) ?? null),
      })),
      // Only posted invoices are ever settled, so each has a number
      allocations: allocations.flatMap((allocation) =>
        allocation.invoiceNumber === null
          ? []
          : [{ ...allocation, invoiceNumber: allocation.invoiceNumber }],
      ),
      entry,
    };
  }

  private async customerOf(tx: Transaction, customerId: string): Promise<PartyRef> {
    const customer = (await customerRefs(tx, [customerId])).get(customerId);
    if (!customer) throw new Error(`Customer ${customerId} is missing`);
    return customer;
  }

  // What the audit log shows: the header and the size, not every line
  private snapshot(
    row: CreditNoteRow,
    customer: PartyRef,
    invoice: { number: string },
    lines: number,
  ) {
    return {
      number: row.number,
      date: row.date,
      invoice: invoice.number,
      customer: customer.code,
      reason: row.reason,
      total: row.total,
      lines,
    };
  }
}
```

- **`invoiceOf()`** refuses anything that is not a posted invoice with one answer, under the invoice box. A posted
  invoice always has a number; the check narrows the type without a cast.
- **`writeLines()`** writes the credit note's `invoice_id` on every line: it is part of all three line foreign keys
  (15d.2), which is how the database knows a line credits *this* invoice.
- **`lockPosted()` and `lockDraft()` share `lockRow()`.** A refund locks the credit note too, so an allocate and a
  refund of the same credit take turns.
- **`read()`** sends the invoice's price setting (`pricesIncludeVat`): the form needs it to show the totals the same
  way the server works them out.

### `sales/refunds.service.ts` (new)

```ts
import { Inject, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import {
  compareMoney,
  type PartyRef,
  type Refund,
  type RefundInput,
  type RefundSource,
  type RefundStatus,
  type RefundSummary,
  unappliedOf,
  type VoidRefundInput,
} from '@omnivo/contracts';
import { creditNotes, parties, receipts, refunds } from '@omnivo/db';
import { and, desc, eq, type SQL, sql } from 'drizzle-orm';
import { alias } from 'drizzle-orm/pg-core';
import { z } from 'zod';

import { audit, created } from '../common/audit/audit.js';
import { isCheckViolation } from '../common/db/pg-errors.js';
import { AppError, notFound, versionConflict } from '../common/http/app-error.js';
import { decodeCursor, toPage } from '../common/pagination/cursor.js';
import { currentPrincipal, getTenantId } from '../common/tenant/tenant-context.js';
import type { Transaction, WithTenant } from '../common/tenant/with-tenant.js';
import { WITH_TENANT } from '../infra/tokens.js';
import { NumberingService } from '../numbering/numbering.service.js';
import { SalesBooksService } from './sales-books.service.js';
import { assertBranch, assertCustomer, assertMoneyAccount } from './sales-lines.js';

type RefundRow = typeof refunds.$inferSelect;

const cursorSchema = z.tuple([z.iso.date(), z.uuid()]);

// The source's number, read through two joins: one of them finds it
const sourceReceipt = alias(receipts, 'source_receipt');
const sourceCreditNote = alias(creditNotes, 'source_credit_note');

// The money a refund pays back, as the check needs it: what came in or was credited, and what of
// it is used already
interface Source {
  number: string;
  amount: string;
  applied: string;
  refunded: string;
}

function toSummary(row: RefundRow, customer: PartyRef, source: RefundSource): RefundSummary {
  return {
    id: row.id,
    number: row.number,
    date: row.date,
    customer,
    amount: row.amount,
    method: row.method,
    reference: row.reference,
    accountId: row.accountId,
    branchId: row.branchId,
    source,
    status: row.status,
    version: row.version,
    updatedAt: row.updatedAt.toISOString(),
  };
}

function overSourceError(): AppError {
  return new AppError(
    409,
    'refund_over_source',
    'This is more than is left to pay back. Lower the amount.',
    { fieldErrors: { amount: ['refund_over_source'] } },
  );
}

// The database's last word (receipts_amount_check, credit_notes_money_check), if two writers got
// past the lock on the source. Answers with the code the form knows.
function overSourceRace(error: unknown): unknown {
  if (
    isCheckViolation(error, 'receipts_amount_check') ||
    isCheckViolation(error, 'credit_notes_money_check')
  ) {
    return overSourceError();
  }
  return error;
}
```

- **Two `alias()` joins for the source's number.** A refund names a receipt or a credit note. Both are left-joined
  under their own names, and exactly one of them finds a row (`refunds_source_check`).

```ts
// Refunds (step 15d): a customer's advance paid back out of a cash, bank or wallet account. Saving
// one posts it at once, like a money receipt: it gets its number (RF-2026-27-0001) and its entry.
// Afterwards it can only be voided.
@Injectable()
export class RefundsService {
  constructor(
    @Inject(WITH_TENANT) private readonly withTenant: WithTenant,
    private readonly numbering: NumberingService,
    private readonly books: SalesBooksService,
  ) {}

  list(query: {
    limit: number;
    cursor?: string | undefined;
    status?: RefundStatus | undefined;
    customerId?: string | undefined;
  }): Promise<{ items: RefundSummary[]; nextCursor: string | null }> {
    const after = decodeCursor(query.cursor, cursorSchema);
    return this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
      const rows = await this.rows(
        tx,
        and(
          query.status === undefined ? undefined : eq(refunds.status, query.status),
          query.customerId === undefined ? undefined : eq(refunds.customerId, query.customerId),
          after === undefined
            ? undefined
            : sql`(${refunds.date}, ${refunds.id}) < (${after[0]}::date, ${after[1]}::uuid)`,
        ),
        query.limit + 1,
      );
      const page = toPage(rows, query.limit, (last) => [last.refund.date, last.refund.id]);
      return {
        items: page.items.map((row) => toSummary(row.refund, row.customer, sourceOf(row))),
        nextCursor: page.nextCursor,
      };
    });
  }

  get(id: string): Promise<Refund> {
    return this.withTenant((tx) => this.read(tx, id));
  }

  async create(input: RefundInput): Promise<Refund> {
    try {
      return await this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
        const customer = await assertCustomer(tx, input.customerId);
        await assertBranch(tx, input.branchId);
        await assertMoneyAccount(tx, input.accountId, 'refund_account_invalid');
        // Locked: a second refund of the same money, or applying it to an invoice, waits for us
        const source = await this.lockSource(tx, customer.id, input);
        if (compareMoney(input.amount, unappliedOf(source)) > 0) throw overSourceError();
        const number = await this.numbering.next(tx, 'sales.refund', input.date);
        // Saved = posted: the trigger adds the amount to the source's `refunded` (migration 0032)
        const [row] = await tx
          .insert(refunds)
          .values({
            tenantId: getTenantId(),
            number,
            date: input.date,
            customerId: customer.id,
            amount: input.amount,
            accountId: input.accountId,
            method: input.method,
            reference: input.reference,
            branchId: input.branchId,
            note: input.note,
            receiptId: input.receiptId,
            creditNoteId: input.creditNoteId,
            createdBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
            updatedBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
          })
          .returning();
        if (!row) throw new Error('Refund insert returned no row');
        // The journal checks the period of the date: a refund in a closed month is refused here
        const entry = await this.books.refund(
          tx,
          { id: row.id, number, date: row.date },
          {
            customerId: customer.id,
            branchId: row.branchId,
            accountId: row.accountId,
            amount: row.amount,
          },
        );
        await audit(tx, {
          action: 'refund.created',
          entityType: 'refund',
          entityId: row.id,
          changes: created({
            number,
            date: row.date,
            customer: customer.code,
            amount: row.amount,
            method: row.method,
            source: source.number,
            entry: entry.number,
          }),
        });
        return this.read(tx, row.id);
      });
    } catch (error) {
      throw overSourceRace(error);
    }
  }

  // A refund typed by mistake, or money that never reached the customer: its entry is reversed on
  // the void date, and its money is the source's advance again (the trigger takes it off
  // `refunded`). The refund stays, voided, so its number is never reused or missing.
  void(id: string, input: VoidRefundInput): Promise<Refund> {
    return this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
      const row = await this.lock(tx, id, input.version);
      if (input.date < row.date) {
        throw new AppError(
          409,
          'receipt_void_date',
          'A refund cannot be voided before the day it was paid.',
          { fieldErrors: { date: ['receipt_void_date'] } },
        );
      }
      const entry = await this.books.entryOf(tx, id, 'sales_refund');
      if (entry === null) throw new Error(`Refund ${id} has no entry`);
      await tx
        .update(refunds)
        .set({
          status: 'voided',
          voidDate: input.date,
          voidReason: input.reason,
          version: sql`${refunds.version} + 1`,
          updatedBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
        })
        .where(and(eq(refunds.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(refunds.id, id)));
      const reversal = await this.books.reverse(tx, entry, {
        date: input.date,
        narration: `Refund ${row.number} voided: ${input.reason}`,
      });
      await audit(tx, {
        action: 'refund.voided',
        entityType: 'refund',
        entityId: id,
        changes: created({ date: input.date, reason: input.reason, reversal: reversal.number }),
      });
      return this.read(tx, id);
    });
  }
```

- **Saved = posted**, like a receipt: the money left the account, and nobody approves cash that was handed over.
- **The source is locked before the amount is checked.** Two refunds of the same advance, or a refund and an
  allocate of it, take turns; the second sees what the first used. `unappliedOf()` is the contract's function: the
  amount less what is applied and what was paid back.
- **The API never writes `refunded`.** It inserts the refund; the trigger of 0032 adds the amount to the source in
  the same statement, and the source's check is the last word.
- **No credit check** (15d.1): a refund only pays back the customer's own money.
- **`void`.** The status goes to `voided` and the trigger takes the amount off the source again, so it is the
  customer's advance once more. The entry is reversed on the void date, like a receipt's. A refund's void reuses the
  receipt's codes (`receipt_void_date`), as the contract says: same form, same words.

```ts
  // The receipt or credit note the money comes from: posted, and this customer's. FOR UPDATE, the
  // lock its own page takes to apply its money (and a receipt's void), so they all take turns.
  // Another workspace's, another customer's, a voided receipt and a draft credit note all get the
  // same answer, under the box that named it.
  private async lockSource(
    tx: Transaction,
    customerId: string,
    input: Pick<RefundInput, 'receiptId' | 'creditNoteId'>,
  ): Promise<Source> {
    const tenantId = getTenantId();
    const invalid = (field: 'receiptId' | 'creditNoteId') =>
      new AppError(409, 'refund_source_invalid', 'Pick a posted receipt or credit note.', {
        fieldErrors: { [field]: ['refund_source_invalid'] },
      });
    if (input.receiptId !== null) {
      const [row] = await tx
        .select()
        .from(receipts)
        .where(and(eq(receipts.tenantId, tenantId), eq(receipts.id, input.receiptId)))
        .for('update');
      if (row?.customerId !== customerId || row.status !== 'posted') throw invalid('receiptId');
      return row;
    }
    if (input.creditNoteId !== null) {
      const [row] = await tx
        .select()
        .from(creditNotes)
        .where(and(eq(creditNotes.tenantId, tenantId), eq(creditNotes.id, input.creditNoteId)))
        .for('update');
      if (row?.customerId !== customerId || row.status !== 'posted' || row.number === null) {
        throw invalid('creditNoteId');
      }
      return { ...row, number: row.number, amount: row.total };
    }
    // The contract makes sure one of the two is there (refund_source)
    throw new AppError(409, 'refund_source', 'Pick the receipt or credit note to pay back from.', {
      fieldErrors: { receiptId: ['refund_source'] },
    });
  }

  // FOR UPDATE: two voids of one refund take turns. A voided refund is final.
  private async lock(tx: Transaction, id: string, version: number): Promise<RefundRow> {
    const [row] = await tx
      .select()
      .from(refunds)
      .where(and(eq(refunds.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(refunds.id, id)))
      .for('update');
    if (!row) throw notFound('Refund');
    if (row.status === 'voided') {
      throw new AppError(409, 'refund_voided', 'This refund is voided and cannot be changed.');
    }
    if (row.version !== version) throw versionConflict();
    return row;
  }

  private rows(tx: Transaction, where: SQL | undefined, limit: number) {
    return tx
      .select({
        refund: refunds,
        customer: { id: parties.id, code: parties.code, name: parties.name },
        receiptNumber: sourceReceipt.number,
        creditNoteNumber: sourceCreditNote.number,
      })
      .from(refunds)
      .innerJoin(
        parties,
        and(eq(parties.tenantId, refunds.tenantId), eq(parties.id, refunds.customerId)),
      )
      .leftJoin(
        sourceReceipt,
        and(eq(sourceReceipt.tenantId, refunds.tenantId), eq(sourceReceipt.id, refunds.receiptId)),
      )
      .leftJoin(
        sourceCreditNote,
        and(
          eq(sourceCreditNote.tenantId, refunds.tenantId),
          eq(sourceCreditNote.id, refunds.creditNoteId),
        ),
      )
      .where(and(eq(refunds.tenantId, getTenantId()), where))
      .orderBy(desc(refunds.date), desc(refunds.id))
      .limit(limit);
  }

  private async read(tx: Transaction, id: string): Promise<Refund> {
    const [found] = await this.rows(tx, eq(refunds.id, id), 1);
    if (!found) throw notFound('Refund');
    const { refund: row } = found;
    const entry = await this.books.entryOf(tx, id, 'sales_refund');
    if (entry === null) throw new Error(`Refund ${id} has no entry`);
    const voidEntry = row.status === 'voided' ? await this.books.reversalOf(tx, entry.id) : null;
    return {
      ...toSummary(row, found.customer, sourceOf(found)),
      note: row.note,
      entry,
      voidEntry,
      voidDate: row.voidDate,
      voidReason: row.voidReason,
    };
  }
}

// Where a refund's money came from. refunds_source_check keeps exactly one of the two ids, and a
// refund is only made from a posted receipt or credit note, which always has a number: anything
// else is a broken row.
function sourceOf(row: {
  refund: RefundRow;
  receiptNumber: string | null;
  creditNoteNumber: string | null;
}): RefundSource {
  if (row.refund.receiptId !== null && row.receiptNumber !== null) {
    return { type: 'receipt', id: row.refund.receiptId, number: row.receiptNumber };
  }
  if (row.refund.creditNoteId !== null && row.creditNoteNumber !== null) {
    return { type: 'credit_note', id: row.refund.creditNoteId, number: row.creditNoteNumber };
  }
  throw new Error(`Refund ${row.refund.id} has no source`);
}
```

- **`lockSource()` gives one answer** for another workspace's, another customer's, a voided receipt and a draft
  credit note, under the box that named it. A credit note's `total` is its amount: the field names differ, the meaning
  does not.
- **`sourceOf()`** throws a plain `Error` for a row with no source. `refunds_source_check` makes that impossible;
  the throw keeps the type honest without a cast.

### `sales/sales-accounts.service.ts` (new) and its controller

```ts
import { Inject, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { type SalesAccounts, type UpdateSalesAccountsInput } from '@omnivo/contracts';
import { ledgerAccounts, tenantSettings } from '@omnivo/db';
import { and, eq, inArray, isNull } from 'drizzle-orm';

import { lockChart } from '../accounts/accounts.service.js';
import { audit, diff } from '../common/audit/audit.js';
import { AppError } from '../common/http/app-error.js';
import { currentPrincipal, getTenantId } from '../common/tenant/tenant-context.js';
import type { Transaction, WithTenant } from '../common/tenant/with-tenant.js';
import { WITH_TENANT } from '../infra/tokens.js';

// The account credit notes take sales back from (step 15d, you chose a setting), as Settings →
// Sales shows and saves it. It lives on the workspace's settings row, but has its own route: PUT
// /settings is the company's details, and needs no account rules.
@Injectable()
export class SalesAccountsService {
  constructor(@Inject(WITH_TENANT) private readonly withTenant: WithTenant) {}

  get(): Promise<SalesAccounts> {
    return this.withTenant((tx) => this.read(tx));
  }

  // An active income ledger, or none (the Sales account itself). Like the stock accounts: a group
  // posts nothing, and an expense or an asset would put the sales that came back in the wrong part
  // of the profit and loss.
  update(input: UpdateSalesAccountsInput): Promise<SalesAccounts> {
    const tenantId = getTenantId();
    return this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
      // The chart's own lock: nobody archives or deletes this account until we commit
      // (AccountsService takes it first, then refuses the account this setting points at)
      await lockChart(tx);
      const before = await this.read(tx);
      if (input.returns !== null) {
        const [account] = await tx
          .select({ id: ledgerAccounts.id })
          .from(ledgerAccounts)
          .where(
            and(
              eq(ledgerAccounts.tenantId, tenantId),
              eq(ledgerAccounts.id, input.returns),
              eq(ledgerAccounts.type, 'income'),
              eq(ledgerAccounts.isGroup, false),
              isNull(ledgerAccounts.archivedAt),
            ),
          );
        if (!account) {
          throw new AppError(409, 'sales_account_invalid', 'Pick an active income account.', {
            fieldErrors: { returns: ['sales_account_invalid'] },
          });
        }
      }
      // No new version: the settings form's version guards the company's details, which this
      // does not touch (the logo works the same way)
      await tx
        .update(tenantSettings)
        .set({ salesReturnsAccountId: input.returns, updatedBy: currentPrincipal().userId })
        .where(eq(tenantSettings.tenantId, tenantId));
      const after = await this.read(tx);
      // The audit log shows codes ("4120"), which a person can read, not ids
      const codeOf = await this.codes(tx, [before.returns, after.returns]);
      await audit(tx, {
        action: 'sales_accounts.changed',
        entityType: 'workspace',
        entityId: tenantId,
        changes: diff(
          { returns: before.returns === null ? null : (codeOf.get(before.returns) ?? null) },
          { returns: after.returns === null ? null : (codeOf.get(after.returns) ?? null) },
        ),
      });
      return after;
    });
  }

  private async codes(
    tx: Transaction,
    ids: readonly (string | null)[],
  ): Promise<Map<string, string>> {
    const wanted = [...new Set(ids.filter((id): id is string => id !== null))];
    if (wanted.length === 0) return new Map();
    const rows = await tx
      .select({ id: ledgerAccounts.id, code: ledgerAccounts.code })
      .from(ledgerAccounts)
      .where(and(eq(ledgerAccounts.tenantId, getTenantId()), inArray(ledgerAccounts.id, wanted)));
    return new Map(rows.map((row) => [row.id, row.code]));
  }

  private async read(tx: Transaction): Promise<SalesAccounts> {
    const [settings] = await tx
      .select({ returns: tenantSettings.salesReturnsAccountId })
      .from(tenantSettings)
      .where(eq(tenantSettings.tenantId, getTenantId()));
    if (!settings) throw new Error(`tenant_settings row missing for tenant ${getTenantId()}`);
    return settings;
  }
}
```

- **Its own route, on the settings row.** `PUT /settings` saves the company's details and knows nothing about
  accounts; this one checks an account. Like step 14's stock accounts.
- **An active income ledger, or none.** A group posts nothing; an expense or an asset would put the sales that came
  back in the wrong part of the profit and loss.
- **The chart lock** (`lockChart()`, step 9) makes this and an archive of the same account take turns:
  `AccountsService` takes the same lock and then refuses the chosen account.
- **No new version on the settings row.** The settings form's version guards the company's details. Changing the
  returns account does not touch them, and bumping the version would make an open settings page fail for nothing (the
  logo works the same way).
- **The audit row shows codes** ("4120"), which a person can read.

- **Three controllers, one per route group**, next to the other sales documents. Each method only passes the parsed
  request on; the contract's `Endpoint()` decorator has already checked the body, the query and the permission.

```ts
import { ledgerAccounts, tenantSettings } from '@omnivo/db';
import { and, eq, isNull } from 'drizzle-orm';

import type { Transaction } from '../common/tenant/with-tenant.js';
import type { AccountTemplate, IndustryTemplate } from './templates.js';

// The template's name for an income code: "4120" → "Sales returns"
function incomeName(template: IndustryTemplate, code: string): string | undefined {
  const walk = (node: AccountTemplate): string | undefined =>
    node.code === code ? node.name : (node.children ?? []).map(walk).find(Boolean);
  return walk(template.chart.income);
}

// Chooses the sales returns account (step 15d) for the transaction's tenant, from its template, and
// returns its code, or null when nothing was chosen: the template has none, one is chosen already,
// or the account at that code is not the template's own. That is the rule migration 0032 used for
// the workspaces that already existed: the code AND the name, an active income ledger. Nothing the
// owner made is ever taken over. Idempotent; the callers lock the tenant row first, like seedChart.
export async function seedSalesReturnsAccount(
  tx: Transaction,
  tenantId: string,
  template: IndustryTemplate,
): Promise<string | null> {
  const code = template.salesReturnsAccount;
  const name = code === null ? undefined : incomeName(template, code);
  if (code === null || name === undefined) return null;
  const [account] = await tx
    .select({ id: ledgerAccounts.id })
    .from(ledgerAccounts)
    .where(
      and(
        eq(ledgerAccounts.tenantId, tenantId),
        eq(ledgerAccounts.code, code),
        eq(ledgerAccounts.name, name),
        eq(ledgerAccounts.type, 'income'),
        eq(ledgerAccounts.isGroup, false),
        isNull(ledgerAccounts.archivedAt),
      ),
    );
  if (!account) return null;
  const chosen = await tx
    .update(tenantSettings)
    .set({ salesReturnsAccountId: account.id })
    .where(and(eq(tenantSettings.tenantId, tenantId), isNull(tenantSettings.salesReturnsAccountId)))
    .returning({ tenantId: tenantSettings.tenantId });
  return chosen.length === 0 ? null : code;
}
```

- **The code *and* the name**, an active income ledger: the rule migration 0032 used for workspaces that already
  existed (15d.2). A chart the owner changed before the job ran is never taken over.
- **Only where nothing is chosen** (`IS NULL` in the `WHERE`), so a second run of the job changes nothing.

`apps/api` type checks, and its unit tests pass (88, with the new template test). Build `packages/db` before the API

We also ran a short integration test against a real Postgres, in a pharmacy workspace (so setup chose 4120):

- An order of 48 delivered, 10 returned before billing: the order went back to confirmed with 38 delivered, the
  challan showed "partly returned", the return was booked at ৳100.00 (Dr Inventory / Cr Cost of goods sold), and 39
  more was refused under the quantity.
- An invoice of 48 for that challan line was refused, 38 was posted. 8 more came back after billing: the return line
  was "billed", with the invoice line.
- A credit note for those 8: Dr 4120 ৳160 / Dr VAT ৳24 / Cr Accounts receivable ৳184, applied to its invoice, the
  invoice's line credited, the return line credited. A second credit for the same return line, and more money than the
  line had left, were refused.
- A receipt with an advance, a refund of part of it (Dr receivable / Cr cash), the receipt's void refused while the
  refund stood, the refund voided and its money back on the receipt. A price-cut credit note on a settled invoice
  became an advance, was refunded, and then had nothing left to apply.
- The chosen 4120 could not be archived. With no account chosen, a credit note debited Sales. Reverse refused a credit
  note's entry.
- A batch item returned from its challan line in three goes (its batch taken from the line, the values adding up to
  the line's), a batch named on a challan line refused, a line on its own at the average cost, an item with no cost
  refused under the item, and a draft saved, changed and deleted. A return on a closed order left it closed, with its
  delivered quantity down.

The 15b and 15c integration tests still pass. 15d.4 turns that test into the full suite.

Three things still fail, as expected:

- **The numbering integration test** counts 14 document types; there are 17 now. 15d.4 updates it.
- **`pnpm typecheck` for the whole repo**: `packages/i18n` needs the new keys, now 30 error codes (15d.5), and the
  app's pills and mocks need the new fields (15d.6, 15d.7).

## 15d.4 — `apps/api`: the tests

This part adds one test file and extends three others. Like every integration test since step 5, they run against a
real Postgres and the real worker:

- `sales/returns.int.spec.ts` (new) follows a medicine distributor through what comes back: goods returned before
  and after the bill, credit notes for returns and for price cuts, a whole invoice credited in one click, advances
  applied to later invoices and paid back by refunds, and three races.
- `sales/sales.tenant-leak.int.spec.ts` gets a fourth `describe`: workspace A must never see, change, credit or pay
  back anything of workspace B's.
- `setup/setup.int.spec.ts` checks which workspaces get a sales returns account from their template.
- `numbering/numbering.int.spec.ts` counts the number series, and 15d adds three.

**These tests found one bug in the 15d.3 code**, and the code above already has the fix. Two credit notes posted
for the same invoice at the same moment could deadlock, and one of them failed with a 500. The cause and the fix
(`FOR NO KEY UPDATE` instead of `FOR UPDATE` on the invoice) are explained in 15d.3, under `allocations.ts` and
under the credit note's posting. The test that found it is "lets a credit note wait for another one" below.

### `sales/returns.int.spec.ts` (new): the setup

```ts
let redis: TestRedis;
let app: NestFastifyApplication;
let worker: INestApplicationContext;
let owner: SignedIn;
let tenantId: string;
// A member with no role: reads every return, credit note and refund, writes none
let viewer: SignedIn;
// The store keeper who takes goods back: writes returns, nothing that moves money
let storeKeeper: SignedIn;
let units: Unit[];
let accounts: Account[];
let rates: TaxRate[];
let main: Warehouse;
let damage: Warehouse;
let napa: Product;
let syrup: Product;
let injection: Product;
let meter: Product;
// Never stocked: it has no average cost
let omeprazole: Product;
let napaBatch: string;
let tamanna: Customer;
let agrabad: Customer;
// Tamanna's order and its challan: 60 bottles of syrup and 20 strips of Napa
let order: SalesOrder;
let challan: Delivery;
// A draft challan of Tamanna's: its lines cannot come back
let draftChallan: Delivery;
let firstReturn: SalesReturn;
// The invoice of what was left on the challan
let firstInvoice: Invoice;
// 5 bottles back after the invoice: billed, so a credit note gives the money back
let billedReturn: SalesReturn;
let firstCreditNote: CreditNote;
// A price cut posted after the invoice was paid: all of it is Tamanna's advance
let advanceNote: CreditNote;
// Tamanna's second invoice, which the advance is applied to
let laterInvoice: Invoice;
let tamannaReceipt: Receipt;
let receiptRefund: Refund;
// The credit note that won the race for INV-0003: ৳50 of it is Tamanna's advance
let racedNote: CreditNote;
```

- **One workspace, one story**, as in 15b and 15c. Each test builds on the ones before it: the challan of the first
  test is billed by the third, its invoice gets the credit notes, and the receipt that pays it is where the refunds
  come from. When a test fails, read the first failure first.
- **A pharmacy workspace**, because its template has "4120 Sales returns" and setup chooses it (15d.3). Every credit
  note in this file books to 4120 unless a test changes the setting.
- **Four products, one for each kind of return.** Napa is sold by the strip but counted by the tablet, in a batch, so
  a return can come back in another unit and must keep its batch. The syrup is plain. The three injections were
  bought at two prices, so their value does not divide by three, which is what the rounding test needs. The
  glucometers have serial numbers. Omeprazole is never stocked, so it has no average cost.
- **Two customers.** Tamanna Pharmacy buys on 30 days and carries the main story. Agrabad Medicine Corner pays on
  the day, and is used where a test needs a second customer or must not change Tamanna's numbers.
- **Three users.** The owner has every permission. `viewer` has no role: reading needs no permission, every write
  needs one. `storeKeeper` may write challans and returns, but not credit notes, refunds or settings: taking goods
  back and paying money out are different jobs (15d.1).

```ts
function send(
  method: 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'DELETE',
  url: string,
  payload?: object,
  as = owner,
) {
  return app.inject({
    method,
    url,
    headers: bearer(as.accessToken),
    ...(payload && { payload }),
  });
}

function problemOf(res: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof send>>) {
  return problemSchema.parse(res.json());
}

function unitId(code: string): string {
  const found = units.find((unit) => unit.code === code);
  if (!found) throw new Error(`no unit ${code}`);
  return found.id;
}

function rateId(name: string): string {
  const found = rates.find((rate) => rate.name === name);
  if (!found) throw new Error(`no VAT rate ${name}`);
  return found.id;
}

function account(code: string): string {
  const found = accounts.find((item) => item.code === code);
  if (!found) throw new Error(`no account ${code}`);
  return found.id;
}

function codeOf(id: string): string {
  return accounts.find((item) => item.id === id)?.code ?? id;
}

function variantOf(product: Product): string {
  const [variant] = product.variants;
  if (!variant) throw new Error(`${product.name} has no variant`);
  return variant.id;
}

function lineOf<T extends { id: string; variantId: string }>(
  lines: readonly T[],
  product: Product,
): T {
  const found = lines.find((item) => item.variantId === variantOf(product));
  if (!found) throw new Error(`no ${product.name} line`);
  return found;
}

```

- **The form builders send every field**, typed with the contract's form types (`SalesReturnLineFormValues`,
  `CreditNoteFormValues`, `RefundFormValues` and the rest). A field renamed in the contract then breaks the type check
  here, not a test at run time.
- **`returnLine()` is a line on its own unless `extra` names a challan line**, and `creditLine()` is a price cut
  unless `extra` names a return line. That is how the forms of 15d.6 build them too.
- **`returnForm()` puts the goods into the "Damage and expiry" store** by default, the way a depot handles goods that
  came back (decision 3). `refundForm()` names no source: every test says where the money comes from.
- **`lineOf()` finds a line by its item**, on a challan, an order, an invoice or a return. A line's position would
  also work, but "the syrup line" says what the test means, and it fails loudly if the line is missing.
- **`stockIn()` reads the stock of one warehouse** by product name, so a test can show where the goods went.
- **`entryLines()` and `auditActions()`** are 15c's: an entry as `[account code, debit, credit]` rows, and the sorted
  actions of one record. The codes are the pharma chart's: 1110 Cash in hand, 1131 the bKash account, 1140 Accounts
  receivable, 1154 Finished goods (the inventory account), 2120 Output VAT, 4110 Sales, 4120 Sales returns, 5110 Cost
  of goods sold.

```ts
// A user who signs up for a workspace of their own, then joins this one; with a role, if given
async function member(
  email: string,
  fullName: string,
  password: string,
  permissions: PermissionKey[] | null,
): Promise<SignedIn> {
  await signUp(app, {
    companyName: `${fullName} Store`,
    workspaceSlug: email.split('@')[0] ?? 'store',
    fullName,
    email,
    password,
  });
  await joinWithoutRoles(pg.superuserUrl, { email, workspace: 'karnaphuli-medicine' });
  if (permissions !== null) {
    const made = await send('POST', '/roles', { name: 'Return desk', description: '' });
    expect(made.statusCode, made.body).toBe(201);
    const role = roleSchema.parse(made.json());
    const matrix = await send('PUT', '/permission-matrix', {
      roles: [{ id: role.id, version: role.version, permissions }],
    });
    expect(matrix.statusCode, matrix.body).toBe(200);
    const { items } = memberPageSchema.parse((await send('GET', '/members')).json());
    const found = items.find((item) => item.email === email);
    if (!found) throw new Error(`${email} is not a member`);
    const assigned = await send('PUT', `/members/${found.membershipId}/roles`, {
      roleIds: [role.id],
      version: found.version,
    });
    expect(assigned.statusCode, assigned.body).toBe(200);
  }
  return logIn(app, { workspace: 'karnaphuli-medicine', email, password, keepSignedIn: false });
}
```
