- **The returns store is under a branch of its own** (Kalurghat). The return's entry then shows two branches, and a
  mistake in which line takes which branch cannot hide.
- **A bKash account (1131) is added under "Mobile wallets" with no tick.** A refund pays out of it, so the tests also
  show that the group's tick is enough, like the bank account in 15c.
- **`customFields: { generic_name }`.** The pharma template makes the generic name required (step 12), so every
  product sends one.
- **The opening stock** is 500 tablets of Napa at ৳0.80 (lot NP2409), 100 bottles of syrup at ৳25, three injections
  worth ৳1,000 together (2 at ৳300 and 1 at ৳400, two lines in one adjustment), and three glucometers at ৳1,500 with
  their serial numbers. Every cost below is a plain multiplication from these.

### Sales returns

```ts
describe('sales returns', () => {
  it('takes goods back from a challan before it is billed, at what they cost', async () => {
    order = await ordered(
      [salesLine(syrup, '60', '40'), salesLine(napa, '20', '12', { unitId: unitId('strip') })],
      tamanna,
    );
    challan = await delivered(tamanna, order.id, [
      deliveryLine(syrup, '60', { orderLineId: lineOf(order.lines, syrup).id }),
      deliveryLine(napa, '20', {
        unitId: unitId('strip'),
        batchId: napaBatch,
        orderLineId: lineOf(order.lines, napa).id,
      }),
    ]);
    expect((await orderNow(order.id)).status).toBe('delivered');

    // 10 bottles, and 30 tablets of the 20 strips: any unit of the item
    firstReturn = await returned(
      returnForm([
        returnLine(syrup, '10', { deliveryLineId: lineOf(challan.lines, syrup).id }),
        returnLine(napa, '30', { deliveryLineId: lineOf(challan.lines, napa).id }),
      ]),
    );
    expect(firstReturn).toMatchObject({
      number: 'SR-2026-27-0001',
      status: 'posted',
      warehouseId: damage.id,
      deliveries: [{ id: challan.id, number: challan.number }],
      creditNotes: [],
    });
    // At the challan's cost: 10/60 of ৳1,500 and 30/200 of ৳160. The batch is the challan line's.
    expect(
      firstReturn.lines.map((line) => [line.deliveryNumber, line.batchId, line.billed, line.value]),
    ).toEqual([
      ['DC-2026-27-0001', null, false, '250.0000'],
      ['DC-2026-27-0001', napaBatch, false, '24.0000'],
    ]);
    // Inventory comes back where the goods are now, cost of goods sold comes off where it was booked
    const entry = journalEntrySchema.parse(
      (await send('GET', `/journal-entries/${firstReturn.entry?.id ?? ''}`)).json(),
    );
    expect(entry.source).toBe('sales_return');
    expect(await entryLines(entry.id)).toEqual([
      ['1154', '274.0000', '0.0000'],
      ['5110', '0.0000', '274.0000'],
    ]);
    expect(entry.lines.map((item) => item.branchId)).toEqual([damage.branchId, main.branchId]);

    expect(await stockIn(damage)).toMatchObject({
      'Napa 500 mg': '30.0000',
      'Paracetamol syrup 60 ml': '10.0000',
    });
    expect(await stockIn(main)).toMatchObject({
      'Napa 500 mg': '300.0000',
      'Paracetamol syrup 60 ml': '40.0000',
    });
    const moves = stockMovementPageSchema.parse(
      (await send('GET', `/stock/variants/${variantOf(syrup)}/movements`)).json(),
    );
    expect(moves.items.find((move) => move.documentId === firstReturn.id)).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'sales_return',
      documentNumber: 'SR-2026-27-0001',
      warehouseId: damage.id,
      quantity: '10.0000',
      value: '250.0000',
    });

    // Not billed yet: the order can deliver them again (in the base unit), and is open again
    const reopened = await orderNow(order.id);
    expect(reopened.status).toBe('confirmed');
    expect(reopened.version).toBe(order.version + 2);
    expect(reopened.lines.map((line) => line.deliveredQuantity)).toEqual(['50.0000', '170.0000']);
    const after = await deliveryNow(challan.id);
    expect(after).toMatchObject({
      returnState: 'partly_returned',
      returns: [{ id: firstReturn.id, number: 'SR-2026-27-0001' }],
    });
    expect(after.lines.map((line) => line.returnedQuantity)).toEqual(['10.0000', '30.0000']);
    expect(await auditActions('sales_return', firstReturn.id)).toEqual([
      'sales_return.created',
      'sales_return.posted',
    ]);
  });
```

- **The first return comes back before the bill.** Tamanna's order of 60 bottles and 20 strips is delivered on
  DC-0001, and the order is "delivered". SR-0001 brings back 10 bottles and 30 *tablets*: the challan line was in
  strips, and a return may use any unit of the item.
- **At the challan's cost** (decision 2): 10/60 of the line's ৳1,500 is ৳250, and 30/200 of ৳160 is ৳24. The Napa line
  takes the challan line's batch without the form naming it. Neither line is billed.
- **The entry has two branches.** Dr Inventory ৳274 on Kalurghat, where the goods are now; Cr Cost of goods sold ৳274
  on the main branch, where the challan booked it. Its source is `sales_return`.
- **The goods are in the returns store**, and the syrup's stock movements show the return with kind
  `sales_return`, its number and its value.
- **The order is open again** (decision 8): it is "confirmed", with 50 and 170 delivered, in the base unit, as
  `deliveredQuantity` always is. Its version went up twice since it was confirmed: once by the challan, once by the
  return. The challan is "partly returned", lists the return, and each line says how much came back.

```ts
  it('refuses goods that did not leave on that challan line, each under its own box', async () => {
    draftChallan = await delivered(tamanna, '', [deliveryLine(syrup, '5')], false);

    // Another item than the challan line's, and a line of a draft challan: both at once
    const wrong = await send(

    // Another customer's challan
    const notTheirs = await send(
      'POST',

      }),
    );
    expect(problemOf(notTheirs).fieldErrors).toEqual({
      'lines.0.deliveryLineId': ['return_delivery_line_invalid'],
    });
    // Tomorrow's goods cannot come back today
    const future = await send(
      'POST',
      '/sales-returns',
      returnForm([returnLine(syrup, '1', { deliveryLineId: syrupLine })], { date: '2099-01-01' }),
    );
    expect(problemOf(future).fieldErrors).toEqual({ date: ['stock_date_future'] });

    // What the form itself can see is a 400 from the contract
    const withBatch = await send(
      'POST',
      '/sales-returns',
      returnForm([
        returnLine(napa, '1', {
          deliveryLineId: lineOf(challan.lines, napa).id,
          batchId: napaBatch,
        }),
      ]),
    );
    expect(withBatch.statusCode).toBe(400);
    expect(problemOf(withBatch).fieldErrors).toEqual({
      'lines.0.batchId': ['return_batch_not_allowed'],
    });
    const twice = await send(
      'POST',
      '/sales-returns',
      returnForm([
        returnLine(syrup, '1', { deliveryLineId: syrupLine }),
        returnLine(syrup, '2', { deliveryLineId: syrupLine }),
      ]),

    expect(twice.statusCode).toBe(400);
    expect(problemOf(twice).fieldErrors).toEqual({
      'lines.1.deliveryLineId': ['return_line_twice'],
    });
  });
```

- **Every bad line comes back under its own box.** 51 bottles is `return_over_delivered` (only 50 are still out).
  A line that names the syrup's challan line but another item, and a line of a draft challan, are
  `return_delivery_line_invalid`, both in one answer. Another customer's challan line gets the same answer, as if it
  did not exist.
- **A date in the future is refused** (`stock_date_future`), like every stock document: goods cannot come back
  before the day they come back.
- **What the form can see is a 400 from the contract**: a batch on a line from a challan (the challan line already
  says which batch left) and the same challan line twice.
- **None of these used a number**: the next return is SR-0002.


- **The invoice bills only what is left.** Billing the whole challan (60 bottles, 20 strips) is refused under both
  lines. 50 bottles and 17 strips post as INV-0001: ৳2,204 + 15% VAT = ৳2,534.60. The challan has nothing left to
  bill.
- **A return after the bill is billed.** SR-0002 brings back 5 bottles: the line points at the invoice line that
  billed it, which is what a credit note needs. Its value is 15/60 of ৳1,500 less the ৳250 that came back before:
  ৳125.
- **The order is left alone.** The sale stands, so its delivered quantity and its version do not change (decision 8).

- **The rounding test.** Three injections worth ৳1,000 leave on one line and come back one at a time: ৳333.33,
  ৳333.34, ৳333.33. Each value is counted over everything returned so far (15d.1's formula), so the three add up
  to exactly ৳1,000, with no paisa left on the books. With a plain "one third each", the three would be ৳999.99.
- **A challan that came back whole leaves both lists**: it is no longer returnable (`?return=returnable` shows only
  DC-0001) and has nothing to bill (`?invoice=to_invoice` is empty). A fourth injection is refused.
- **A line on its own comes back at the average cost**: 2 strips of Napa sold before the system existed are 20
  tablets × ৳0.80 = ৳16. The batch printed on the strips is named, and a batch item without one is
  `stock_batch_required`. Omeprazole has no cost at all, so its return is `return_cost_unknown` under the item
  (15d.3): the person must bring in its opening stock first.
- **Only serial numbers that left on the line can come back.** GM-1003 never left, so it is `return_serial_invalid`.
  GM-1002 comes back at its ৳1,500, and the stock card shows it in the returns store.

```ts
  it('keeps drafts free, and checks them again when they are posted', async () => {
    const napaLine = lineOf(challan.lines, napa).id;
    // 170 tablets are still out on the line. Two drafts of 100 each: drafts hold nothing.
    const form = (quantity: string) =>
      returnForm([returnLine(napa, quantity, { deliveryLineId: napaLine })], {
        date: '2026-10-08',
        reason: 'expired',
        post: false,
      });
    const one = await returned(form('100'));
    const two = await returned(form('100'));
    expect([one.number, two.number, one.lines[0]?.value]).toEqual([null, null, null]);
    // The draft keeps the challan line's batch
    expect(one.lines[0]?.batchId).toBe(napaBatch);

    const posted = await send('POST', `/sales-returns/${one.id}/post`, { version: one.version });
    expect(posted.statusCode, posted.body).toBe(200);
    expect(salesReturnSchema.parse(posted.json()).number).toBe('SR-2026-27-0008');
    const refused = await send('POST', `/sales-returns/${two.id}/post`, { version: two.version });
    expect(problemOf(refused).fieldErrors).toEqual({
      'lines.0.quantity': ['return_over_delivered'],
    });
    expect((await returnNow(two.id)).status).toBe('draft');

    const fixed = await send('PUT', `/sales-returns/${two.id}`, {
      ...form('50'),
      post: true,
      version: two.version,
    });
    expect(fixed.statusCode, fixed.body).toBe(200);
    expect(salesReturnSchema.parse(fixed.json())).toMatchObject({
      number: 'SR-2026-27-0009',
      lines: [{ billed: true, value: '40.0000' }],
    });
    expect(await auditActions('sales_return', two.id)).toEqual([
      'sales_return.created',
      'sales_return.posted',
      'sales_return.updated',
    ]);

    // A posted return is final
    const change = await send('PUT', `/sales-returns/${one.id}`, {
      ...form('1'),
      version: one.version + 1,
    });
    expect(problemOf(change).code).toBe('stock_not_draft');
    const remove = await send(
      'DELETE',
      `/sales-returns/${one.id}?version=${String(one.version + 1)}`,
    );
    expect(problemOf(remove).code).toBe('stock_not_draft');

    // A draft that is deleted is gone, and never had a number
    const third = await returned(form('1'));
    expect(
      (await send('DELETE', `/sales-returns/${third.id}?version=${String(third.version)}`))
        .statusCode,
    ).toBe(204);
    expect((await send('GET', `/sales-returns/${third.id}`)).statusCode).toBe(404);
    expect(await auditActions('sales_return', third.id)).toEqual([
      'sales_return.created',
      'sales_return.deleted',
    ]);

    const drafts = salesReturnPageSchema.parse(
      (await send('GET', '/sales-returns?status=draft')).json(),
    );
    expect(drafts.items).toEqual([]);
    const agrabads = salesReturnPageSchema.parse(
      (await send('GET', `/sales-returns?customerId=${agrabad.id}`)).json(),
    );
    expect(agrabads.items.map((item) => item.number)).toEqual([
      'SR-2026-27-0006',
      'SR-2026-27-0005',
      'SR-2026-27-0004',
      'SR-2026-27-0003',
    ]);
  });

  it('leaves a closed order closed', async () => {
    const small = await ordered([salesLine(syrup, '10', '40')], agrabad);
    const part = await delivered(agrabad, small.id, [
      deliveryLine(syrup, '4', { orderLineId: lineOf(small.lines, syrup).id }),
    ]);
    const now = await orderNow(small.id);
    const closed = await send('POST', `/sales-orders/${small.id}/close`, { version: now.version });
    expect(closed.statusCode, closed.body).toBe(200);
    const closedOrder = salesOrderSchema.parse(closed.json());
    await returned(
      returnForm([returnLine(syrup, '1', { deliveryLineId: lineOf(part.lines, syrup).id })], {
        customerId: agrabad.id,
      }),
    );
    const after = await orderNow(small.id);
    expect(after).toMatchObject({ status: 'closed', version: closedOrder.version });
    expect(lineOf(after.lines, syrup).deliveredQuantity).toBe('3.0000');
  });
});
```

- **Drafts hold nothing.** 170 tablets are still out on the Napa line. Two drafts of 100 each are both saved. Neither
  has a number or a value, and the first already stores the challan line's batch.
- **Posting checks again.** The first posts as SR-0008. The second is refused under its quantity and stays a draft.
  Changed to 50 and posted in the same PUT, it becomes SR-0009, billed (the line was invoiced in the third test),
  worth ৳40. Its audit rows are created, updated and posted.
- **A posted return is final**: changing or deleting it is `stock_not_draft`. A draft that is deleted is gone (404),
  with created and deleted in the log, and it never used a number.
- **The lists**: no drafts are left, and Agrabad's returns come newest first.
- **A closed order stays closed.** A return on it lowers the line's delivered quantity (4 → 3), but the order keeps
  its status and its version: migration 0028 freezes a closed order's header (15d.3).

### Credit notes

```ts
describe('credit notes', () => {
  it('gives the money back for a billed return, on the invoice it came from', async () => {
    const syrupInvoiceLine = lineOf(firstInvoice.lines, syrup).id;
    const backLine = billedReturn.lines[0]?.id ?? '';
    firstCreditNote = await credited(

      ['INV-2026-27-0001', '230.0000'],

    // The sale back from Sales returns (4120, the pharma template's choice), the VAT back, and
    // the receivable down with Tamanna on the line
    const entry = journalEntrySchema.parse(

    );
    expect(entry.source).toBe('sales_credit_note');
    expect(await entryLines(entry.id)).toEqual([
      ['4120', '200.0000', '0.0000'],
      ['2120', '30.0000', '0.0000'],
      ['1140', '0.0000', '230.0000'],

    expect(entry.lines.map((item) => item.party?.id ?? null)).toEqual([null, null, tamanna.id]);
    expect(new Set(entry.lines.map((item) => item.branchId))).toEqual(new Set([main.branchId]));

    const invoice = await invoiceNow(firstInvoice.id);
    expect(invoice).toMatchObject({
      amountCredited: '230.0000',
      creditNoteTotal: '230.0000',

    });
    expect(invoice.lines.map((line) => line.credited)).toEqual(['230.0000', '0.0000']);
    expect(creditStateOf(invoice)).toBe('partly_credited');
    const back = await returnNow(billedReturn.id);
    expect(back.lines[0]?.creditedQuantity).toBe('5.0000');
    expect(back.creditNotes.map((note) => note.number)).toEqual(['CN-2026-27-0001']);
    expect(await auditActions('credit_note', firstCreditNote.id)).toEqual([

  it('refuses lines the invoice did not bill, each under its own box', async () => {
    const syrupInvoiceLine = lineOf(firstInvoice.lines, syrup).id;
    const napaInvoiceLine = lineOf(firstInvoice.lines, napa).id;
    const backLine = billedReturn.lines[0]?.id ?? '';
    const refuse = async (body: object) => {
      const res = await send('POST', '/credit-notes', body);
      expect(res.statusCode, res.body).toBe(409);
      return problemOf(res).fieldErrors;
    };
    // The same return's money twice
    expect(
      await refuse(
        creditForm(firstInvoice, [
          creditLine(syrupInvoiceLine, '1', '40', { returnLineId: backLine }),
        ]),
      ),
    ).toEqual({ 'lines.0.quantity': ['credit_note_over_return'] });
    // A return line that came back before the bill (the invoice billed less instead), and a
    // return line on another invoice line than the one that billed it
    expect(
      await refuse(
        creditForm(firstInvoice, [
          creditLine(syrupInvoiceLine, '1', '40', {
            returnLineId: lineOf(firstReturn.lines, syrup).id,
          }),
          creditLine(napaInvoiceLine, '1', '12', { returnLineId: backLine }),
        ]),
      ),
    ).toEqual({
      'lines.0.returnLineId': ['credit_note_return_invalid'],
      'lines.1.returnLineId': ['credit_note_return_invalid'],

    // More than the line billed, and a unit the item does not have

      await refuse(creditForm(firstInvoice, [creditLine(syrupInvoiceLine, '51', '1')])),
    ).toEqual({ 'lines.0.quantity': ['credit_note_over_quantity'] });
    expect(
      await refuse(

          creditLine(syrupInvoiceLine, '1', '1', { unitId: unitId('strip') }),
        ]),

    // Dated before the invoice
    expect(
      await refuse(
        creditForm(firstInvoice, [creditLine(syrupInvoiceLine, '1', '1')], { date: '2026-10-06' }),
      ),
    ).toEqual({ date: ['credit_note_date'] });
    // A draft invoice: nothing to credit yet
    const draft = await invoiced(
      invoiceForm([invoiceLine(syrup, '1', '40')], { warehouseId: main.id, post: false }),
    );
    expect(
      await refuse(creditForm(draft, [creditLine(draft.lines[0]?.id ?? '', '1', '40')])),
    ).toEqual({ invoiceId: ['credit_note_invoice_invalid'] });
    expect(
      (await send('DELETE', `/invoices/${draft.id}?version=${String(draft.version)}`)).statusCode,
    ).toBe(204);

    // What the form can see: the same return line twice
    const twice = await send(
      'POST',
      '/credit-notes',
      creditForm(firstInvoice, [
        creditLine(syrupInvoiceLine, '1', '40', { returnLineId: backLine }),
        creditLine(syrupInvoiceLine, '1', '40', { returnLineId: backLine }),
      ]),
    );
    expect(twice.statusCode).toBe(400);
    expect(problemOf(twice).fieldErrors).toEqual({
      'lines.1.returnLineId': ['credit_note_return_twice'],
    });
  });
```

- **CN-0001 gives back the 5 bottles of SR-0002** at the invoice's price: ৳200 + ৳30 VAT = ৳230, all applied to
  INV-0001, which still owed more. The customer, the branch and the price setting are the invoice's. The line keeps
  the invoice line's item and VAT rate, and names the return.
- **The entry**: Dr 4120 Sales returns ৳200, Dr Output VAT ৳30, Cr Accounts receivable ৳230 with Tamanna on the line,
  every line on the invoice's branch. Its source is `sales_credit_note`.
- **The invoice and the return follow.** The invoice shows ৳230 credited, lists CN-0001, and its syrup line says
  ৳230 of it was credited, so `creditStateOf()` says "partly credited". The return line says 5 were credited and the
  return lists the credit note.
- **Every bad line comes back under its own box.** The same return's money twice is `credit_note_over_return`. A
  return line that came back before the bill (the invoice already billed less) and a return line put on the Napa
  invoice line are both `credit_note_return_invalid`, in one answer. 51 bottles is `credit_note_over_quantity`; a
  strip on the syrup line is `stock_unit_invalid`. A date before the invoice is `credit_note_date`, and a draft
  invoice is `credit_note_invoice_invalid`. The same return line twice on one credit note is a 400 from the contract.

```ts
  it('caps the money on each invoice line, under every line that takes from it', async () => {
    const syrupInvoiceLine = lineOf(firstInvoice.lines, syrup).id;
    const napaInvoiceLine = lineOf(firstInvoice.lines, napa).id;
    // The syrup line charged ৳2,300, and ৳230 came back: ৳2,070 is left. ৳2,070 + ৳1.15 is not.
    const over = await send(

      creditForm(

      'lines.1.unitPrice': ['credit_note_over_line'],

    // A price cut of ৳1 a strip on all 17 strips: ৳17 plus ৳2.55 VAT, applied to the invoice
    const cut = await credited(

  it('credits a whole invoice in one click, to the paisa, the way the invoice worked it out', async () => {
    // A counter sale while prices included VAT, with a percent and an amount discount
    await setPricesIncludeVat(true);
    const counter = await invoiced(
      invoiceForm(
        [
          invoiceLine(napa, '7', '12.35', {
            unitId: unitId('strip'),
            batchId: napaBatch,
            discount: '3.5',
          }),
          invoiceLine(syrup, '3', '41.50', { discountType: 'amount', discount: '2' }),
        ],
        { customerId: agrabad.id, warehouseId: main.id },
      ),
    );
    expect(counter.number).toBe('INV-2026-27-0002');
    await setPricesIncludeVat(false);

    const draft = await credited(
      creditForm(counter, wholeInvoiceCreditLines(counter), {
        reason: 'billing_error',
        post: false,
      }),
    );
    // The invoice's own setting, not the workspace's: every line gives back exactly what it charged
    expect(draft).toMatchObject({
      number: null,
      pricesIncludeVat: true,
      net: counter.net,
      vat: counter.vat,
      total: counter.total,
      applied: '0.0000',
      entry: null,
    });
    const amounts = (lines: readonly { net: string; vat: string; total: string }[]) =>
      lines.map((line) => [line.net, line.vat, line.total]);
    expect(amounts(draft.lines)).toEqual(amounts(counter.lines));
    const posted = await send('POST', `/credit-notes/${draft.id}/post`, { version: draft.version });
    expect(posted.statusCode, posted.body).toBe(200);
    expect(creditNoteSchema.parse(posted.json())).toMatchObject({
      number: 'CN-2026-27-0003',
      applied: counter.total,
    });

    const after = await invoiceNow(counter.id);
    expect(after.amountCredited).toBe(counter.total);
    expect(creditStateOf(after)).toBe('credited');
    // Settled by the credit note: not open, and counted with the paid ones
    expect(await invoiceNumbers(`payment=open&customerId=${agrabad.id}`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(await invoiceNumbers(`payment=paid&customerId=${agrabad.id}`)).toEqual([
      'INV-2026-27-0002',
    ]);
    // Once a credit note is posted, the button is gone, and the server refuses the full amounts
    expect(canCreditWhole(after)).toBe(false);
    const again = await send(
      'POST',
      '/credit-notes',
      creditForm(after, wholeInvoiceCreditLines(after), { reason: 'billing_error' }),
    );
    expect(problemOf(again).code).toBe('credit_note_over_line');
    // A line of this invoice on a credit note for another one
    const elsewhere = await send(
      'POST',
      '/credit-notes',
      creditForm(firstInvoice, [creditLine(counter.lines[1]?.id ?? '', '1', '1')]),
    );
    expect(problemOf(elsewhere).fieldErrors).toEqual({
      'lines.0.invoiceLineId': ['credit_note_line_invalid'],
    });
  });
```

- **The money cap goes under every line that takes from it.** The syrup line charged ৳2,300 and ৳230 came back, so
  ৳2,070 is left. A price cut of 45 × ৳40 (exactly ৳2,070) and a second line of ৳1.15 together are too much, and both
  lines get `credit_note_over_line` under their price: the person decides which one to lower.
- **A price cut**: ৳1 a strip on all 17 strips is ৳17 + ৳2.55 VAT, CN-0002, applied to the invoice.
- **"Credit whole invoice" gives back exactly what was billed** (decision 5). The counter sale is made while prices
  include VAT, with a percent discount on one line and a ৳2 discount on the other, so the amounts have odd paisa.
  The setting is then switched off. `wholeInvoiceCreditLines()` (the same function the app's button uses) makes a
  draft whose net, VAT, total and every line match the invoice to the paisa, because the credit note works its lines
  out with the *invoice's* setting, not the workspace's.
- **Posted, it settles the invoice**: credited in full, "credited", out of the open list and in the paid one.
- **After that, the button is gone** (`canCreditWhole()` is false), and the server refuses the same lines again: the
  money cap. A line of this invoice on a credit note for another invoice is `credit_note_line_invalid`.

```ts
  it('lets a credit note wait for another one of the same invoice, then answers under its line', async () => {
    // Hold the invoice's lock as another posting would, and send two credit notes for all of
    // INV-0003's line (৳92 each). Both wait on the lock. The first then posts; the second waits
    // for it, reads what it took back, and answers under its line.
    const line = laterInvoice.lines[0]?.id ?? '';
    const body = creditForm(laterInvoice, [creditLine(line, '2', '40')], { date: '2026-10-09' });
    const superuser = postgres(pg.superuserUrl, { max: 1 });
    let first: ReturnType<typeof send> | undefined;
    let second: ReturnType<typeof send> | undefined;
    await superuser.begin(async (tx) => {
      await tx`SELECT id FROM invoices WHERE id = ${laterInvoice.id} FOR UPDATE`;
      first = send('POST', '/credit-notes', body);
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 150));
      second = send('POST', '/credit-notes', body);
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 150));
    });
    await superuser.end();
    const [one, two] = await Promise.all([first, second]);
    if (!one || !two) throw new Error('the credit notes were never sent');
    expect(one.statusCode, one.body).toBe(201);
    // ৳42 was still due on INV-0003: that much is applied, ৳50 is advance
    racedNote = creditNoteSchema.parse(one.json());
    expect(racedNote).toMatchObject({ number: 'CN-2026-27-0005', applied: '42.0000' });
    expect(two.statusCode).toBe(409);
    expect(problemOf(two).fieldErrors).toEqual({ 'lines.0.unitPrice': ['credit_note_over_line'] });
  });
```

- **An advance from a credit note.** Tamanna pays INV-0001 in full (৳2,285.05 of a ৳3,000 receipt). A price cut on
  the paid invoice then has nothing to apply to: CN-0004 is ৳57.50, all of it advance (decision 4).
- **Applying it later** works like a receipt's: ৳57.51 is `credit_note_over_allocated` under the list; ৳50 goes to
  INV-0003 and the version goes up; the old version is `version_conflict`. The audit row shows what changed
  (INV-0003: nothing → ৳50). A draft has no money to apply (`credit_note_not_posted`).
- **Two credit notes at once.** The test holds the invoice's lock as the superuser, as another posting would, and
  sends two credit notes for all of INV-0003's line, 150 ms apart. When the lock is released, the first posts as
  CN-0005 and applies the ৳42 INV-0003 still owed (৳50 of it is advance). The second waited for it, read what it took
  back, and is refused under its line.
- **This is the test that found the deadlock.** With `FOR UPDATE` on the invoice (in the credit note's posting or in
  `checkAllocations()`), the first answer is a 500. Without any lock, the second credit note reads the old numbers,
  passes, and is stopped only by the database's check: the right code, but no field, so the form could not say which
  line to fix. We checked all three.

- **The sales returns account** (decision 7). The pharma setup chose 4120. A cash account and a group are refused
  (`sales_account_invalid`). While 4120 is chosen, archiving it is `account_used_by_sales`. Deleting it is refused
  too, but as `account_in_use`, because credit notes have booked to it, and an account with entries is never
  deleted. A new account with no entries shows the setting's own answer: chosen, then deleted, it is
  `account_used_by_sales`.
- **No account chosen: the sale comes back off Sales.** The audit log shows both changes by code (4120 → 4130 →
  nothing), newest first. A credit note then debits 4110. The setting goes back to 4120 afterwards.
- **The journal's Reverse refuses both kinds of entry**: a return's (`journal_is_stock`: another stock document puts
  it right) and a credit note's (`journal_is_sales`).
- **An archived customer cannot get a credit note**: `sales_customer_invalid` under `customerId`, a field the credit
  note form does not have (15d.6 shows it as a form-level error).
- **The list by invoice** shows INV-0001's four credit notes, newest first.

```ts
describe('refunds', () => {
  it('pays an advance back from a receipt, and gives it back when voided', async () => {
    // ৳3,000 came in, ৳2,285.05 is applied: ৳714.95 is left

    expect((await receiptNow(tamannaReceipt.id)).refunded).toBe('500.0000');

    const receipt = await receiptNow(tamannaReceipt.id);
    const overApplied = await send('PUT', `/receipts/${receipt.id}/allocations`, {

    expect(problemOf(noReason).fieldErrors).toEqual({ reason: ['receipt_void_reason_required'] });
    const voided = await send('POST', `/refunds/${receiptRefund.id}/void`, {

    expect(receiptRefund).toMatchObject({

    const reversal = journalEntrySchema.parse(

    );
    expect(reversal.source).toBe('reversal');
    expect(await entryLines(reversal.id)).toEqual([
      ['1140', '0.0000', '500.0000'],

    expect((await receiptNow(tamannaReceipt.id)).refunded).toBe('0.0000');
    const twice = await send('POST', `/refunds/${receiptRefund.id}/void`, {

    expect(voidedList.items.map((item) => item.number)).toEqual(['RF-2026-27-0001']);

      ),
    );
    const fromDraft = await send('POST', '/refunds', refundForm('1', { creditNoteId: draft.id }));
    expect(problemOf(fromDraft).fieldErrors).toEqual({ creditNoteId: ['refund_source_invalid'] });
    const sales = await send(
      'POST',
      '/refunds',
      refundForm('1', { receiptId: tamannaReceipt.id, accountId: account('4110') }),
    );
    expect(problemOf(sales).fieldErrors).toEqual({ accountId: ['refund_account_invalid'] });
    expect(
      (await send('DELETE', `/credit-notes/${draft.id}?version=${String(draft.version)}`))
        .statusCode,
    ).toBe(204);
  });
```

- **A refund pays back what is not applied.** The receipt's advance is ৳714.95, so ৳714.96 is `refund_over_source`
  under the amount. ৳500 posts as RF-0001 at once: Dr Accounts receivable with Tamanna / Cr Cash, source
  `sales_refund`. The receipt shows ৳500 refunded.
- **What was paid back is gone.** The receipt can now apply at most ৳2,500 (`receipt_over_allocated`), and it cannot
  be voided while the refund stands (`receipt_has_refunds`): void the refund first.
- **A refund is voided like a receipt**: not before the day it was paid (`receipt_void_date`), not without a reason
  (a 400). The void reverses the entry on the void date, and the money is the receipt's again. Voiding it twice is
  `refund_voided`. Reverse in the journal refuses its entry (`journal_is_sales`).
- **A credit note's advance goes back by bKash**: ৳7.50 of CN-0004, out of the 1131 account, with the TrxID. CN-0004
  can then apply at most ৳50.
- **The source must be one posted document of the same customer.** Neither or both is a 400 from the contract.
  Another customer's receipt and a draft credit note are `refund_source_invalid`, under the box that named them. The
  sales account is not where money is kept (`refund_account_invalid`).

```ts
  it("lets a refund wait for the receipt's allocation, then answers under its amount", async () => {
    const fresh = await invoiced(
      invoiceForm([invoiceLine(syrup, '15', '40')], { date: '2026-10-09', warehouseId: main.id }),
    );
    expect(fresh).toMatchObject({ number: 'INV-2026-27-0005', total: '690.0000' });
    // Hold the receipt's lock, then apply its advance to the new invoice and ask for all of the
    // advance back. The allocation goes first; the refund waits for it, and finds ৳24.95 left.
    const receipt = await receiptNow(tamannaReceipt.id);
    const superuser = postgres(pg.superuserUrl, { max: 1 });
    let allocate: ReturnType<typeof send> | undefined;
    let refund: ReturnType<typeof send> | undefined;
    await superuser.begin(async (tx) => {
      await tx`SELECT id FROM receipts WHERE id = ${receipt.id} FOR UPDATE`;
      allocate = send('PUT', `/receipts/${receipt.id}/allocations`, {
        version: receipt.version,
        allocations: [
          { invoiceId: firstInvoice.id, amount: '2285.05' },
          { invoiceId: fresh.id, amount: '690' },
        ],
      });
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 150));
      refund = send('POST', '/refunds', refundForm('714.95', { receiptId: receipt.id }));
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 150));
    });
    await superuser.end();
    const [applied, paidBack] = await Promise.all([allocate, refund]);
    if (!applied || !paidBack) throw new Error('the requests were never sent');
    expect(applied.statusCode, applied.body).toBe(200);
    expect(paidBack.statusCode).toBe(409);
    expect(problemOf(paidBack).fieldErrors).toEqual({ amount: ['refund_over_source'] });
    // The refused refund used no number
    const rest = await refunded(refundForm('24.95', { receiptId: receipt.id }));
    expect(rest.number).toBe('RF-2026-27-0003');
  });

  it('adds up to what Tamanna owes in the books', async () => {
    // Billed ৳2,534.60 + ৳92 + ৳690 = ৳3,316.60. Credited ৳230 + ৳19.55 + ৳57.50 + ৳92 + ৳1.15 =
    // ৳400.20. Received ৳3,000, paid back ৳7.50 + ৳24.95 (the voided ৳500 came and went).
    // 3,316.60 − 400.20 − 3,000 + 32.45 = −51.15: ৳51.15 is still Tamanna's advance, the ৳50 of
    // CN-0005 that no invoice has used and the ৳1.15 of CN-0006.
    const balance = customerCreditSchema.parse(
      (await send('GET', `/customers/${tamanna.id}/credit`)).json(),
    );
    expect(balance.balance).toBe('-51.1500');
  });
});
```

- **A refund and an allocation of one receipt take turns.** With the receipt locked by the superuser, the receipt's
  advance is applied to a new invoice (INV-0005, ৳690), and a moment later the whole ৳714.95 is asked back. The
  allocation goes first; the refund waits for it, finds ৳24.95 left, and is refused under its amount. A refund of
  ৳24.95 then takes RF-0003: the refused one used no number.
- **Honestly, this test cannot tell whether the lock is there.** Without the `FOR UPDATE` on the receipt in
  `lockSource()`, the refund reads the old ৳714.95 and passes its own check, but its insert must then update the
  receipt (the trigger adds to `refunded`), which waits for the allocation anyway. The database's check
  `receipts_amount_check` then refuses it, and `overSourceRace()` answers with the same code under the same field.
  We checked: the test passes both ways. It stays, because it proves the outcome a person sees.
- **The books add up.** Billed ৳3,316.60, credited ৳400.20, received ৳3,000, paid back ৳32.45 (the voided ৳500 came and
  went): Tamanna's balance is −৳51.15, an advance. That is exactly the money of CN-0005 and CN-0006 that no invoice
  used.

### Permissions, what holds on, a race between two documents, and the period lock

```ts
describe('who may do what', () => {
  it('lets anyone read returns, credit notes and refunds, and only the right people write them', async () => {
    for (const url of [
      '/sales-returns',
      `/sales-returns/${firstReturn.id}`,
      '/credit-notes',
      `/credit-notes/${firstCreditNote.id}`,
      '/refunds',
      `/refunds/${receiptRefund.id}`,
      '/sales-accounts',
    ]) {
      expect((await send('GET', url, undefined, viewer)).statusCode, url).toBe(200);
    }
    const ownLine = returnLine(napa, '1', { unitId: unitId('strip'), batchId: napaBatch });
    const writes = [
      send('POST', '/sales-returns', returnForm([ownLine]), viewer),
      send(
        'POST',
        '/credit-notes',
        creditForm(firstInvoice, [creditLine(firstInvoice.lines[0]?.id ?? '', '1', '1')]),
        viewer,
      ),
      send(
        'PUT',
        `/credit-notes/${advanceNote.id}/allocations`,
        { version: 1, allocations: [] },
        viewer,
      ),
      send('POST', '/refunds', refundForm('1', { receiptId: tamannaReceipt.id }), viewer),
      send(
        'POST',
        `/refunds/${receiptRefund.id}/void`,
        { version: 1, date: '2026-10-10', reason: 'x' },
        viewer,
      ),
      send('PUT', '/sales-accounts', { returns: '' }, viewer),
    ];
    for (const res of await Promise.all(writes)) {
      expect(res.statusCode).toBe(403);
      expect(problemOf(res).code).toBe('permission_missing');
    }

    // The store keeper takes goods back, and moves no money
    const back = await returned(returnForm([ownLine], { customerId: agrabad.id }), storeKeeper);
    expect(back.status).toBe('posted');
    const money = [
      send(
        'POST',
        '/credit-notes',
        creditForm(firstInvoice, [creditLine(firstInvoice.lines[0]?.id ?? '', '1', '1')]),
        storeKeeper,
      ),
      send('POST', '/refunds', refundForm('1', { receiptId: tamannaReceipt.id }), storeKeeper),
      send('PUT', '/sales-accounts', { returns: '' }, storeKeeper),
    ];
    const refused = await Promise.all(money);
    expect(refused.map((res) => res.statusCode)).toEqual([403, 403, 403]);
    expect(refused.map((res) => problemOf(res).params?.permissions)).toEqual([
      'sales.credit_note.manage',
      'sales.refund.manage',
      'core.settings.manage',
    ]);
  });
});

describe('what returns and refunds hold on to', () => {
  it('keeps a customer, a product and an account that they name', async () => {
    const patenga = await addCustomer('Patenga Pharmacy');
    const vitamin = await addProduct('Vitamin B complex');
    // A draft may name an item with no cost yet: the cost is looked up when it is posted
    await returned(returnForm([returnLine(vitamin, '1')], { customerId: patenga.id, post: false }));
    const customer = await send(
      'DELETE',
      `/customers/${patenga.id}?version=${String(patenga.version)}`,
    );
    expect(problemOf(customer).code).toBe('customer_in_use');
    const product = await send(
      'DELETE',
      `/products/${vitamin.id}?version=${String(vitamin.version)}`,
    );
    expect(problemOf(product).code).toBe('product_in_use');
    // The bKash account a refund paid out of
    const wallet = accountSchema.parse((await send('GET', `/accounts/${account('1131')}`)).json());
    const removed = await send(
      'DELETE',
      `/accounts/${wallet.id}?version=${String(wallet.version)}`,
    );
    expect(problemOf(removed).code).toBe('account_in_use');
  });
});
```

- **The viewer reads everything**, the sales returns setting too, and every write is `permission_missing` (403),
  decided by the route before the service runs.
- **The store keeper takes goods back and moves no money.** Their return posts; a credit note, a refund and the
  setting are refused, each naming the permission it needs.
- **A draft return holds on to its customer and its item** (`customer_in_use`, `product_in_use`): the foreign keys of
  15d.2, through the lists of 15d.3. A draft may name an item with no cost: the cost is looked up when it is posted.
  The bKash account a refund paid out of is `account_in_use`.

```ts
describe('a return and an invoice of one challan line', () => {
  it('lets the second one see what the first did', async () => {
    const counter = await delivered(agrabad, '', [deliveryLine(syrup, '6')]);
    const line = lineOf(counter.lines, syrup).id;
    // Hold the challan's lock as another posting would. The invoice of all 6 bottles asks first,
    // the return of 2 a moment later: both wait. The invoice then posts, and the return, which
    // waited for it, finds the line billed and points at the invoice line.
    const superuser = postgres(pg.superuserUrl, { max: 1 });
    let bill: ReturnType<typeof send> | undefined;
    let back: ReturnType<typeof send> | undefined;
    await superuser.begin(async (tx) => {
      await tx`SELECT id FROM deliveries WHERE id = ${counter.id} FOR UPDATE`;
      bill = send(
        'POST',
        '/invoices',
        invoiceForm([invoiceLine(syrup, '6', '40', { deliveryLineId: line })], {
          customerId: agrabad.id,
          date: '2026-10-08',
        }),
      );
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 150));
      back = send(
        'POST',
        '/sales-returns',
        returnForm([returnLine(syrup, '2', { deliveryLineId: line })], {
          customerId: agrabad.id,
          date: '2026-10-08',
        }),
      );
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 150));
    });
    await superuser.end();
    const [billed, came] = await Promise.all([bill, back]);
    if (!billed || !came) throw new Error('the requests were never sent');
    expect(billed.statusCode, billed.body).toBe(201);
    expect(came.statusCode, came.body).toBe(201);
    const invoice = invoiceSchema.parse(billed.json());
    expect(salesReturnSchema.parse(came.json()).lines[0]).toMatchObject({
      billed: true,
      invoiceLineId: invoice.lines[0]?.id,
    });
  });
});
```

- **A return and an invoice of the same challan line.** Both lock the challan when they post (15d.3). With the
  challan held by the superuser, the invoice of all 6 bottles asks first and a return of 2 a moment later. The
  invoice posts; the return waited for it, finds the line billed, and points at the invoice line.
- **Without the lock in the return's `challanLines()`**, the return does not wait: it posts first, unbilled, and the
  invoice of 6 is then refused, because only 4 are left to bill. We checked: the test fails that way. Without the
  lock, the two could also both pass, each reading the line before the other committed: the invoice bills all 6 and
  the return counts as unbilled, so the goods come back while the bill stays whole and no credit note is offered.

```ts
describe('the period lock', () => {
  it('refuses a return, a credit note or a refund on a day the books are closed', async () => {
    const lockedDay = '2026-10-09';
    const draftReturn = await returned(
      returnForm([returnLine(napa, '1', { unitId: unitId('strip'), batchId: napaBatch })], {
        customerId: agrabad.id,
        date: lockedDay,
        post: false,
      }),
    );
    const draftNote = await credited(
      creditForm(
        firstInvoice,
        [creditLine(lineOf(firstInvoice.lines, napa).id, '1', '0.5', { unitId: unitId('strip') })],
        { date: lockedDay, post: false },
      ),
    );
    expect(
      (await send('PUT', '/period-lock', { lockDate: lockedDay, version: 0 })).statusCode,
    ).toBe(200);
    const postReturn = await send('POST', `/sales-returns/${draftReturn.id}/post`, {
      version: draftReturn.version,
    });
    expect(problemOf(postReturn).code).toBe('journal_period_locked');
    expect((await returnNow(draftReturn.id)).status).toBe('draft');
    const postNote = await send('POST', `/credit-notes/${draftNote.id}/post`, {
      version: draftNote.version,
    });
    expect(problemOf(postNote).code).toBe('journal_period_locked');
    expect((await creditNoteNow(draftNote.id)).status).toBe('draft');
    const refund = await send(
      'POST',
      '/refunds',
      refundForm('1', { creditNoteId: racedNote.id, date: lockedDay }),
    );
    expect(problemOf(refund).code).toBe('journal_period_locked');
  });
});
```

- **The period lock runs last**, because it closes the books for everything before it. Drafts dated on the lock date
  are saved first. Posting the return or the credit note is then `journal_period_locked`, and both stay drafts. A
  refund dated that day is refused the same way.

```diff
+        invoiceBody(customerOfA.id, warehouseOfA.branchId, serviceLine(serviceOfA, rateOfA)),
+      ),
+      invoiceSchema,
+    );
+  });
+
+  it("never lists or reads B's returns, credit notes, refunds or setting", async () => {
+    for (const url of [
+      '/sales-returns',
+      `/sales-returns?customerId=${customerOfB.id}`,
+      '/credit-notes',
+      `/credit-notes?invoiceId=${invoiceOfB.id}`,
+      '/refunds',
+      `/refunds?customerId=${customerOfB.id}`,
+    ]) {
+      const page: unknown = (await as(tenantA, 'GET', url)).json();
+      const items = url.startsWith('/sales-returns')
+        ? salesReturnPageSchema.parse(page).items
+        : url.startsWith('/credit-notes')
+          ? creditNotePageSchema.parse(page).items
+          : refundPageSchema.parse(page).items;
+      expect(items, url).toEqual([]);
+    }
+    for (const url of [
+      `/sales-returns/${returnOfB.id}`,
+      `/sales-returns/${draftReturnOfB.id}`,
+      `/credit-notes/${noteOfB.id}`,
+      `/credit-notes/${draftNoteOfB.id}`,
+      `/refunds/${refundOfB.id}`,
+    ]) {
+      expect((await as(tenantA, 'GET', url)).statusCode, url).toBe(404);
+    }
+  });
+
+  it('cannot change, post, delete, apply or void any of them', async () => {
+    const attempts = [
+      as(tenantA, 'PUT', `/sales-returns/${draftReturnOfB.id}`, {
+        ...returnBody(customerOfA.id, warehouseOfA.id, returnLine(goodsOfA)),
+        version: draftReturnOfB.version,
+      }),
+      as(tenantA, 'POST', `/sales-returns/${draftReturnOfB.id}/post`, {
+        version: draftReturnOfB.version,
+      }),
+      as(
+        tenantA,
+        'DELETE',
+        `/sales-returns/${draftReturnOfB.id}?version=${String(draftReturnOfB.version)}`,
+      ),
+      // A valid form of A's own: a 400 from the contract would never reach the tenant check
+      as(tenantA, 'PUT', `/credit-notes/${draftNoteOfB.id}`, {
+        ...creditBody(invoiceOfA.id, invoiceOfA.lines[0]?.id ?? '', {
+          lines: [
+            {
+              ...creditBody('', invoiceOfA.lines[0]?.id ?? '').lines[0],
+              unitId: serviceOfA.baseUnitId,
+            },
+          ],
+        }),
+        version: draftNoteOfB.version,
+      }),
+      as(tenantA, 'POST', `/credit-notes/${draftNoteOfB.id}/post`, {
+        version: draftNoteOfB.version,
+      }),
+      as(
+        tenantA,
+        'DELETE',
+        `/credit-notes/${draftNoteOfB.id}?version=${String(draftNoteOfB.version)}`,
+      ),
+      as(tenantA, 'PUT', `/credit-notes/${noteOfB.id}/allocations`, {
+        version: noteOfB.version,
+        allocations: [],
+      }),
+      as(tenantA, 'POST', `/refunds/${refundOfB.id}/void`, {
+        version: refundOfB.version,
+        date: '2026-10-09',
+        reason: 'Taken over',
+      }),
+    ];
+    for (const res of await Promise.all(attempts)) expect(res.statusCode, res.body).toBe(404);
+
+    const returnNow = salesReturnSchema.parse(

+    );
+    expect(returnNow).toMatchObject({ status: 'draft', version: draftReturnOfB.version });
+    const draftNow = creditNoteSchema.parse(
+      (await as(tenantB, 'GET', `/credit-notes/${draftNoteOfB.id}`)).json(),
+    );
+    expect(draftNow).toMatchObject({ status: 'draft', version: draftNoteOfB.version });
+    const noteNow = creditNoteSchema.parse(
+      (await as(tenantB, 'GET', `/credit-notes/${noteOfB.id}`)).json(),
+    );
+    expect(noteNow).toMatchObject({ applied: noteOfB.applied, version: noteOfB.version });
+    const refundNow = refundSchema.parse(

+    );
+    expect(refundNow).toMatchObject({ status: 'posted', version: refundOfB.version });
+  });
+
+  it("cannot take back, credit or pay back with B's customer, challan, invoice, receipt or accounts", async () => {
+    const forB = await as(
+      tenantA,
+      'POST',
+      '/sales-returns',
+      returnBody(customerOfB.id, warehouseOfA.id, returnLine(goodsOfA)),
+    );
+    expect(problemOf(forB).fieldErrors).toEqual({ customerId: ['sales_customer_invalid'] });
+    const intoB = await as(
+      tenantA,
+      'POST',
+      '/sales-returns',

+    );
+    expect(problemOf(intoB).fieldErrors).toEqual({ warehouseId: ['stock_warehouse_invalid'] });
+    const fromChallanOfB = await as(
+      tenantA,
+      'POST',
+      '/sales-returns',
+      returnBody(
+        customerOfA.id,
+        warehouseOfA.id,

+    expect(problemOf(fromChallanOfB).fieldErrors).toEqual({
+      'lines.0.deliveryLineId': ['return_delivery_line_invalid'],
+    });
+
+    const lineOfA = invoiceOfA.lines[0]?.id ?? '';
+    const withUnit = (body: ReturnType<typeof creditBody>, extra: object) => ({
+      ...body,
+      lines: [{ ...body.lines[0], unitId: serviceOfA.baseUnitId, ...extra }],
+    });
+    const invoiceOfBForA = await as(
+      tenantA,
+      'POST',
+      '/credit-notes',

+    );
+    expect(problemOf(invoiceOfBForA).fieldErrors).toEqual({
+      invoiceId: ['credit_note_invoice_invalid'],
+    });
+    const lineOfB = await as(
+      tenantA,
+      'POST',
+      '/credit-notes',
+      withUnit(creditBody(invoiceOfA.id, lineOfA), { invoiceLineId: invoiceOfB.lines[0]?.id }),
+    );
+    expect(problemOf(lineOfB).fieldErrors).toEqual({
+      'lines.0.invoiceLineId': ['credit_note_line_invalid'],
+    });
+    const returnLineOfB = await as(
+      tenantA,
+      'POST',
+      '/credit-notes',
+      withUnit(creditBody(invoiceOfA.id, lineOfA), { returnLineId: returnOfB.lines[0]?.id }),
+    );
+    expect(problemOf(returnLineOfB).fieldErrors).toEqual({
+      'lines.0.returnLineId': ['credit_note_return_invalid'],
+    });
+    // A's own credit note, applied to B's invoice
+    const own = await made(
+      as(tenantA, 'POST', '/credit-notes', withUnit(creditBody(invoiceOfA.id, lineOfA), {})),

+    const applyToB = await as(tenantA, 'PUT', `/credit-notes/${own.id}/allocations`, {

+    expect(problemOf(applyToB).fieldErrors).toEqual({

+
+    const cashOfA = accountOfA('1110');
+    const fromReceiptOfB = await as(

+      'POST',

+    expect(problemOf(fromReceiptOfB).fieldErrors).toEqual({ receiptId: ['refund_source_invalid'] });
+    const fromNoteOfB = await as(

+    expect(problemOf(settingOfB).fieldErrors).toEqual({ returns: ['sales_account_invalid'] });

+      expect(setting.returns).toBeNull();

+  it('numbers its returns, credit notes and refunds on its own', async () => {

```

- **B's documents**: stock of its juice, a challan of 10, a posted return of 2 and a draft one, an invoice for a
  loading charge with a posted credit note and a draft one, and an advance of ৳50 of which ৳20 is paid back. B's
  receipt is read again afterwards, because the refund gave it a new version: A's attempts send B's current versions,
  so only the tenant check stands between A and B's rows.
- **`made()` takes the request itself**, not its answer, so each call reads as one step ("make this, expect a 201")
  and ESLint has nothing to say about an `async` function that does not wait.
- **Every read is a 404 or an empty list**, also the lists filtered by B's customer or B's invoice.
- **Every write is a 404**: change, post and delete of B's drafts, applying B's credit note, voiding B's refund.
  Afterwards they are exactly as B left them.
- **The attempts send valid forms of A's own.** The credit note change sends a real unit of A's service: with an
  empty unit it would be a 400 from the contract, and the test that expects a 404 would fail for the wrong reason
  (this happened while writing it).
- **A cannot use B's records in its own documents.** B's customer is `sales_customer_invalid`, B's warehouse
  `stock_warehouse_invalid`, B's challan line `return_delivery_line_invalid`, B's invoice
  `credit_note_invoice_invalid`, B's invoice line `credit_note_line_invalid`, B's return line
  `credit_note_return_invalid`; applying A's credit note to B's invoice is `credit_note_allocation_invalid`; B's
  receipt and credit note are `refund_source_invalid`, B's cash account `refund_account_invalid`, and B's Sales
  account `sales_account_invalid` for A's setting. These are the same answers as for an id that does not exist.
- **Numbers are per workspace**: A's first return, credit note and refund have the same numbers as B's.

The RLS coverage test needs no change: it finds the six new tables by their `tenant_id` column and checks that each
has row-level security turned on and forced, with a policy.

- **Garments gets none.** Its 4120 is "Local sales", an income account like any other. Choosing by code alone would
  make every garments credit note book to local sales; the setting is filled only from an account with the code
  *and* the name "Sales returns" (15d.3).
- **The pharma workspace whose setup was retried keeps 4120.** Its chart came from the chart job (the step 9 path for
  old workspaces), which chose 4120, and the retried setup left it alone. A new pharma workspace that goes through
  setup normally is the one in `returns.int.spec.ts`.

- **17 series, not 14.** 15d.1 added `sales.return` (SR), `sales.credit_note` (CN) and `sales.refund` (RF), each
  numbered by fiscal year. Reading the list never uses a number up, so each still starts at `0001`.

### Check this part

```bash
pnpm --filter @omnivo/api typecheck
pnpm --filter @omnivo/api exec vitest run src/sales src/setup src/numbering --maxWorkers=3
pnpm --filter @omnivo/api test:tenant-leak
```

The `vitest` line runs only the files this part touches. `pnpm test:integration` runs all of them; part 15d.8 runs
every check once at the end.

> **What we checked in this part.** The API type-checks, and ESLint and Prettier are clean. All API tests pass: 46
> files (unit, integration and tenant-leak), 482 tests, run with three workers. Five things were checked by breaking
> the code on purpose. With `FOR UPDATE` on the invoice in the credit note's posting, or in `checkAllocations()`, the
> two credit notes deadlock and one answers with a 500. With no lock on the invoice, the second credit note is
> refused with no field. Without the challan lock in the return's `challanLines()`, the return no longer waits for the
> invoice. Without the receipt lock in the refund's `lockSource()`, the refund race test still passes, for the
> reason given above.

## 15d.5 — `packages/i18n`: the words

The pages of 15d.6 need their words in English and Bangla, and the app cannot type-check without them, so they come
first. This part changes only the two locale files. The ui package needs nothing new: the return form is built from
the stock line rows (step 13), the credit note from the sales line editor (15b), the money parts from the
allocation table (15c), the invoice picker from the native select, and the printed pages from `PrintSheet` (15c).

When this part starts, `packages/i18n` has one error: the `errors` object is missing the 30 new codes. When it
ends, the i18n package compiles, and the app has nine type errors left. All of them are about the new fields of
15d.1, not about words: the payment pills in `sales-parts.tsx` do not pass `amountCredited` yet, and the invoice
test fixtures and the MSW mock lack `amountCredited`, `creditNoteTotal`, `creditNotes`, a line's `credited`, and a
delivery's `returnedQuantity`, `returnState` and `returns`. 15d.6 and 15d.7 fix them.


- **New keys go into `en.ts` first** (CLAUDE.md → Language). `bn.ts` has the type `Messages`, taken from `en`, so a
  key missing in Bangla fails the type check. The `errors` object ends with `satisfies Record<ErrorCode, string>`,
  so the 30 codes of 15d.1 and 15d.3 must all be here, or the package does not compile.
- **Keys built from contract values.** The numbering page calls `` t(`numbering.documents.${type}`) ``, the journal
  `` t(`journal.sources.${source}`) ``, the roles matrix `` t(`permissions.${key}`) ``, the audit log
  `` t(`audit.actions.${action}`) `` and `` t(`audit.entityTypes.${type}`) ``, and the stock card
  `` t(`stock.kinds.${kind}`) ``. These template strings are typed from the contract's unions. So the three number
  series (`sales.return`, `sales.credit_note`, `sales.refund`), the three journal sources, the three permissions, the
  twelve audit actions, the three entity types and the movement kind `sales_return` each need a key. Before this
  part, these were nine of the app's eighteen type errors.
- **The new unions the pages show get a key for every member**: `deliveries.returnStates`, `invoices.creditStates`,
  `salesReturns.reasons`, `creditNotes.reasons`, `refunds.sources`, and each document's `statuses`. That includes
  `none` in `returnStates` and `creditStates`, even though the pages will show no pill for it: a template string
  typed from the union needs a key for every member, and a filter or a tooltip may show it later.
- **`nav.salesReturns` says "Sales returns", not "Returns".** Purchasing (a later step) brings returns to suppliers,
  and a store keeper should never wonder which way the goods went. "Credit notes" and "Refunds" are the words on the
  documents themselves.
- **`settings.salesAccounts*` is a card of its own,** like the stock accounts of step 14. It saves through its own
  route (`PUT /sales-accounts`, 15d.1), so it has its own button and its own toast; putting it inside the Sales card
  would mix two saves in one card. The hint says what the setting changes: the profit and loss shows sales and what
  came back as two numbers. `salesReturnsAccountNone` is the empty choice (`null`, decision 7) and says what happens
  then, so an empty box does not look like a missing value.
- **The journal hints.** The journal refuses to reverse an entry that a sales document made (`journal_is_sales`).
  In 15c, `invoiceEntryHint` said only that the invoice stays as it is, because credit notes did not exist yet; now
  it says how to take part of it back. `creditNoteEntryHint` and `refundEntryHint` follow the 15c hints: a credit
  note is never undone, and a refund is undone by voiding it. A sales return needs no hint of its own:
  `sales_return` is in `STOCK_JOURNAL_SOURCES` (15d.1), so the journal page already shows `stockEntryHint` for it.
- **`stock.kinds.sales_return` is "Came back".** It is the stock card's movement column, next to "Delivered".
  "Returned" alone could also mean goods sent back to a supplier.
- **Deliveries.** A posted challan shows how much of it came back (`returnStates`) and lists the returns
  (`returnsTitle`), and each line says how much came back (`lineReturned`). `makeReturn` is the challan page's button
  that opens a new return with the challan's lines. It says "Take goods back", what the store keeper does, because
  "Make return" reads as if the company sent something.
- **Invoices.** `creditStates` is the pill that `creditStateOf()` (15d.1) works out; the page shows "Credited"
  instead of the payment pill when the whole total was taken back (decision 5). `credited` is the row under "Paid",
  and `creditNotesTitle` the list of the posted credit notes (the invoice's `creditNotes`). `writeCreditNote` opens a
  new credit note for this invoice. `creditWhole` is the "Credit whole invoice" button: it posts a draft built by
  `wholeInvoiceCreditLines()` and opens it, and `creditWholeDone` is the toast. The toast says it is a draft to check
  and post, so nobody thinks the invoice is credited already. `returnedBeforeBilling` is the line under a challan
  line that partly came back before it was billed: the invoice bills only `billableQuantity()`, and without the line
  the quantity would look wrong.
- **Money receipts.** `refunded` is the "Paid back" row, and `refund` the button that pays back the receipt's
  advance. `unappliedNotice` now says that advance money can also be paid back.
- **Sales returns.**
  - `reasons` follow `RETURN_REASONS`. `unsold` says "Did not sell", which is what a retailer sending back slow
    stock says.
  - `warehouseHint` says that every item comes back into one warehouse (decision 3), and points at a damage or
    expiry store, because that is where expired strips belong.
  - There are two ways to add a line, like on the invoice. "Add from challans" opens a picker of the customer's
    posted challans that can still take goods back (`GET /deliveries?return=returnable`); "Add items" (from
    `stockLines`) adds a line on its own. Under each line, `fromChallan` with `leftToReturn` (what can still come
    back), or `ownLine`, which says the line comes back at the average cost (decision 2), so the cost on the stock
    card is no surprise.
  - `challanLineHint` names only the item and the batch. Those two are fixed (a challan line has one batch, and the
    server refuses another one with `return_batch_not_allowed`), but the unit and the quantity may change: 3 strips
    can come back from a line of 2 boxes.
  - `postHint` says that a return moves no money. Someone used to other systems expects the return to give the
    money back; here that is a credit note (decision 1).
  - On the return's own page, each line says whether it was billed when the return was posted (`lineBilled` with the
    invoice number, or `lineNotBilled`), from the line's `billed`. `lineCredited` is what credit notes gave back for
    it. `creditNotice` is a document notice, shown while billed goods are not credited in full; `makeCreditNote` is
    its button.
- **Credit notes.**
  - The form picks the customer first, then one of their posted invoices in a select (`invoiceOption`). The invoice
    list has no text search (15c.1), but it can filter by customer and status. The customer is not sent: the server
    takes it from the invoice (15d.1). `invoiceLocked` keeps both boxes read only while lines are on the form, like
    `invoices.customerLocked`, so lines of one invoice never sit under another.
  - `invoiceHint` says why a credit note is for one invoice: the VAT taken back is the VAT that invoice charged.
  - `customerArchived` is shown as a form-level error when posting answers `sales_customer_invalid`. The form has no
    customer field for the error to sit under, and the general text talks about orders.
  - `lateNotice` is the `warn` notice of decision 6, shown when `creditNoteIsLate()` is true. It says what the law
    says and who to ask, and saving and posting stay open.
  - Two ways to add a line. "Add invoice lines" picks lines of the invoice; its description says how to write a price
    cut (keep the quantity, type the cut per unit as the price), because that is not obvious. "Add returned goods"
    picks the return lines this invoice billed that are not credited yet, at the invoice's price. Under each line,
    `fromInvoiceLine` or `fromReturn` says what it credits, and `leftToCredit` shows the money cap of 15d.1 (the
    invoice line's total less `credited`), so the person sees the limit before the server says
    `credit_note_over_line`.
  - `postHint` says what posting books, and where the money goes: first to the invoice, the rest as an advance
    (decision 4).
  - On its own page, `applied`, `refunded` and `unappliedNotice` work like the receipt's, and `refund` pays the
    advance back. The apply dialog uses the allocation table of 15c, which takes its words from `receipts.*`
    ("Apply to invoices", "Left as advance"); they fit a credit note too, so they are not copied.
- **Refunds.**
  - `sources` are the two places money can be paid back from (`REFUND_SOURCE_TYPES`). The form's source select shows
    each with what is left (`sourceOption`, from `unappliedOf()`), and `amountHint` repeats the cap under the amount,
    so `refund_over_source` is rare.
  - `account` is "Paid from", the mirror of the receipt's "Received into". The reference examples are their own:
    money going out is written down differently ("Handed to the shop owner"), even when the bKash and cheque formats
    are the same.
  - `saveHint` says that saving posts at once, like a receipt. The void words follow the receipt's; the date hint
    names the case that makes a refund void (the money never reached the customer), and `keepRefund` is the
    dialog's "No" button for the same reason as `keepReceipt`.
- **Print.** Three titles. A printed credit note shows the original invoice's number and date (`originalInvoice`,
  `invoiceDate`): the customer's accountant files it against that invoice, and the Mushak 6.7 (later) prints the same.
  `reason` shows why. `challan` labels the challan a return line came from. `paidTo`, `amountPaidBack` and
  `paidBackFrom` are the refund slip's words, the mirror of the receipt's `receivedFrom` and `amountReceived`.
- **Permissions.** Each text says what the person may do, in the words of the screen. `sales.refund.manage` says
  "Pay money back", because paying money out of the company is the reason this key is separate (15d.1).
- **The audit words.** `audit.fields` gets the field names 15d.3 writes that the log did not know: `invoice` (a
  credit note's invoice), `applied` (what posting applied to it), `source` (a refund's receipt or credit note) and
  `returns` (the sales returns account, written as the account's code). The rest (`number`, `date`, `customer`,
  `warehouse`, `reason`, `lines`, `total`, `entry`, `amount`, `method`, `reversal`) were there already.
  `credit_note.allocated` writes the invoice numbers as field names, like `receipt.allocated`, so the log shows them
  as they are.
- **Each error message says how to fix the problem** (CLAUDE.md → Copy). A few notes:
  - `return_over_delivered`, `credit_note_over_line`, `credit_note_over_invoice` and `refund_over_source` also cover
    the races of 15d.3: when another document won, the API maps the database check to these codes. So each says that
    another document may have taken some first, and to reload.
  - `credit_note_over_line` sits under the price of every line that takes from that invoice line (15d.3), so it names
    both the price and the quantity: the person decides which one to lower.
  - `return_cost_unknown` gives both ways out: take the goods back from their challan, or bring in the item's opening
    stock so it has a cost.
  - `sales_account_invalid` comes from two places: the settings card, and the posting of a credit note when the
    chosen account is no longer usable. The text names the fix for both: Settings → Sales.
  - `refund_amount_required` asks for "the amount paid back". This is why 15d.1 made `positiveAmountSchema()` take
    the code.
  - `receipt_void_date` changes from "the receipt's date" to "the day the money was paid". A refund's void reuses
    this code (15d.1), and the new words fit money paid in and money paid out.
  - `journal_is_sales` now covers all four sales sources: a receipt or a refund is voided, and an invoice is taken
    back with a credit note.

- **The document names are the office words.** "সেলস রিটার্ন", "ক্রেডিট নোট" and "রিফান্ড" are what Bangladeshi
  offices write on these papers, the same way 15c used "মানি রিসিট". "ফেরত" is the plain word for goods or money
  that came back ("ফেরত এসেছে", "টাকা ফেরত দিন").
- **"ধরা" for applying money to an invoice**, as in 15c, for the credit note's money too.
- **"সেটিংস → বিক্রি" in the error texts.** These are the names the Bangla screen shows (the nav and the Sales card
  title). The two stock errors of step 14 still say "Settings → Inventory" in English; they are left as they are,
  because this part changes only what 15d adds.
- **Typed examples use ASCII digits**: the bKash TrxID, the cheque and card numbers, the DBBL reference, and "0" in
  the amount errors. The inputs always show ASCII digits (CLAUDE.md → Money input), so the example looks like what
  the person will type. Plain text uses Bangla digits: "১০ বোতল", "৳২", "৬ মাস".
- **"মেয়াদোত্তীর্ণ"** (expired) for the damage or expiry store in `warehouseHint`, the word printed on medicine
  returns.

### Check this part

```bash
pnpm --filter @omnivo/contracts build
pnpm --filter @omnivo/i18n typecheck
pnpm --filter @omnivo/i18n test
pnpm --filter @omnivo/i18n build
pnpm --filter @omnivo/ui typecheck
```

Build `@omnivo/contracts` first: the i18n package reads its built `ErrorCode` type, so until then the 30 new codes
are unknown and the `satisfies` line fails the other way round. Build `@omnivo/i18n` before you type-check the ui
package and the app, which read its built types.

> **What we checked in this part.** `packages/i18n` type-checks, ESLint and Prettier are clean, its unit tests pass
> (11), and it builds. `packages/ui` type-checks against the new build. The app has nine type errors left, all about
> the new fields in the payment pills, the invoice test fixtures and the MSW mock (15d.6, 15d.7). No error is about a
> missing translation key.

## 15d.6 — `apps/app`: the screens, and the printed pages

Three new documents get their screens, under Sales after Money receipts: Sales returns, Credit notes and Refunds.
Each has a list, a form and a page, the way invoices and money receipts have them since 15c. A sales return and a
credit note are forms while they are drafts and pages once posted. A refund has no draft, like a receipt: its form
saves and posts at once, and its page can only void it. All three print, on the A4 layout of 15c.

The older screens learn about them:
- A **challan** says how much came back (a pill, a line under each item, a list of its returns) and gets "Take goods
  back".
- An **invoice** says what credit notes took back (the "Credited" pill, a row under "Paid", a list), and gets "Write
  credit note" and "Credit whole invoice" (decision 5). An invoice that bills a challan line where goods came back
  before billing bills only what is left.
- A **money receipt** says what was paid back, and gets "Pay back".
- **Settings** get the "Sales accounts" card (decision 7), the **journal** links the three new entries back to
  their documents, and the **stock card** links a return's movement to the return.

Some earlier parts changed while the screens were built:
- 15d.5: one text changed. `creditNotes.invoiceLinePickerDescription` said a click adds "what can still be taken
  back", but the picker adds the line as it was billed and shows the limit under it (see "Credit notes" below). The
  English and Bangla texts now say that.
- Three older chunks went over their 100 KB budget: 15d.1 made the contracts' `routes` bigger, and every page that
  calls the API carries them. The last section of this part says how each came back under.

When this part starts, the app has nine type errors. When it ends, it has four left, all in the MSW mock (an invoice
line without `credited`, an invoice without `amountCredited`, `creditNoteTotal` and `creditNotes`, a receipt without
`refunded`, a challan line without `returnedQuantity`); 15d.7 fixes them.

- **`LineOrigin.returnedQuantity`** is what came back on a return before the challan line was billed. The invoice
  form shows it under the line ("6 pcs came back before billing: this bills the rest"), because without it the
  quantity would look wrong next to the challan's. A saved draft's lines do not carry it (the invoice line has no
  such field), so a draft says `'0'` and shows no note. The quantity is still right: the server checked it when the
  draft was saved.
- **`billedUnitOf()`**: a challan line is billed in its own unit while nothing came back ("2 case", as it left).
  Once something came back, the line is billed in the base unit. 2 cases of 24 with 6 pieces back leaves 42 pieces,
  and 42 pieces is 1.75 cases: a number nobody wants on an invoice, and one that may not even round to the base
  quantity the API checks (`billableQuantity()`, 15d.1).
- **`challanLineToInvoice()` bills `billableQuantity()`**, not the challan's quantity. The API refuses any other
  quantity for a challan line (15d.3). Three things follow the new quantity:
  - The price moves to `billedUnitOf()`'s unit with `priceInUnit()`, as in 15c: ৳504 a case is ৳21 a piece.
  - An amount discount is shared by what is billed now, not by what left. ৳96 off 48 pieces gives 42/48 of it,
    ৳84, to the 42 pieces billed. Using what left would give the whole ৳96 to pieces that partly came back.
  - With nothing back, `billable` is the challan line's own base quantity, so the 15c results do not change.
- **`challanLinesLeft()` leaves out a line that all came back** (`returnedQuantity` equal to `baseQuantity`). It has
  nothing to bill, and the API would refuse a line of 0. The API's `to_invoice` filter already leaves out a challan
  whose every line came back (15d.3); this covers one line of a challan that still has others.
- **`amountDue()` is gone.** It was `total − amountPaid`, which is wrong once a credit note pays part of the invoice.
  Every caller now uses the contracts' `amountDueOf()` (15d.1), which takes `amountCredited` off too. Keeping a
  second formula in the app would let the two drift apart; the contract's is the one the API uses.
- **`allocationRows()` uses `amountDueOf()`**, so the receipt form and both apply dialogs never offer to pay what a
  credit note already took off.

- **The `origins` map gets its type** (`Map<string, LineOrigin>`). Without it TypeScript infers the type from the

- **The price lookup asks for `billedUnitOf()`'s unit.** A challan without an order is priced by the customer's
  price list (15c). When the line is billed in pieces, the lookup must ask for the piece price; asking for the case
  price and billing it per piece would bill 24 times too much.
